  `returnPercent` is the exact return **with** the guarantee, four decimals (84.9999). The app links
  it from the lucky tab and shows it before the first lucky send: the eight tiers and the guarantee
  («×5 مضمون بعد 15 محاولة بدون ربح» / "×5 guaranteed after 15 draws without a win").
- **18+ gate** *(owner)*: accounts have **no birth date**, so the minimal honest mechanism is a
  one-time statement: `PUT /me/lucky-gifts/age-confirmation` `{"adult": true}` → 200
  `{ageConfirmedAt}` (the first time is kept; audited `lucky.age_confirm`).
  The app asks with a clear "I am 18 or older" screen (never pre-ticked) before the first lucky send.
  No way to withdraw it in the app (support can). **Legal review:** whether a self-declaration is
  enough for the stores and each country, and whether a real age check (birth date at sign-up or an
  ID check) is needed — before production.
- **Admin:** `gift-admin lucky-wins [--limit N] [--min-multiplier M]` lists the latest lucky sends
  with a win (time, sender, gift, draws, top multiplier, coins won, downgraded); `gift-admin
  lucky-day [YYYY-MM-DD]` prints a day's spend, paid, budget left and realised return. There is no
  admin API.
- **Not in v1.27-live / v1.31-live:** buying coins (B5), recipients' earnings, jackpots or pools,
  lucky gifts outside a live, per-user loss limits, a history of one's own draws in the app, a
  viewer switch for the ticker (D151).

### 10.28 Country and featured hosts *(v1.27.1-live, DRAFT — D133)*

- **A user's country:** `Me.country` — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (upper case) or null. **Every account
  starts with none**: nothing asked it at sign-up, the profile had none and the boards are one region
  for everyone (§10.15); the server never infers it from the IP. The user sets it with
  `PATCH /me` `{"country": "SA"}` (lower case accepted; an unknown or malformed code, a grouping such
  as `EU`, or `XK` → 400 `country` / `invalid_value`; null clears it). This follows the owner's D45
  decision ("the user chooses their country, optional; location is never inferred; XK excluded")
  and the field name of the approved, unmerged KL-048 contract (`country`). `PATCH /me` now takes `locale` and/or
  `country` (at least one; `{}` → 400 `body` / `required`). It is not shown on profiles. It decides
  `scope=nearby` (§10.4) and is one of the two inputs of the lucky-gift region list (§10.27).
- **Featured hosts** *(owner: a Featured filter)*: `live_featured_hosts` (one row per host: `rank`
  0–1 000 000, lower first, default 100; optional `until`, after which the row no longer counts).
  Managed only with the `feature-admin` CLI (migration role): `add --user <email|username> [--rank N]
  [--until <ISO time>]` (adds or updates), `remove --user …`, `list`; every change is audited
  (`live.feature.add` with before / after, `live.feature.remove`). A featured host's rooms are listed
  by `featured=true` while LIVE (§10.4); the ordering ties rooms of the same rank by the popular
  order. There is no admin API.

### 10.29 The host's wish list *(v1.27.3-live, DRAFT — D136)*

- **What:** the host chooses up to **4** gifts from the catalogue (any tab, `LUCKY` too while lucky
  gifts are on) that the room shows as a see-through card; viewers tap one to open the gift panel
  with that gift and the host chosen (nothing is sent by the tap).
- **Writing:** `StartLiveRoomRequest.wishGifts` and `UpdateLiveRoomRequest.wishGifts` (host only):
  distinct codes in display order, `[]` empties it; more than 4 → 400 `wishGifts` / `too_many`; a
  repeated code → `invalid_value`; a code that is not a gift that can be sent now → `invalid_value`.
  A go-live without the field copies the host's last live's list. A real change while live moves
  the room info version (§10.12, `roomInfoVersion`) and is audited (`live.room.edit`, fields
  `wishGifts`); setting the same list changes nothing. Counts against the `PATCH` bucket only.
- **Reading:** `LiveRoom.wishGifts` (the room detail, start, edit and end responses; not hub cards):
  `{giftCode, name, priceCoins, assetKey, imageUrl, received}` in the list's order, the name by
  `Accept-Language`; a gift that can no longer be sent is left out (kept in the stored list).
  `received` = the sum of `quantity` of this live's sends of that gift that named the host (whoever
  sent them, the host included, D128). A send of a wished gift to the host moves the room info
  version in the send's transaction (the metadata follows with the score's write, ≤ 2 s).
- Storage: `live_rooms.wish_gifts` (`VARCHAR(40)[]`, CHECK `live_rooms_wish_gifts_max` ≤ 4).

### 10.30 An emoji on one's own seat *(v1.27.5-live, DRAFT — D138)*

- **What (owner):** in a room with seats (`AUDIO`, `MULTI`), the host (tile 0) or someone seated
  plays one of the owner's animated emojis (the nine packs of D102, token `:<pack>_<id>:`, CP-003
  shape) **once** inside their own tile, over their picture; everyone in the room sees it.
- **Sending:** `sendLiveSeatEmoji` (`POST /live/rooms/{roomId}/seat-emoji`, `{"token"}`). Checks in
  order: 404 (room not visible), 409 `LIVE_ROOM_ENDED`, 400 `token` (`required`; `invalid_value`
  for anything that is not a pack emoji — Unicode emoji and unknown ids included), 403
  `LIVE_KICKED`, 409 `LIVE_SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` (a `SOLO`/`PK` room, or the caller is neither the host
  nor seated now), 429 with `Retry-After` (counting rule: **one every 2 s per user**). The answer is
  the `LiveSeatEmoji` `{id, seat, user, token, createdAt}`; nothing is stored or audited.
- **Delivery:** a reliable data message on topic **`seat-emoji`** to everyone in the media room
  (best effort, like every data message): `{"type":"seat-emoji","id","seat","user":UserSummary,
  "token","createdAt"}`. Apps hold no data publish permission (CP-010 `canPublishData: false`), so
  every seat emoji goes through this check. The sender's app shows its own at once and drops the
  echo (same `user`); a new emoji on a tile replaces the one playing there.
- **Apps:** the emoji plays one cycle centred over the tile's picture (about 85 % of it, under the
  name) and fades; with reduced motion the first frame shows for 1.5 s. Unknown tokens are ignored.

### 10.31 The host's statistics of a live *(v1.27.6-live, DRAFT — D140)*

- **What (owner):** the end-of-live screen shows more than the score — who came, from where, and
  how they engaged. `getLiveRoomStats` (`GET /live/rooms/{roomId}/stats`) answers it for the
  **host only**, while the live is on or after it ended. Checks: 401; 404 (room not visible, as
  `getLiveRoom`); 403 `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` for anyone but the host. Per-user default bucket (§7).
- **Privacy:** aggregates only. No endpoint lists the audience record or says who watched from
  where; a country is the viewer's own `Me.country` (§10.28, never inferred, XK excluded as in D45).
- **Fields and how they are computed:**
  - `durationSeconds`: start → end (→ now while LIVE). `score`: the live score (§10.10).
    `hostOwnPoints`: the host's own row of `live_room_tappers` (their taps since D120 and gifts
    since D128 count in the score); the host is never their own supporter, so a live whose points
    all came from the host shows supporters 0.
  - `supporters`: rows of the Contribution list (§10.12) as the host reads it, without the 50 cap;
    `topSupporters`: its first three, same order.
  - `giftCount`: Σ `quantity` of the live's sends (`live_gifts.room_id`), whoever sent them to
    whomever in the room. `chatMessages`: the live's messages not deleted (the chat sweeper
    removes them 30 days after the end). `newFollowers`: `follows` to the host created between
    the start and the end (now while LIVE) whose follower is ACTIVE — an unfollow removes the row.
  - `viewers` (from the audience record below; `null` for a live started before D140):
    `unique` = audience rows (a person or a guest counts once, however often they came back; the
    host has no row), `guests` = rows without a user, `peak` = the most presence rows at once
    (`live_rooms.peak_viewer_count`, raised with every recount), `atEnd` = `viewer_count` (the
    viewers when it ended; now while LIVE), `averageWatchSeconds` = round(Σ watch time / `unique`).
  - `viewerCountries`: the audience grouped by the viewer's country; the five largest (ties: code
    A → Z), then `OTHER` (all further countries), then `UNKNOWN` (guests and people without a
    country) — each only when non-zero; `[]` without viewers. **Rounding:** `percent` =
    round-half-up(`viewers` × 1000 / `unique`) / 10, each bucket on its own; the shares are shown
    as they are (their sum may be 99.9–100.1). Apps never re-normalize.
- **Audience record** (`live_room_audience`, one row per room and identity): written only from
  media presence (§10.8). A recorded join opens a visit (`open_since`); every removal of a presence
  row — `participant_left`, `room_finished`, a kick, guests switched off, the end, the sweeper's
  reconciliation — closes it, adding the time (never past the room's end) to `watch_ms`. A visit
  still open when read counts until the end (now while LIVE). Rows go with the room (cascade) or
  the user.


### 10.32 Premium usernames and the regular username rule *(v1.28-live, DRAFT — D146)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-27) are marked *(owner)*; every other value is a CTO default the owner may
change (server configuration where noted, otherwise a contract change).

- **Regular usernames** *(owner)*: a **new** username (registration and `PUT /me/username`) has
  **6–30** characters of a–z, 0–9 and `_` (narrowed from v1.0's `.` and `_`), at least **one letter
  and one digit**, never `_` first or last, and is not a premium username. It is sent canonical
  (lower case, trimmed). 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` on `username` with the first issue in this order:
  `premium` (a premium username: it can only be rented — the app offers the store), `too_short`,
  `too_long`, `invalid_format`, `letters_and_digits`. **Existing usernames are kept**
  (grandfathered): nobody is asked to change, and lookups, login, profiles and every path accept the
  stored shape `Username` (now 1–30, so 1–2-character premium names work everywhere).
- **Changing the username** (`changeUsername`, `PUT /me/username` `{username}` → `Me`): the rule
  above, then 409 `PREMIUM_USERNAME_ACTIVE` while a premium username is the caller's (give it back
  first), then 409 `USERNAME_TAKEN` (reserved, another account's, held by a pending registration or
  kept for a renter). The same name → 200, nothing changed; the old name is free at once (a link to
  it stops working); follows, lives and everything else follow the account, not the name.
  5 changes / day / user (`RATE_LIMIT_USERNAME_CHANGE_USER`, replacing the default). Audited
  `user.username.change` `{from, to}`.
- **Premium usernames (يوزر مميز)** *(owner)*: every name of 1–30 lower-case letters and digits
  (never `_` or `.`) that is **not** a valid regular username, plus nice patterns. Four tiers
  *(owner, matching the owner's medal art)*, decided by the name alone and **only by the server**
  (`premium-username-rules.ts`, adapted from the owner's `specialIdTierFor`; the apps show the tier
  they are given), checked in this order:

  | Tier | Names | Examples |
  | ---- | ----- | -------- |
  | `LEGEND` | 1–3 characters | `7`, `ab`, `777`, `a1b` |
  | `RUBY` | one character repeated, 4 or more | `7777`, `aaaa`, `777777` |
  | `GOLD` | 4–5 characters; or a pattern: a palindrome, doubled halves, a sequence of digits or letters (up or down), a run of three equal characters | `sara`, `1221`, `abba`, `1212`, `123456`, `abcdef`, `888991`, `ali777` |
  | `SILVER` | 6+ letters only or digits only (with none of the patterns) | `112233`, `laylaa`, `kabsoo` |

  Mixed names with a pattern (`ali777`) are premium too, so they are no longer regular names.
- **Reserved** *(owner)*: never rented — the v1.0 reserved names (`admin`, `support`, `official`,
  `staff`, `moderator`, `owner`, `system`, …, with `.`/`_` ignored), any name containing `kabso`, and
  the owner's list `premium_username_reserved` (seeded with a few brand and authority words; offensive
  words are added on the server with `premium-admin reserve add`, not committed to this public
  repository). An admin may still **grant** a reserved name (e.g. to an official account).
- **Prices** *(owner: the owner sets them, none hard-coded)*: a monthly price in coins per tier
  (`premium_username_tier_prices`) and optionally per name (`premium_username_name_prices`, which wins
  over its tier's). **While a tier has no price its names are not on sale**: status `NOT_FOR_SALE`,
  the store lists none of them and says so; nothing is ever priced by default. Managed only with
  `premium-admin price set|clear|list` (whole coins 1–1 000 000 000; audited
  `premium_username.price`).
- **Status of a name** (`getPremiumUsernameStatus`, `GET /premium-usernames/{username}`, never 404):
  `INVALID` → `REGULAR` (not premium) → the lease that holds it: `YOURS` / `YOURS_GRACE` (the caller's)
  or `TAKEN` / `HELD` (another user's, in use / in grace, `heldUntil`) → `RESERVED` → `TAKEN` (the
  username of another account — a grandfathered short name, for instance —, a live pending
  registration's, or the regular name kept for a renter) → `NOT_FOR_SALE` → `AVAILABLE`. `priceCoins`
  for AVAILABLE, YOURS and YOURS_GRACE.
- **The store** (`getPremiumUsernameStore`, `GET /premium-usernames[?tier=]`): the four tiers with
  their price (or null), `periodDays`, `graceDays`, and up to 30 **suggested** names AVAILABLE to the
  caller now — generated from patterns (one repeated digit, ascending / descending digit runs, digit
  palindromes, short letters and letter runs) and the names with their own price; never stored,
  never a promise that a name stays free.
- **Rental** *(owner: monthly rental, not a purchase)* — `rentPremiumUsername`
  (`POST /me/premium-username/rentals` `{username, priceCoins}`, `Idempotency-Key` required):
  - **Period: 30 days** (`PREMIUM_USERNAME_PERIOD_DAYS`). Rent: the name becomes the caller's
    username **at once** for one period; the username the caller had is stored as `regularUsername`
    and **kept for them** (nobody can register or change to it while the lease is ACTIVE).
  - **Renew** (the caller's ACTIVE name): the end moves by one period; prepaid at most
    **365 days ahead** (`PREMIUM_USERNAME_MAX_PREPAID_DAYS`); a grant without an end is not renewed.
  - **One premium username at a time.** Renting another name while one is ACTIVE → 409
    `PREMIUM_USERNAME_ACTIVE` (give it back first: `DELETE /me/premium-username`, no refund).
  - **Payment**: coins from the wallet in the same transaction (§10.19 ledger, reasons
    `PREMIUM_USERNAME_RENT` / `PREMIUM_USERNAME_RENEW`, reference = the payment row
    `premium_username_payments`); a balance never goes below 0 (409 `INSUFFICIENT_COINS`, nothing
    changed). `priceCoins` must equal the current price (409 `PREMIUM_USERNAME_PRICE_CHANGED`: the
    owner changed it; the app reads the status again). Not counted for families, levels or medals.
  - **Idempotent**: the same `Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours and the same body → 200 with the first
    result (the lease as it is now, `coins` = the balance right after that payment), never charged
    twice; another body → 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.
  - **Concurrency**: every write about one name and one user is serialized (advisory transaction
    locks) and backed by unique indexes (one ACTIVE/GRACE holder per name, one ACTIVE lease per user,
    one ACTIVE hold per regular name, `user_profiles.username`): two people renting the same name at
    once → exactly one wins; the other gets 409 `PREMIUM_USERNAME_UNAVAILABLE` and pays nothing.
  - 20 rent / renew / give-back calls per hour per user (`RATE_LIMIT_PREMIUM_RENT_USER`, replacing
    the default).
- **Reminders and expiry** (a sweeper every 60 s, `PREMIUM_USERNAME_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 0
  disables; batched, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`):
  - **Reminders** **3 days and 1 day** before the end (`PREMIUM_USERNAME_REMINDER_DAYS=3,1`): an
    in-app notification `PREMIUM_USERNAME_EXPIRING` (system, always on, at most one per configured
    day count per period; a renewal starts them again).
  - **Expiry**: at the end the user goes back to `regularUsername` (should it have been taken in a
    race, a free `<name><4 digits>` is used and stored), the lease turns **GRACE** for **7 days**
    (`PREMIUM_USERNAME_GRACE_DAYS`) and `PREMIUM_USERNAME_EXPIRED` is sent. During grace only the
    previous renter may rent the name again (`YOURS_GRACE`; a new period from then; the name becomes
    their username again) — everyone else sees `HELD`.
  - **End of grace**: the lease is ENDED and the name returns to the pool.
  - Notification target: `type: PREMIUM_USERNAME`, `id` = the name, `endsAt` = the period's end
    (EXPIRING) or the grace's end (EXPIRED).
- **Admin** (no API; `premium-admin` CLI, migration role): `grant --user <email|username> --username
  <name> (--days N | --forever) [--replace]` (no charge; source `GRANT`; refuses a name another user
  holds or uses; `--replace` ends the user's other ACTIVE one first), `revoke --user …` (ends ACTIVE
  and GRACE leases now, no grace, no refund), `list`, `status <name>`, `price …`, `reserve …`. Every
  rent, renew, grant, revoke, release, expiry and end of grace writes an `audit_logs` row
  (`premium_username.rent|renew|grant|revoke|release|expire|grace_end`) in its transaction.
- **The badge**: `UserSummary.premiumTier`, `PublicProfile.premiumTier` and `Me.premiumTier` carry
  the tier while the user's username **is** their premium name (stored as
  `user_profiles.premium_tier`, set and cleared with the username); absent otherwise (grandfathered
  short names get no badge). The apps draw the owner's special-ID badge (the tier's medal and pill
  with `@username`) wherever the username is shown (live header, profile, person card, chat rows,
  search results); its light sweep loops only while motion is allowed.
- **Account end**: a suspended or deleted account's lease runs to its end like any other (no refund).
- **Not in v1.28-live**: buying coins (B5), auctions or bids, transfers between users, auto-renewal,
  refunds, a history of past premium names in the app.

### 10.33 «إفيهات» quips and the host share per gift category *(v1.32-live, DRAFT — D154)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-28, D154 items 5, 5b–5f) are marked *(owner)*.

- **What a quip is** *(owner)*: a gift of the category **`QUIPS`** (the panel tab «إفيهات» / "Quips")
  that plays a short sound to **everyone in the live** and shows its line of text as a chat bubble
  while it plays (readable when muted). `Gift.quip` = `{soundKey, durationMs, text}` (null for every
  other gift): `soundKey` names a sound **bundled in the app** (`room/<id>`, `kabi/<id>`), `durationMs`
  is its length (200 … 15 000), `text` the words (or null: a sound without words). The owner's pack
  (his own Kabso sounds, loudness-normalised; provenance in the app's `assets/sounds/quips/`) is added
  with `gift-admin quips-seed`: **8 free sounds** (clap, laugh, welcome, wow, ta-da, ya salam, bell,
  ooh; tag `free`) and **27 Kabi lines** at **ghazal 99, funny 199, tease 299 coins** (tags `ghazal`,
  `funny`, `tease`). An admin manages quips like any gift (`gift-admin add|update … --category QUIPS
  --sound <key> --sound-ms <ms> [--quip-text <text>]`; a new sound needs an app release that bundles
  it). Only a QUIPS gift may cost **0** (CHECK `gifts_price_range`); the sound fields are set exactly
  for QUIPS (CHECK `gifts_quip_fields`). Quips are never in the bag (`grant` refuses them).
- **Sending** (`sendLiveGift`, §10.23, with these differences): `source` must be `COINS` and `quantity`
  1 (else 400 `invalid_value`); recipients as for any gift. **Free quips** *(owner)*: each person may
  send **one free quip per live** (any of the free ones; table `live_free_quips`, one row per live and
  person) — a second → 409 `QUIP_FREE_USED`; a free quip needs no coins, writes no ledger row and
  counts for nothing (score, boards, Contribution, levels, family). A **paid** quip is charged and
  counted exactly like a normal gift (ledger `LIVE_GIFT`, 100 points a coin, charm and support).
- **One at a time** *(owner)*: every live room has **one queue** of quips (`live_rooms.quip_busy_until`,
  written under the room row's lock): a quip starts when the queue is free (now at the earliest) and
  keeps it busy for `durationMs` + 400 ms. A quip that would start more than
  `QUIP_QUEUE_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` (default **60**) from now → 409 `QUIP_QUEUE_FULL` (nothing stored,
  charged or played). The response carries `quip` (`LiveQuip`), and the room gets a reliable data
  message on topic **`quip`**: `{"type":"quip","quip":LiveQuip}` — **instead of** the `gift` message (a
  quip is heard, not shown as a gift effect). `LiveQuip` = `{id, roomId, kind: GIFT|SOUNDBOARD,
  giftCode, soundKey, durationMs, text, free, sender: UserSummary, startsAt, delayMs, createdAt}`.
  **App:** plays it `delayMs` after the message arrives (so every phone plays the queue in the same
  order without a shared clock), one at a time, from the bundled file; shows `text` (or the quip's name
  when `text` is null) with the sender when it starts to play — D224: as a **gift strip** (the gifts'
  column, queue and 3 s) and a **chat line** like a gift's («فلان أرسل إفيه: …»), both made by the app
  from this message (no extra server event); plays nothing when the app's **Sound effects** setting is
  off or the viewer muted quips in this live (the strip and line still show); a quip from someone the
  reader blocked is skipped.
- **The soundboard** *(owner: host and moderators keep a free soundboard, 1 per 2 s)*:
  `playLiveSound` (`POST /live/rooms/{roomId}/sounds`, `{"soundCode"}` = an enabled **free** QUIPS
  gift). Checks: 401; 429 from the route's bucket; 404 (cannot see the room); 409 `LIVE_ROOM_ENDED`;
  400 body; 403 `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` (not the host or a moderator of this live); 409 `GIFT_UNAVAILABLE`
  (not an enabled free quip); 429 (one every 2 s per user, `Retry-After`); 409 `QUIP_QUEUE_FULL`. 201
  `{quip: LiveQuip}` (`kind` `SOUNDBOARD`, `free` true); it takes the same queue and the same data
  message. Nothing is stored but the queue's tail.
- **The host share per category** *(owner: quips 50 %, normal gifts 65 % — D149)*: server config
  `GIFT_HOST_SHARE_PERCENTS` (default `POPULAR:65,EVENT:65,FUN:65,QUIPS:50`; every non-lucky category
  once, 0–100, up to two decimals; LUCKY keeps `LUCKY_GIFT_HOST_SHARE_PERCENT`, §10.27). Every send
  stores the share in force (`live_gifts.host_share_bps`, basis points), so a later change never
  rewrites history; sends before v1.32-live were backfilled (lucky: their draws' share; others 6 500).
  This is the **earnings** share only (what the host will be paid out of a send's value, D149); the
  score, charm and boards are unchanged (§10.23, §10.27). A gift sent in a direct conversation
  (v1.40-social, §11.13) stores the DM recipient share instead (`GIFT_DM_RECIPIENT_SHARE_PERCENT`,
  quips included; lucky: the lucky share).
  *(v1.106-social, D341, §10.140)* A normal gift whose recipients are all **direct** (the hosting permission, no
  agency) stores `GIFT_DIRECT_HOST_SHARE_PERCENT` (70 %) instead of the category share — a creator's live
  `GIFT_DIRECT_CREATOR_SHARE_PERCENT` (75 %); quips unchanged.
- **Not in v1.32-live:** hosted (downloadable) quip sounds (a new sound needs an app release), a
  room-wide switch to turn viewers' quips off, quips outside a live, payouts of the host share (D149).

### 10.34 Traffic cards «بطاقة الزيارات» *(v1.33-live, DRAFT — D154b; CP-014 part C, the room boost)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-28, D154 items 15, 15b, 15c) are marked *(owner)*. This is the room boost of
CP-014 part C (never built before): one mechanism, no second "boost".

- **What it is** *(owner)*: a card that puts a LIVE room in one of **`LIVE_BOOST_SLOTS` = 3** paid
  slots at the top of the live list for its length, with a small «مميز» / "Featured" label. Lengths
  and prices are server config `LIVE_BOOST_PRICES` *(owner 15c: 10 min 10 000 · 20 min 18 000 · 30 min
  25 000 · 60 min 45 000 coins)*; `getLiveBoostOffers` returns them with `savePercent` (rounded saving
  against the shortest length per minute: 0 / 10 / 17 / 25).
- **Who** *(owner)*: the host for their own live, or **any viewer for the host** (a gift of exposure).
  **The host earns nothing from it** *(owner 15c)*: no score, charm, support, boards or earnings share;
  the buyer's family gets nothing either. Paid with coins (ledger `LIVE_BOOST`) or with one of the
  buyer's **cards** (`live_boost_cards`, by length), which only an admin grants as rewards:
  `boost-admin grant <email|username> <minutes> <quantity>` (a length on sale; audited
  `live.boost_card.grant`), `boost-admin cards <user>`, `boost-admin queue`.
- **The queue** *(owner: a queue and an honest ETA)*: one FIFO queue over the slots; a card starts at
  once when a slot is free, else when the slot that frees first frees. A live has **at most one card
  running or waiting** (409 `BOOST_ROOM_BUSY`). A card that would start more than
  `LIVE_BOOST_MAX_WAIT_MINUTES` (180) from now → 409 `BOOST_QUEUE_FULL`. `startsAt` is a promise "at the
  latest": cards are planned again only when one is cancelled or cut short, which never makes a later
  card start later. `nextStartAt` (offers) is when a new card would start now. When a live ends, its
  **waiting** card is cancelled (`CANCELLED`) and **refunded** (coins with `LIVE_BOOST_REFUND`, or the
  card back), its **running** card stops there (its time is used; the slot frees at once). Settled by a
  background job (`LIVE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`) and before every purchase.
- **`buyLiveBoost`** (`POST /live/rooms/{roomId}/boosts`, `{minutes, source: COINS|CARD, clientId}`):
  checks 401, 429, 404 (cannot see the room), 409 `LIVE_ROOM_ENDED`, 400 body (`minutes` not on sale →
  `invalid_value`), a retry with the same `clientId` → 200 the first card, 409 `BOOST_ROOM_BUSY`, 409
  `BOOST_QUEUE_FULL`, 409 `INSUFFICIENT_COINS` / `BOOST_CARD_INSUFFICIENT`. 201 `{boost: LiveBoost, coins,
  cards}`. The room gets `{"type":"boost","boost":LiveBoost}` on topic `boost` (best effort).
  `LiveBoost` = `{id, roomId, host, buyer: UserSummary, minutes, source, coinsCharged, state:
  WAITING|RUNNING|DONE|CANCELLED, startsAt, endsAt, createdAt}`.
- **The list:** `listActiveLiveBoosts` (`GET /live/boosts/active`, guests too) → `{data: [{room:
  LiveRoomSummary, endsAt}]}`: the rooms whose card runs now, at most `slots`, the earliest started first,
  only LIVE, fresh, ACTIVE hosts and no block with the caller. **App:** the hub shows them first, each
  marked «مميز», and leaves them out of the list under it. `listLiveRoomBoosts` lists a room's last 12
  cards (its host's tool shows the running or waiting one and when it starts).
- **Not in v1.33-live:** buying cards to keep for later (cards come only from admin rewards), choosing a
  start time, boosting outside a live, refunds of a running card, an admin UI.
- **v1.51-live (D233):** the lengths are the four rocket stages, priced in coins and editable in the panel — §10.81.

### 10.35 Newcomers «الجدد» *(v1.34-live, DRAFT — D154c)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-28, D154 item 13) are marked *(owner)*.

- **Who is a newcomer** *(owner: 30 days, was 7)*: a user whose account is younger than server config
  `NEWCOMER_DAYS` (default **30**, 1–365). The signup date itself is **never** sent anywhere.
- **The badge** *(owner: «جديد 🌱» next to their name in chat for 30 days, visible to all)*:
  `LiveChatAuthorBadges.newcomer` (§10.11), on send, list and the `chat` data message, cached like the
  other badges (up to 30 s). **App:** a small «جديد 🌱» / "New 🌱" chip after the author's name.
- **The list** *(owner: visible to host + moderators)*: `listLiveNewcomers` (`GET
  /live/rooms/{roomId}/newcomers`) → `{newcomerDays, data: [UserSummary]}`: the signed-in people in the
  live's media session now (CP-010) who are newcomers, the most recent arrivals first, at most 100,
  never the host, never someone in a block either way with the caller. Checks: 401, 404, 409
  `LIVE_ROOM_ENDED`, 403 `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` (not the host or a moderator).
- **«رحّب» / Welcome** *(owner: a ready welcome line mentioning them, rate-limited)*: the app sends an
  ordinary chat message (`sendLiveChatMessage`, §10.11 — its limits, blocked words and muting apply)
  with the ready text «أهلاً @username 🌱 نوّرت البث» / "Welcome @username 🌱 glad you're here"; it
  offers it once per person per live on that phone. No new write operation.
- **Not in v1.34-live:** newcomer statistics, automatic welcomes, a newcomer badge outside the live chat.

### 10.36 The host's data center «مركز البيانات» *(v1.35-live, DRAFT — D154d)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-28, D154 item 14) are marked *(owner)*.

- **(a) End of a live** *(owner: duration, peak, total viewers, new followers, gifts count + coin value,
  top 3 supporters)*: `getLiveRoomStats` (§10.31) already answered all but the value; v1.35-live adds
  `giftCoins` (Σ `totalCoins` of the live's sends) and `earningsCoins` (the host's share of the gifts
  **they** received: Σ floor(recipient coins × the send's `host_share_bps` / 10 000), §10.33 — quips 50 %,
  other gifts 65 %, lucky 10 %; display only, payouts are D149). The app's end screen shows both.
- **(b) The data center** *(owner: DAY / WEEK / MONTH / YEAR; live hours, earnings, follower growth,
  best hours, simple charts)*: `getMyLiveStats` (`GET /live/stats/me?period=DAY|WEEK|MONTH|YEAR`, the
  caller's own lives only; 400 `period` otherwise). Periods in `LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE`: DAY = today by
  hour; WEEK = the last 7 days by day; MONTH = the last 30 days by day; YEAR = the last 12 months by month
  (each from the start of its first bucket to now). `totals` = `{lives, liveSeconds, giftCount, giftCoins,
  earningsCoins, newFollowers, uniqueViewers, peakViewers}`; `series` = one bucket per hour / day / month
  `{start (local "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"), liveSeconds, earningsCoins, newFollowers}`; `heatmap` = the non-empty
  cells of lives started per ISO weekday × hour `{weekday, hour, lives, viewers}` (the best hours). Lives
  count by their **start**; follows by when they were made (ACTIVE followers; an unfollow removes the row).
  The live running now counts once it ends.
- **Storage** *(owner: persist a per-live summary at the end)*: `live_summaries`, one row per ended live
  written **once** by a summariser (the live sweeper's interval, 200 a batch, and the caller's own lives
  before each read) — so every end path (the host, the heartbeat timeout, a suspension, an admin) and
  lives from before v1.35-live are covered without hooking each one. The rows are never changed. The
  owner's "daily rollups for the year" are not a separate table: a host's year is at most a few thousand
  summary rows, aggregated per read with the `(host, started_at)` index.
- **Not in v1.35-live:** a live in progress in the periods, other hosts' data, exports, payouts (D149).

### 10.37 A live's program «قائمة البرامج» *(v1.36-live, DRAFT — D154e)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-28, D154 item 10) are marked *(owner)*. Separate from the live schedule
(§10.16), which plans future lives.

- **What** *(owner: up to 10 segments, time + title, for the current live)*: `setLiveProgram`
  (`PUT /live/rooms/{roomId}/program`, `{"items": [{"startsAt", "title"}]}`) — the host of a LIVE room
  replaces the whole program (`[]` clears it). Checks: 401, 404, 403 `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` (not the host), 409
  `LIVE_ROOM_ENDED`, 400 (≤ 10 → `items` / `too_many`; titles 1–60 code points after the §6 hygiene, no
  line break → `required` / `too_long` / `invalid_format` on `items.N.title`; `startsAt` strictly
  ascending, from one minute before the live's start to 24 h after it → `items` / `invalid_value`).
  Titles are masked with the host's blocked words *(owner: through the blocked-words filter)*, like
  chat (§10.14). Stored in `live_program_items`; a segment that keeps its start and title keeps its
  announcement.
- **Reading** *(owner: viewers see a compact card, current highlighted; persists with the live, late
  joiners see it)*: `getLiveProgram` (`GET …/program`, anyone who can see the room, guests too, also
  after the end) → `LiveProgram` `{roomId, items: [{position, startsAt, title}], current}` — `current`
  is the last segment started while the live is on, else null.
- **Announcements** *(owner: server-timed; honest if the host ends early)*: every change goes to the
  room as `{"type":"program","program":LiveProgram}` on topic **`program`**; when a segment starts the
  server sends `{"type":"program-segment","item":LiveProgramItem}` once (a job on the live sweeper's
  interval, safe on several instances). Nothing is sent for a live that ended (its remaining segments
  are simply never announced), and a segment first seen more than 10 minutes after its start is marked
  without a message.
- **App:** the host edits it from Room Tools «قائمة البرامج»; everyone sees a small card under the room's
  header with the segment on now and the next one (a tap opens the whole list) and, when a segment
  starts, the card says «بدأت الفقرة: …» for a few seconds.
- **Not in v1.36-live:** reminders before a segment, segments in the live list, segment lengths.

### 10.38 Stickers on a live «ملصقات» *(v1.37-live, DRAFT — D154h)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-28, D154 item 3) are marked *(owner)*.

- **What** *(owner: Kabi stickers + free text, at most 3 at once; the host drags, scales, rotates;
  everyone sees them)*: `setLiveStickers` (`PUT /live/rooms/{roomId}/stickers`, `{"items": [...]}`) —
  the host of a LIVE room replaces all its stickers (`[]` clears them; a move sends them again with
  their `id`, which they keep). Each is exactly one of `artKey` (from the catalogue) and `text` (1–40
  code points after the §6 hygiene, one line, masked with the host's blocked words *(owner: through the
  blocked-words filter)*), with `x`, `y` in 0–1 — the sticker's centre relative to the picture, so it
  lands in the same place on every screen *(owner: positions normalised)* — `scale` 0.25–4 and
  `rotation` −π–π radians. The order is the drawing order (the last on top). Checks: 401, 404, 403
  `AUTH_FORBIDDEN`, 409 `LIVE_ROOM_ENDED`, 400 (`items` / `too_many`; `items.N.artKey` /
  `invalid_value`; `items.N.text` / `required` / `too_long` / `invalid_format`; `items.N.x` … range;
  an `id` twice → `items` / `invalid_value`). Rate: the taps rule (`RATE_LIMIT_LIVE_TAPS_USER`,
  bucket `live:stickers`), enough for drags sent when a gesture ends.
- **Reading** *(owner: late joiners get the current state)*: `getLiveStickers` (`GET …/stickers`,
  anyone who can see the room, guests too; `[]` once the live ended). Every change also goes to the
  room as `{"type":"stickers","stickers":LiveStickers}` on topic **`sticker`**.
- **Catalogue** *(owner: admins can add sticker packs later)*: `listLiveStickerArt` (`GET
  /live/stickers`) — the built-in Kabi pack (the app's own animated art, in the code), then the
  enabled rows of `live_sticker_art` that admins add (SQL for now; an admin screen later). An app
  shows only art it can draw; a sticker of unknown art is skipped on that phone.
- **Not in v1.37-live:** paid stickers *(owner: not now)*, viewers' stickers, uploaded images.

### 10.39 YouTube watch-together «يوتيوب» *(v1.38-live, DRAFT — D154i)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-28, D154 item 9) are marked *(owner)*.

- **Playback** *(owner: the official YouTube embedded player only, per YouTube's terms; each phone
  streams from YouTube; the server only relays the sync state)*: no video passes through Kabso. The
  state is `LiveWatch` — `video` (`LiveWatchVideo`: id, title, channel, thumbnail) or null,
  `playing`, `positionMs` at `updatedAt`, `serverTime` (to place the position on a phone whose clock
  differs) and `searchEnabled`. A phone plays from `positionMs + (serverTime − updatedAt)` plus the
  time since it received the state, while `playing`; it seeks when it drifts more than 2 s.
- **The host** (`setLiveWatch`, `PUT /live/rooms/{roomId}/watch`): sends the player state on every
  play, pause and seek and every 15 s while playing (the taps rule, bucket `live:watch`). `video` is
  an 11-character id or a YouTube link (watch, youtu.be, shorts, embed, live, music, mobile); the
  server asks YouTube (oEmbed) for its title and whether it may be embedded — 422
  `YOUTUBE_VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE` otherwise *(owner: non-embeddable videos → an honest message)*. Null
  stops watching. Every change reaches the room as `{"type":"watch","watch":LiveWatch}` on topic
  **`watch`**; late joiners read `getLiveWatch` (guests too; no video once the live ended).
- **Suggestions** *(owner: viewers suggest by link or search; the host approves or rejects; one per
  60 s per viewer; titles through the blocked-words filter)*: `suggestLiveWatch` → `PENDING` (the room
  gets `{"type":"watch-suggestion","suggestion":LiveWatchSuggestion}`; the host's app lists it, the
  others ignore it); `listLiveWatchSuggestions` (host, oldest first, ≤ 50);
  `decideLiveWatchSuggestion` `{approve}` — approve plays it from the start, reject turns it down.
  Titles (the host's and the suggestions') are masked with the host's blocked words.
- **Search** *(owner: a server-side YouTube Data API key; no key → paste a link, search «غير مفعّل
  بعد»)*: `searchYoutube` (`GET /live/youtube/search?q=`, signed in) — embeddable videos, safe search
  moderate, 10 results, cached 10 min per query (the free quota is about 100 searches a day); 503
  `YOUTUBE_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE` without `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` or when YouTube fails. The key is a server
  secret, never in the app or in git.
- **Not in v1.38-live:** a queue of several videos, viewers' own controls, YouTube Shorts' vertical
  layout.
- *(v1.39-live, DRAFT — D173)* **Cinema in audio rooms** *(owner: «عندما مشاهدة يوتيوب لا يكون هناك
  إلا ١٠ كراسي فقط»)*: while an AUDIO room has a video (`live_watch` row) it is a cinema of
  **10 seats** — the host's (0) and seats 1–9, the 10 seats drawn in the owner's cinema picture.
  `LiveSeats.cinema` is true; seats 10+ are listed `LOCKED`. When the video starts (`setLiveWatch` or
  an approved suggestion), in one seat transaction: everyone on seat 10+ moves to the first free seat
  1–9 in seat order (mic mute kept) or, with none free, leaves the seat (publish permission withdrawn;
  the app tells them why); pending requests and invitations for seats 10+ expire; locked seats 10+
  are dropped. While it lasts, a request, invitation or lock for seat 10+ → 409
  `LIVE_SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` (without a seat number the first free seat 1–9 is used). When the video
  stops the room's own `seatCount` is usable again; nobody is moved back. Both moves raise the seat
  version (§10.9). Rooms of 10 seats or fewer change nothing. MULTI rooms are never a cinema (their
  video floats in a window, D160).

### 10.40 The Me hub's wallet, earnings and creator center *(v1.43-social, DRAFT — D164)*

Owner request (2026-10-29): make the Me hub's «قريباً» buttons work **without fake data and without new
business rules**. Only what stored data already answers is built; recharge, withdrawal, VIP, SVIP, the
task center and the event center wait for owner decisions (proposal CP-024).

- **Coin history** «المحفظة»: `listMyWalletLedger` (`GET /wallet/me/ledger`, cursor / limit §5) — the
  caller's `wallet_ledger` rows (§10.19), newest first (`created_at` desc, `id` desc; signed social cursor
  bound to the caller): `{id, reason, delta, balanceAfter, createdAt}`. `delta` is signed (never 0). The
  row's `reference_id` is **not** returned (it can name another person's send or payment). New
  `WalletLedgerReason` values may appear with later features; clients show an unknown one as a generic
  change. The balance itself stays `getMyWallet`. Recharge is not built (B5: no payment method yet).
- *(v1.52-social, D179: **superseded** — the cherry balance of §10.46 is the source of truth; the two reads below
  stay for older apps, deprecated.)*
- **Earnings** «اربح المال»: there is **no separate earnings balance** in the ledger — a recipient's share is
  not credited as coins. Earnings are computed per read from the gift sends the caller received
  (`live_gift_recipients` × `live_gifts`, live and direct-conversation sends alike): for each send,
  floor(recipient `coins` × the send's stored `host_share_bps` / 10 000) (§10.33; the data center's
  `earningsCoins` of §10.36 is the same sum for one live). Sends whose share is 0 (free quips, a 0 % share)
  are left out. `getMyEarnings` (`GET /wallet/me/earnings`) → `{totalCoins, last7DaysCoins,
  last30DaysCoins, sendCount}` (rolling windows ending now). `listMyEarnings` (`GET
  /wallet/me/earnings/history`, cursor / limit §5, newest first, signed social cursor bound to the
  caller) → `{id (the send), createdAt, context LIVE|DM, giftCode, giftName (reader's language, §10.1),
  quantity, giftCoins, shareBps, coins, sender}`; `sender` is null when the sender is not ACTIVE or a block
  stands between them either way. **Display only:** earnings cannot be spent or withdrawn (payout method
  and rules are D149, undecided).
- **Creator center** «مركز صنّاع المحتوى»: `getMyCreatorStats` (`GET /me/creator-stats?period=`,
  `LAST_7_DAYS` | `LAST_30_DAYS` | `ALL_TIME` | *(v1.49-social, D172)* `THIS_MONTH`; 400 `period`
  otherwise). Rolling windows ending now; `from` is null for `ALL_TIME`. `THIS_MONTH` is the current
  calendar month so far: from the 1st at 00:00 in `LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE` (the app's one region, as the
  families' month) until now; `month` is that month as `YYYY-MM` (null for the other periods), so the app
  names the month of the region rather than of the phone's zone.
  - `followers.total`: ACTIVE accounts following the caller now (like `PublicProfile.followerCount`);
    `followers.newInPeriod`: of those, the follows made in the window (null for `ALL_TIME`). An unfollow
    deletes its row, so this is **not** a net growth figure.
  - `posts` / `reels`: the caller's `format: POST` / `format: REEL` posts **published in the window**,
    published and not deleted or removed, with the sums of their current `viewCount`, `likeCount`,
    `commentCount`, `shareCount` (the counters are totals, not per day; per-day history is not stored).
  - `live`: the caller's ended lives **started in the window**, from `live_summaries` (§10.36; the caller's
    unsummarised lives are summarised first): `{lives, liveSeconds, giftCount, giftCoins, earningsCoins,
    newFollowers, peakViewers}`. A live in progress is not counted until it ends.
  - Not included: the popularity points (kept only 15 days, §10.15), per-day charts of post metrics (not
    stored), other people's data.
- **Rate limits:** all three reads use the per-user default (§7).
- **Not in v1.43-social:** recharge (B5), withdrawal (D149), VIP / SVIP, the task center, the event
  center — proposal `docs/contracts/proposals/CP-024-me-hub-programs.md`.

### 10.41 The Me hub's programs: Task Center, Event Center, SVIP and recharge packages *(v1.44-social, DRAFT — D166, CP-024)*

Owner (2026-10-29) approved CP-024 with defaults (recorded in `docs/contracts/proposals/CP-024-me-hub-programs.md`).
Every value below is server config or an admin-managed row: the owner changes it without an app release.

- **Clock:** days start at 00:00 and weeks on Monday in `LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE` (the boards' clock, §10.15).
- **Task Center** «مركز المهام» (`getMyTasks`, `checkIn`, `claimMyTask`):
  - Tasks are rows of `task_definitions` (code, `DAILY` | `WEEKLY`, metric, target, `rewardCoins` — cherries
    since v1.53-social, §10.41.3 —, audience
    `EVERYONE` | `HOSTS`, names ar/en, enabled, order), changed only with the `task-admin` CLI. Defaults: watch
    a live of someone else for 15 s (1×) +5; follow 10 people +5; 10 live chat messages in someone else's live
    +5; 10 gift sends paid with coins +15 (daily); host tasks (weekly, hosting permission holders only): live
    60 minutes +100, receive gifts worth 1 000 coins +100.
  - **Progress is computed by the server** per read from stored data: `live_room_audience` (first joined in
    the period, ≥ 15 s watched), `follows` (made in the period and still standing; an unfollow deletes the row,
    so a follow that no longer stands at claim time does not count), `live_chat_messages` (not deleted),
    `live_gifts` (`coins_charged > 0`), `live_rooms` (minutes inside the period; a live in progress up to its
    last heartbeat), `live_gift_recipients` (from other ACTIVE senders). Counterparts must be ACTIVE; nothing
    is reported by the app. "Share a live room" is not offered: a share is a copy of a link on the phone, which
    the server cannot see (it would be self-reported).
  - Claim order: 404 unknown / disabled / not for the caller → already claimed in this period → 200 (nothing
    paid again) → 409 `TASK_NOT_COMPLETED` → (daily) 409 `TASK_DAILY_CAP_REACHED` → 201. One payout per
    person, task and period (`task_claims_once`); claims and check-ins of one person are serialized by a row
    lock, so concurrent claims pay once and the cap holds. Paid as `wallet_ledger` `TASK_REWARD`
    (reference: the claim) in the claim's transaction.
  - **Daily cap** `TASK_DAILY_CAP_COINS` = 50: daily tasks and the check-in together; a claim pays at most
    what is left; weekly host tasks are outside it (once a week each).
  - **Check-in** once per day: `TASK_CHECK_IN_COINS` = 5, plus `TASK_CHECK_IN_STREAK_BONUS_COINS` = 20 on every
    7th day in a row (a missed day restarts the streak); `CHECK_IN_REWARD` (reference: the check-in), within
    the cap (after it the check-in keeps the streak and pays 0). 201 now / 200 already today.
  - XP is not awarded: the level systems count coin value (CP-005), so free level points would let tasks
    buy levels. Rewards are coins only.
- **Event Center** «مركز الفعاليات» (`listEvents`, `getEvent`, `getEventLeaderboard`):
  - Events are created with the `event-admin` CLI: titles and rules ar/en, an optional https banner URL,
    start, end (or permanent), metric (`GIFT_COINS_RECEIVED`, `GIFT_COINS_SENT`, `LIVE_MINUTES`,
    `TAPS_RECEIVED`, `NEW_FOLLOWERS`), audience, regions (ISO countries), featured («رائج»), prizes per rank
    (1–100, coins).
  - Tabs: `CALENDAR` (events for everyone overlapping a month), `PERMANENT`, `REGIONAL` (events targeted at
    the caller's own country, §10.28; none without a country). Empty when nothing is configured.
  - The board is computed from existing tables (gift recipients and sends, `live_rooms`, `live_room_tappers`
    of lives started in the window, `follows`) for the event's window: ACTIVE people, the audience and
    regions, ties by user id; top 100 and the caller's own rank; blocked people are left out of the caller's
    list (ranks stay).
  - After the end the sweeper (`EVENTS_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`) freezes the top 100 into `event_results`
    once; `EVENT_PRIZE_REVIEW_HOURS` = 24 later (unless `event-admin hold`) every prize is paid once as
    `EVENT_PRIZE` (reference: the result row, unique), to ACTIVE winners; others forfeit.
- **SVIP** (`getMySvip`): earned, never bought (real-money top-up is blocked, B5). Gift spending
  (`LIVE_GIFT`, `LUCKY_GIFT`, `DM_GIFT`, `CP_GIFT` ledger rows) in the rolling `SVIP_WINDOW_DAYS` = 30 days
  reaches `SVIP_TIERS` = 50 000 / 150 000 / 400 000; a tier lasts `SVIP_STATUS_DAYS` = 30 days after the last
  moment its threshold was met. Computed from the ledger per read (no table). The perks (badge, frame,
  coloured chat name, entry banner, daily bullet, entry effect, viewer-list priority, monthly bag gift) are
  listed with `available: false` until each is built; clients never show one as active. Points redemption
  for anti-mute / unban is out of scope (it would undermine moderation).
- **Recharge packages** (`listRechargePackages`): `WALLET_RECHARGE_PACKAGES` (`coins+bonus:price[:original]`,
  prices in minor units of `WALLET_RECHARGE_CURRENCY`); defaults (D203, owner 2026-10-31) are the website's
  amounts at $12.50 per 1 000 000 coins: 100 000 $1.25, 500 000 $6.25, 1 000 000 $12.50, 5 000 000 $62.50,
  10 000 000 $125, 50 000 000 $625, no bonus. `purchasesEnabled` is false
  and there is no purchase operation until B5.
- **Rate limits:** every route uses the per-user default (§7).
#### 10.41.1 The daily task pool *(v1.50-social, DRAFT — D176)*

Owner (2026-10-30): «أريد أن تصنع الكثير من المهام اليومية، ترسل لكل شخص بناءً على مستواه» — many daily
tasks, each person getting a few a day by level; rewards are **coins only** («العملات فقط»: no experience
or level points from tasks). Every value is a default the owner changes with `task-admin` (no release).

- **Templates:** `task_definitions` rows with `pool = true` (code `P_…`, DAILY), a variety group (`WATCH`,
  `LIVE`, `SOCIAL`, `GIFT`, `CONTENT`, `MESSAGE`, `HOST`) and one target and one coin reward per level band
  1…4 (`band_targets`, `band_rewards`; 0 = not offered in that band). `HOST` templates are for hosting
  permission holders only. *(v1.94-social, D297: the group `CREATOR`, audience `CREATORS`, is for creator-programme
  members only — and they never get `HOST` templates; §10.110.)* Fixed (non-pool) tasks keep §10.41; D166's four fixed daily tasks are switched
  off by the migration (the pool offers the same actions per band; the team can switch them on again).
- **Bands** (`task_pool_bands`): the band is the last whose `min_level` the person's level reaches — the
  higher of their **Support** and **Charm** («الجاذبية», `ATTRACTIVENESS`) current levels (enabled
  categories; 0 = none). Defaults: 1 «مبتدئ» from 0 — 6 tasks a day; 2 «نشيط» from 10 — 7; 3 «متقدّم» from 30
  — 7; 4 «نخبة» from 60 — 8; of these, host tasks for hosts 2 / 2 / 2 / 3.
- **Assignment** (`task_assignments`): fixed at the person's first read (or claim) of the day — the day of
  §10.41's clock — with the band's target and reward at that moment; later template, band or level
  changes apply from the next day (a template switched off is hidden). The choice is deterministic for the
  person and the day (FNV-1a of `userId:day` seeding a shuffle of the offered templates): hosts get the
  band's host tasks first; everyone's tasks then fill the band's count, at most one per group, then at
  most two; never the same template twice. The next day is a new assignment.
- **Progress** (computed per read from stored data, counterparts ACTIVE, as §10.41): `WATCH_LIVES` (lives
  watched ≥ 15 s), `WATCH_MINUTES` (whole minutes watched in lives first joined in the day),
  `AUDIO_ROOMS` (audio rooms joined, ≥ 15 s), `LIVE_CHAT_MESSAGES`, `LIVE_TAPS` (taps the server counted in
  lives started in the day), `FOLLOWS`, `POST_COMMENTS` (on someone else's posts, not deleted),
  `GIFT_SENDS`, `NEW_HOST_GIFTS` (paid gift sends to a host whose permission is ≤ 30 days old), `POSTS` /
  `REELS` (published, not removed or deleted), `STORIES` (not deleted or removed), `DM_FRIENDS` (different
  people messaged who follow each other with the caller; a message lives 24 h, so the day's are stored),
  `DM_VOICE_MESSAGES`, and for hosts `HOST_LIVE_MINUTES`, `HOST_GIFTS_RECEIVED` (gift sends received),
  `HOST_GUESTS` (seat requests or invitations ACCEPTED in the caller's lives).
- **Not offered** (the server cannot see them, and nothing is self-reported): sharing a room (a link copied
  on the phone), recharging (no purchases, B5), and any action only the app could report.
- **Claim** as §10.41: a pool task is claimable only when it is one of the caller's tasks of today (else
  404); its reward is the assignment's, within `TASK_DAILY_CAP_COINS` like every daily task.
- **Defaults** (targets / coins for bands 1–4; *v1.53-social, D184:* now cherries, each ×10 — §10.41.3): watch lives 15 s 1·2·3·5 / 3·4·5·6; watch minutes
  5·15·30·30 / 4·6·8·10; audio rooms 1·2·3·3 / 3·4·5·6; live comments 3·5·10·20 / 3·4·5·6; hearts
  20·50·100·200 / 2·3·4·5; follow 1·3·5·10 / 2·3·4·5; post comments 1·3·5·10 / 2·3·4·5; send a gift
  1·1·3·5 / 5·6·8·10; send gifts —·10·10·15 / —·12·15·20; support a new host 1·1·1·2 / 5·6·8·10; post
  1·1·1·2 / 4·5·6·8; reel —·1·1·1 / —·6·8·10; story 1·1·1·2 / 3·4·5·6; message a friend 1·1·2·3 / 2·3·4·5;
  voice message 1·1·1·2 / 2·3·4·5; host: live minutes 30·30·60·60 / 8·10·12·15, gifts received
  3·5·10·20 / 5·6·8·10, accept a guest 1·1·2·3 / 4·5·6·8.
- **Wire:** `ProgramTask.pooled`, the new `ProgramTask.metric` values (clients map an unknown metric to a
  generic icon) and `MyTasks.band` (`band`, `level`, `name`, `host`).

#### 10.41.2 The Event Center calendar and the Task Center banner *(v1.50-social, DRAFT — D176)*

- `EventSummary.summary`: the calendar bar's second line (a short prize line, ≤ 80 characters, ar/en, null

#### 10.41.3 Task rewards in cherries *(v1.53-social, DRAFT — D184)*

Owner (2026-10-30): the Task Center shows only the active tasks (the «مهام الماس» tab is removed — the app
has no tab bar there) and the active tasks («المهام النشطة», «مكافآت المهام», the weekly host tasks) reward
**cherries** instead of coins, at the same value. This replaces §10.41.1's "coins only".

- **Conversion:** 1 coin = 10 cherries. Migration `20261231110000_task_cherries` multiplies every stored
  reward by 10 — `task_definitions.reward_cherries` (was `reward_coins`), `band_rewards`,
  `task_assignments.reward_cherries` (offers) — and widens the bounds to 1 000 000 000 cherries a task
  (owner: rewards may grow a lot). Defaults: the D166 fixed tasks 50 / 50 / 50 / 150, host weekly tasks
  1 000 / 1 000; the pool's §10.41.1 coins ×10. Owner-changeable with `task-admin set --reward/--rewards`
  (in cherries).
- **Raised rewards (owner, same day):** at most about **$5 a month** from tasks — at $1.10 per 1 000 000
  cherries ≈ 4 500 000 cherries a month ≈ **150 000 a day**. Migration `20261231120000_task_rewards_raise`
  multiplies every stored task reward (fixed, band and today's offers) by **300** from the values above, so
  a band's full daily list lands near the cap: the D166 fixed tasks 15 000 / 15 000 / 15 000 / 45 000, host
  weekly tasks 300 000 / 300 000 (outside the daily cap), the pool's §10.41.1 coins ×3 000 (e.g. 3 coins →
  9 000 cherries). Claims already made keep what they paid.
- **Credit:** a claim writes `task_claims` (`reward_amount`, `reward_currency` `CHERRIES`) and, in the same
  transaction, a `cherry_ledger` row `TASK_REWARD` (a credit; reference `<code>@<period start>`, e.g.
  `P_FOLLOW@2026-10-30`, so the ledger itself allows one per person, task and day or ISO week) with the
  balance. The row appears in the Cherries tab's history (`listMyCherryLedger`, `gift: null`). Claim
  order and statuses as §10.41.
- **Cap:** daily tasks share `TASK_DAILY_CAP_CHERRIES` = 150 000 (owner: ≈ $5 a month; was 500, the old 50
  coins); the app shows it with thousands separators («مكافآت اليوم: x من 150,000 كرزة»); a claim pays at most what
  is left, then 409 `TASK_DAILY_CAP_REACHED`. Weekly host tasks stay outside it.
- **Check-in («مكافآت تسجيل الدخول»):** unchanged — it pays **coins** (`wallet_ledger` `CHECK_IN_REWARD`,
  5 a day, +20 every 7th day); `TASK_DAILY_CAP_COINS` (50) now counts only coins (the check-in and daily
  claims made in coins before this version), so task cherries never reduce it.
- **History:** claims made before the migration keep what they paid (`reward_currency` `COINS`, their
  `wallet_ledger` `TASK_REWARD` rows untouched); on the wire `claimedCoins` is their coins and
  `claimedCherries` 0 (a cherry claim: `claimedCoins` 0).
- **Wire:** `ProgramTask.rewardCherries` / `claimedCherries`, `MyTasks.dailyCapCherries` /
  `dailyEarnedCherries` (`dailyCapCoins` / `dailyEarnedCoins` are the check-in's), `TaskClaimResult.paidCherries`
  / `balanceCherries`; `ProgramTask.rewardCoins` is deprecated and 0.
- **Withdrawal:** task cherries are cherries like gift cherries but stay **locked** for withdrawal until the
  unlock rule of §10.46.1 passes.
- *(v1.57-social, D188)* **Superseded values:** the ×300 raise and the 150 000 daily cap came from wrong
  pricing; §10.51 sets the defaults, the 50 000 daily cap and a monthly cap.

#### 10.41.4 The generated Task Center and the smart assignment *(v1.86-social, DRAFT — D281)*

Owner (D281): more than 100 000 different, varied Task Center tasks, generated from templates × parameters, assigned
smartly to each person from their own data (activity, host or viewer, level, recent completion, variety). The Task
Center's reward rules stay (§10.41.3, §10.51); they are separate from the host targets' profit share (§10.62.2). From
the smart engine's first day (§10.62.2, «The switch») a person's pool tasks of the day come from here; before it, §10.41.1.

- **The catalogue.** A task is *an enabled pool template × an amount on the template metric's ladder × a window of the
  day × (one gift / one category)*, code `K.<template>.<subject|*>.<amount>.<from>-<to>`. Ladders: actions 40 steps
  (1 … 1 000), minutes 24 (5 … 480), hearts 25 (10 … 3 000), coin values 75 (100 … 9 000 000), «join a family» 1. Windows:
  the 147 of §10.62.2. The host targets' metrics (`HOST_GIFT_CHERRIES`, `HOST_LUCKY_CHERRIES`) are never Task Center
  tasks. **115 983 tasks** from the default templates with no gifts; + 5 880 per paid gift and 5 880 per category (257 103
  with 20 gifts).
- **New measurable actions (templates seeded by migration `20270315090100_host_target_engine`).** `P_SEND_GIFT_OF`
  (`GIFT_COUNT_SENT`: how many of ONE gift were sent, paid, to other ACTIVE people), `P_SEND_CATEGORY`
  (`CATEGORY_GIFTS_SENT`), `P_GIFT_HOSTS` (`GIFTED_HOSTS`: different ACTIVE people gifted), `P_FAMILY_JOIN`
  (`FAMILY_JOIN`: joined or founded a family in the window and still in it), `P_FAMILY_CHAT`
  (`FAMILY_CHAT_MESSAGES`), and for hosts `P_PK_BATTLES` (`PK_BATTLES`: battles started, never the void ones) and
  `P_PK_WINS` (`PK_WINS`). Left out as before: anything the server cannot see (sharing, recharging, app-reported events).
  A chosen gift's and a category's band target is a COIN VALUE: the count is that value in the gift's price (the
  category's cheapest).
- **The assignment.** At the person's first read of the day, deterministic for the person and the day:
  1. **Read:** their 7-day daily average of every offered metric (the same stored-data queries as the progress); tasks
     assigned and claimed in the last 7 days; the variants of the last `task_no_repeat_days` (default 3) and yesterday's
     templates; whether they are in a family; the gifts they sent most (30 days); the hours they join lives (30 days);
     their level band and whether they host.
  2. **Weigh:** what they already do weighs more (1 + 2 × min(1, average / the band's target)); a template given yesterday
     × 0.4; «join a family» only outside a family, the family chat only inside one; gift tasks only with gifts. A seeded
     weighted order.
  3. **Select** as §10.41.1: hosts get their band's host tasks first, then at most one per group, then two, up to the
     band's daily count; never one template twice.
  4. **Amount:** their average × the completion factor (0.7 when they never finish … 1.3 when they always do; 1 with fewer
     than 5 tasks), or the band's target when they never do it, kept within ½ … 3 × the band's target and snapped up to the
     ladder; a gift task names their favourite gift (else a paid gift at random); one WATCH / LIVE task may take their
     usual 3 hours (≥ 60 % of their joins) with half the amount.
  5. **No repeat:** a variant of the last `task_no_repeat_days` moves one ladder step up.
  6. **Reward (unchanged rules):** a coin-valued task pays the template's rate per coin (0.1 cherry a coin for gifts,
     D188) — never more than twice the band's reward; any other task the band's reward × amount / target, within ½ … 2 ×
     (free actions stay symbolic). The daily cap (50 000) and the monthly cap ($5) apply at the claim as before.
  7. Stored in `task_assignments` (+ `variant`, `subject`, `window_from` / `window_to`, `name_ar` / `name_en`, `reason`).
- **Progress and claims** count only the window of a windowed task and only the named gift / category.
- **Contract (additive).** `ProgramTask.gift` (`TaskGift`, a chosen-gift task's picture and name, else null),
  `ProgramTask.window` (`HH:MM`, else null); `name` states the gift, category or window; metrics `GIFT_COUNT_SENT`,
  `CATEGORY_GIFTS_SENT`, `GIFTED_HOSTS`, `FAMILY_JOIN`, `FAMILY_CHAT_MESSAGES`, `PK_BATTLES`, `PK_WINS` (an older app shows
  an unknown metric with the generic icon). The panel's knob `taskNoRepeatDays` and the catalogue's task counts
  (§10.62.2).

### 10.42 Editing the own profile *(v1.45-social, DRAFT — D168)*

Owner request (2026-10-29, from the phone): «فعّل الأزرار المتبقية في تعديل الملف وتغيير الصورة» —
make the remaining controls of «تعديل الملف الشخصي» work, the photo included. Built only where no new
owner business rule is needed (CP-001's name and bio rules, the media pipeline of §11.1); links, gender,
account category, the grid order and the private-account switch stay "Soon" with questions to the owner
(D168).

- **Name and bio:** `PATCH /me` takes `displayName` and/or `bio` besides `locale` and `country` (at least
  one of the four; `{}` → 400 `body` / `required`).
  - `displayName`: exactly the registration rules of §6 (NFC, trimmed, 1–50 graphemes, ≤ 100 code
    points, text hygiene, joiners, zalgo, mixed scripts; `too_short`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`), and
    the configured reserved terms → 400 `displayName` / `reserved_term`. Display names are not unique.
  - `bio`: CRLF → LF, NFC, trimmed, each line loses its trailing spaces, blank lines at either end go;
    then at most **300 code points** and **4 line breaks** (`too_long`), each line under the free-text
    hygiene of §6 (`invalid_format`). An empty result or `null` clears it (`Me.bio` and
    `PublicProfile.bio` null). Raw input over 1 200 code points → `too_long` before any work.
  - The response is the updated `Me`. A change of name or bio is audited `user.profile.update`
    (metadata: which fields changed, never their values). Profiles, follow lists, rooms, comments and
    messages show the new name from their next read; nothing stored elsewhere is rewritten (live chat
    lines already sent keep the name they were sent with).
- **The profile photo:** the app uploads the photo as an **`AVATAR`** asset (§11.1: a centre-cropped
  square, `640.webp` and `320.webp`, metadata stripped; the app may crop it square first), then
  `PUT /me/avatar {mediaId}` → 200 `{avatarUrl}`. Order after auth and the rate limit:
  `MEDIA_UPLOADS_ENABLED` off → 503 `MEDIA_UPLOADS_UNAVAILABLE` → body (strict; `mediaId` a UUID, else
  400 `mediaId` / `invalid_value`) → the asset: a READY, unattached `AVATAR` of the caller from the last
  24 hours, else 400 `mediaId` / `invalid_value`. The previous `AVATAR` asset is deleted with its objects
  (after commit); a photo that was not an asset (none today) is simply replaced. Setting the current
  photo again changes nothing. Audited `user.avatar.update` (`set` / `removed`).
- `DELETE /me/avatar` → 204: `avatarUrl` null (the app shows the initial), the asset deleted;
  idempotent; works while uploads are off.
- `avatarUrl` (the 640 px WebP) is what `Me`, `PublicProfile` and every `UserSummary` already carry: the
  new photo shows everywhere from the next read. It is visible to everyone at once, like stories (D91)
  and posts (D162a); safety relies on reports of the user and moderators.
- **Rate limits:** `PATCH /me` keeps 30 / hour per user; `PUT` and `DELETE /me/avatar` share 30 / hour per
  user (§7).
- **Not in v1.45-social** (owner questions, D168): profile links, gender, account category, reordering
  the profile grid, the private-account switch (no follow requests yet, §10.5), a cover photo, a
  birthday. *(v1.47-social, D175: links, gender, category and the private account with follow
  requests are §10.47; the grid order stays as it is — pinning 3 posts is enough (owner).)* The username keeps its own endpoint (`PUT /me/username`, §10.32); the country stays in
  settings (§10.28).

### 10.43 Levels never go down *(v1.46-levels, DRAFT — owner D169, 2026-10-30)*

*(owner)* In all four level categories (CP-005) a level **never goes down**, with one exception:

- **The kept level** is `user_level_states.current_level` itself: every write sets it to the
  higher of the level kept so far and the level the points reach — after earning, after a
  reversal or a refund (any `LevelReversalPolicy`), after an admin deduction, after a rebuild and
  after a new version is published (`PRESERVE_POINTS` or `RECOMPUTE_FROM_LEDGER`: points as they
  are, the level `max(old, new ladder)`). No second "peak" column: the stored level is the floor.
- **Progress** counts from the kept level's threshold: while the points are below it,
  `progressPercent` is 0 and `pointsToNext` is the honest distance to the next level.
- **The exception — fraud:** an admin adjustment (`POST /admin/levels/users/{userId}/adjustments`)
  with `fraud: true` and a negative `pointsDelta` (else 400, issue `fraud_needs_deduction`) lowers
  the level to what the remaining points reach; history reason `FRAUD`; audited (`fraud` in the
  metadata); stored on the ledger row (`points_ledger.fraud`, CHECK: negative ADJUSTMENT only), so
  a replay of the same `Idempotency-Key` with a different flag is 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.
  Gift reversals and refunds are never fraud by themselves.
- **Frames** (§10.22) are permanent; a fraud demotion is the only way one is removed: the
  `LEVEL_REWARD` frames of the support tiers lost are deleted (a worn one leaves nothing worn).
### 10.44 A live in the background; the host away «سيعود المضيف قريباً» *(v1.42-live, DRAFT — D170)*

Owner (2026-10-29): in an audio or video live, a viewer, a guest on a seat and the host who put the
app in the background (another app in front) stay in the live: the sound goes on, a person on the
mic is still heard, and nothing leaves the room. In a **video** live the host's camera stops in the
background (the phones do not allow it), viewers see «سيعود المضيف قريباً», and a video live that
stays like that for more than 5 minutes is closed.

- **Nothing leaves on background.** The apps keep the media session (Android: a foreground service
  of type `microphone|mediaPlayback` with an ongoing notification — tap to return, End live / Leave;
  iOS: `UIBackgroundModes` `audio`). Leaving happens only when the person leaves, the app is killed
  (the host's heartbeats stop: `HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT`, §10.2, unchanged) or the server ends the room.
- **The host away** (`setLiveHostPresence`, `POST /live/rooms/{roomId}/host-presence`
  `{away: boolean}`, 204): the host's app sends `away: true` when it goes to the background in a
  video room (after muting its camera track) and `away: false` when it returns (after unmuting).
  In a `SOLO` or `MULTI` room the server keeps `host_away_since` — set once (a repeat keeps the first
  time, so the time is **continuous**) and cleared by `away: false`. An `AUDIO` room stores nothing
  (the host keeps talking; no away state, no auto close). A failed report is sent again with the
  next heartbeat. Checks as the heartbeat: 503 hosting off; 404 not the host / no such room / bad id;
  400 a body other than `{away: boolean}`; 409 `LIVE_ROOM_ENDED` (a stale room is ended as
  `HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` first).
- **The away limit:** `LIVE_HOST_AWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default **300**, 30–86400). The live
  sweeper (every `LIVE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, after the stale-room run) ends every fresh LIVE
  video room away for at least that long with `endReason = HOST_AWAY_TIMEOUT` and `endedAt =
  host_away_since + limit`, in bounded batches (`SKIP LOCKED`, the `status = 'LIVE'` guard: each
  room once), audited `live.room.end` with `{reason: HOST_AWAY_TIMEOUT, hostUserId}`; seats, medals
  and statistics as every end (`roomsEndedIn`); the media session is closed by the media
  reconciliation, as for a timeout. The host's next heartbeat or presence call gets 409 and the app
  shows the ended live.
- **What viewers see** comes from the media session, not from the API: the host's camera track is
  muted while away, so the app shows «سيعود المضيف قريباً» (the same state as a host not in the
  session) instead of a black or frozen picture, and the video again when it is unmuted.
- **Why an app call, not a media webhook:** muting a track sends no LiveKit webhook, and a killed
  app is already covered by the heartbeat rule (45 s); `track_unpublished` would only repeat that.
- **Older apps** show `HOST_AWAY_TIMEOUT` as a generic «انتهى البث» (unknown reasons map to it).
- **Not in v1.42-live:** an away state in `LiveRoom` responses, a warning to the host before the
  close, an away rule for audio rooms or for seated guests.
### 10.45 The bag v2: expiry, gifts and sending *(v1.48-social, DRAFT — D171)*

Owner request (2026-10-29, Arabic, D171): «الحقيبة تعرض العنصر الذي تم شراؤه أو استلامه كهدية — من التطبيق
أو من مستخدم آخر — ولا تعرض العناصر الأخرى. زر «ارتداء» يصبح «إزالة» … وبجانبه «إرسال» … وكل عنصر يظهر الوقت
المتبقي لاختفائه من الحقيبة»; amendment «يمكن أن تجزّئ المدة» (send part of the remaining time). Owner
points are marked *(owner)*; the rest are CTO defaults the owner may change.

- **Only owned items** *(owner)*: `GET /me/bag` lists what the caller owns now — never an expired item.
  Items the caller does not own are not shown by the app (the catalogue route stays for later use; no
  store exists, so nothing is sold yet and no `PURCHASE` source exists).
- **Expiry** *(owner: «الوقت المتبقي»)*: each owned item has `expiresAt` (`null` = permanent). The
  server computes it; the app counts down from it. An item whose `expiresAt` has passed is gone: no read
  returns it, it cannot be worn or sent, `PublicProfile.profileCard` no longer shows it (so expiry takes
  it off), and a sweeper deletes the rows (every `BAG_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, default 300). Items given
  before v1.48 (free, backfill, admin) are permanent.
- **Sources** (`BagItemSource`): `FREE_SIGNUP`, `BACKFILL`, `ADMIN` (the app shows «هدية من Kabso»),
  `GIFT` (*new*: sent by another user; `giftedBy` is that user's `UserSummary`, or null when the account
  is no longer ACTIVE or a block stands between them either way). When time is **added** to an item one
  already owns (a gift or an admin grant), the row's `source` / `giftedBy` become the latest giver's;
  `acquiredAt` stays.
- **Wearing** is unchanged (§10.22): one item per category; an expired one is not owned (409
  `BAG_ITEM_NOT_OWNED`).
- **Sending** *(owner)*: `POST /me/bag/transfers {code, username, days?}` → 201 `BagTransfer {id, code,
  category, name, recipient, whole, durationSeconds, remaining}`.
  - `days` absent or null = **the whole item** *(owner: «الكل»)*: it leaves the caller's bag (taken off
    if worn) and the recipient receives its **remaining time** (exactly, to the second) or, if it was
    permanent, a permanent item. `remaining` is null.
  - `days` = 1 … 3650 = **part of the time** *(owner amendment)*: the caller keeps the item (still worn
    if it was) with `expiresAt` moved back by `days × 24 h`; the recipient receives `days × 24 h`.
    `days × 24 h` must be **less than** the remaining time (409 `BAG_SEND_EXCEEDS_REMAINING`; send the
    whole item instead). A **permanent item is sent whole only** (409 `BAG_SEND_PERMANENT_WHOLE_ONLY`):
    sending days out of a permanent item would mint unlimited time. `remaining` is the caller's item
    after the send (`BagItem`).
  - **Stacking** *(owner amendment)*: if the recipient already owns the item, the time is **added** to
    it (from its `expiresAt`, never from before now); a whole permanent item makes theirs permanent; if
    theirs is already permanent → 409 `BAG_RECIPIENT_HAS_PERMANENT` (the time would be lost). Otherwise
    the recipient gets a new item, not worn, counting from now. What the recipient wears never changes.
  - **Not transferable** (`BagItem.transferable: false`; 409 `BAG_ITEM_NOT_TRANSFERABLE`): **free** items
    (catalogue `free`, given to every account) and **level rewards** (source `LEVEL_REWARD`, D169's
    support-tier frames, earned by one's own level). The app says why from
    the `source`.
  - **New categories and sources** (e.g. D169's `AVATAR_FRAME`, `LEVEL_REWARD`) need nothing here:
    their items are listed, worn and (unless above) sent like any other.
  - Refusals, after auth, rate limit and 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` (strict body; `username` 1–30, `code`
    1–40, `days` an integer 1–3650 or null): 404 `NOT_FOUND` — no ACTIVE account with that username, or a
    block either way (the same answer, like CP requests); 400 `username` / `invalid_value` — oneself; 409
    `BAG_ITEM_NOT_OWNED` — not owned (or expired, or unknown); then the 409s above. Nothing changes on any
    refusal.
  - **Atomic and serialized:** one transaction locks the pair of users, then the two holders of the item
    in a fixed order, so concurrent sends never give away more than the caller has. The recipient's
    `BAG_ITEM_RECEIVED` notification (§11.10) and a `bag_transfers` ledger row (sender, recipient, item,
    `whole`, `duration_ms` — null for a permanent item — and both `expires_at` after) are in the same
    transaction. No coins move.
- **Admin grants**: `bag-admin grant <email> <code> [<days>|forever]` (default `forever`, as before):
  a new item, or time added to an owned one (`forever` makes it permanent; an item already permanent is
  left as it is). Audited `bag.grant` with `days` (null = forever).
- **Rate limit** (§7): sends 30 / hour per user (`bag:send`).
- **Not in v1.48-social:** a store or purchases, other categories (entrance effects, chat bubbles — none
  exist in the catalogue or the app; avatar frames came with v1.46-levels, D169), refunds or taking a sent item back, hiding the
  sender's name on a gift.

### 10.46 The cherry economy, phase 1: cherry balances, host agencies, commissions and withdrawals *(v1.52-social, DRAFT — D179, CP-027)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-30, chat, Arabic; `ECONOMY_spec`) are marked *(owner)*. Every rate and threshold
is server config with the owner's value as default; the owner changes it without an app release.

- **Two different "cherry" numbers.** (1) The **cherry balance** «رصيد الكرز» defined here: the host currency
  *(owner: 1 coin = 10 cherries)*, credited per gift, withdrawable. (2) The **in-room cherry score** of the
  live (the room chip, the host pill, the rankings, seat points; 100 points per counted coin, §10.10, D134):
  a popularity measure, **not** money and **not** this balance. The two are never added or converted.
- **The cherry ledger** (tables `cherry_wallets`, `cherry_ledger`): append-only; every change is a ledger row
  `{user, delta (signed, never 0), balanceAfter, reason, reference}` written with the balance in one
  transaction; `(user, reason, reference)` is unique. Reasons: `GIFT_RECEIVED`, `AGENCY_COMMISSION`,
  `PARENT_COMMISSION`, `WITHDRAWAL_REFUND` (credits); `GIFT_REVERSAL`, `AGENCY_COMMISSION_REVERSAL`,
  `PARENT_COMMISSION_REVERSAL`, `WITHDRAWAL_HOLD` (debits); clients show an unknown reason as a generic change.
- **Instant credit per gift** *(owner)*: in the gift send's own transaction (live sends, §10.23 / §10.27 /
  §10.33, and direct-conversation sends, §11.13), each recipient gets floor(recipient coins × the send's stored
  `host_share_bps` × `CHERRIES_PER_COIN` (10) / 10 000) cherries (`GIFT_RECEIVED`, reference: the send). With
  the stored shares: a normal gift 65 % (100 coins → 650 cherries), lucky 10 % (→ 100), a paid quip 50 % (→ 500),
  a gift in a conversation 50 % (→ 500; lucky there 10 % → 100); 1 coin at 65 % → 6 (6.5 rounded down). A free
  quip credits nothing. A replayed send (`clientId`) never credits again. Gifts sent from the **bag** credit
  like coin gifts (the D164 earnings counted them; **owner question**). The cherries are **on top of** nothing:
  they are the recipient's share; commissions below are paid by the company on top of it *(owner)*.
- **History before v1.52** (the choice): the gifts received before this release were **backfilled once** by the
  migration `20261231090000_cherry_economy` — one `GIFT_RECEIVED` row per (send, recipient) with the same
  arithmetic, at the send's time, and the balances — so the history and the balance are continuous and come
  from one source (the alternative, a ledger that starts at the cutover, would hide earnings the D164 screen
  already showed). No commission is backfilled (no agency existed). D164's computed earnings
  (`getMyEarnings`, `listMyEarnings`, §10.40) stay for older apps, **deprecated**: they are coin values
  (×1), the ledger is the source of truth (×10, reversals included).
- **Host agencies** «وكالة المضيفين» (tables `agencies`, `agency_hosts`, `agency_complaints`):
  - An agency is created for its owner, the **host agent**, by the team (`economy-admin agency-create <email>
    [--parent <code>]`); it has an **invite code** (8 characters `A–Z 2–9` without `0 O 1 I`, matched without
    case). `--parent` / `agency-parent` links it to the **agency admin** (parent agency) that activated it.
  - **Joining** *(owner)*: the host types the code, sees the agency (`getAgencyByCode`) and accepts
    (`joinAgency`): the link is ACTIVE at once. One agency per host; an agency owner is never a host (409
    `AGENCY_JOIN_NOT_ALLOWED`); another agency → 409 `AGENCY_ALREADY_MEMBER`; the same agency again → 200.
  - **Leaving** *(owner)*: within `AGENCY_LEAVE_DAYS` (14) of joining (`leaveAgency`); after that 409
    `AGENCY_LEAVE_WINDOW_CLOSED` and the only way is a **complaint** to the admin (`complainAboutAgency`, one open
    at a time), which the team resolves with `economy-admin complaint-resolve <id> release|keep|move --to <code>`
    (release ends the link, move ends it and links the host to another agency with a new leave window, keep
    rejects the complaint). Every step is audited.
  - **Active host** *(owner)*: live on ≥ `AGENCY_ACTIVE_HOST_MIN_DAYS` (7) days **and** ≥
    `AGENCY_ACTIVE_HOST_MIN_HOURS` (10) hours in the last `AGENCY_ACTIVE_HOST_WINDOW_DAYS` (30) days, from the
    host's own lives in `live_rooms` (start → end, a live in progress to its last heartbeat; a day counts when
    it has live time in `LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE`); an account that is not ACTIVE is never an active host.
  - **Ranks** (`AgencyRank`): `AGENT` *(owner)* — ≥ `AGENCY_RANK_MIN_ACTIVE_HOSTS` (5) active hosts, **or** the
    owner's exception: its hosts earned ≥ `AGENCY_RANK_EXCEPTION_CHERRIES` (200 000 000) cherries in the month
    (the current or the last calendar month); `ADMIN` *(owner)* — an agent with ≥ `AGENCY_ADMIN_MIN_SUB_AGENCIES`
    (3) sub-agencies that each qualify as an agent **by the same test** (5 active hosts or the 200M exception —
    our reading of "each with at least 5 active hosts"; **owner to confirm**); `LAPSED` — did not qualify at the
    last month start; `NEW` — created and not evaluated yet: its **grace** (CTO default) lasts until the month
    start two months after its creation month (an agency needs time to recruit before it can have 5 active
    hosts); a NEW agency earns commission.
  - **Evaluation** *(owner: re-evaluated at the start of each month, rank kept until the month's end)*: the
    sweeper (`AGENCY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 3 600; `economy-admin agency-evaluate` does the same) re-evaluates
