    every agency past its grace at its first run in a new month (`LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE`): the rank becomes what
    it qualifies for, up or down, and is kept to the month's end. Other runs only **promote** (an agency that
    reaches 5 active hosts mid-month becomes AGENT at once; a rank is never lowered mid-month).
  - **Lapsed** *(owner: "no commission on hosts who join after that, existing hosts stay linked")*: each link
    stores `commission_eligible` = the agency was not LAPSED when the host joined. A LAPSED agency keeps earning on
    its eligible hosts and earns nothing on hosts who joined while lapsed; once it qualifies again it earns on all.
- **Commissions, credited instantly per gift, paid by the company on top of the host's share** *(owner)*
  (tables `agency_earnings`, one row per (send, linked recipient), and `agency_months`, an agency's month in
  `LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE`): for a recipient who is an ACTIVE host of an agency, in the same transaction,
  - the agency's owner gets floor(host cherries × rate) (`AGENCY_COMMISSION`), rate = `AGENCY_COMMISSION_BPS`
    (15 %) or `AGENCY_COMMISSION_TIER_BPS` (16 %) **in the month after a month in which its hosts earned ≥
    `AGENCY_TIER_MONTHLY_CHERRIES` (1 500 000 000)** cherries *(owner)*;
  - the parent agency's owner gets floor(host cherries × `AGENCY_PARENT_COMMISSION_BPS` (3 %))
    (`PARENT_COMMISSION`) while the parent's rank is ADMIN *(owner: 3 % of each sub-agency's hosts' cherries)*;
  - the host's cherries count for the agency's month (the 16 % tier, the 200M exception) whether or not a
    commission is due. Example *(owner)*: 1 000 000 coins of normal gifts → host 6 500 000 cherries, agency
    975 000 (15 %), parent 195 000 (3 %). Lock order: the agencies' month rows (sorted), then the cherry
    balances (sorted), each in one statement — sends, reversals and withdrawals cannot deadlock.
- **Reversal** (`economy-admin reverse-gift <send id>`; fraud, a refunded payment): mirrors every cherry credit of
  the send — `GIFT_REVERSAL`, `AGENCY_COMMISSION_REVERSAL`, `PARENT_COMMISSION_REVERSAL` — marks its agency rows
  reversed and takes them out of the months' totals, once (a second run changes nothing). A balance may go
  below 0 (cherries already withdrawn): a debt that blocks withdrawals until gifts cover it. The sender's coins,
  points and levels are not touched (no coin refund exists yet).
- **Withdrawals** *(owner: 1 000 000 cherries = $1.10, minimum $10 for hosts and agents)* (table
  `cherry_withdrawals`; no payment provider yet): `requestCherryWithdrawal` (`Idempotency-Key`, `{amountMinor,
  payoutDetails}`) holds ceil(amount × `CHERRY_PAYOUT_RATE` cherries / minor) cherries (`WITHDRAWAL_HOLD`; $10 =
  9 090 910 cherries); amount ≥ `CHERRY_WITHDRAWAL_MIN_MINOR` (1 000) in `CHERRY_PAYOUT_CURRENCY` (USD); one
  pending request at a time (409 `WITHDRAWAL_PENDING`); 409 `INSUFFICIENT_CHERRIES`. The team pays by hand to
  `payoutDetails` within `CHERRY_WITHDRAWAL_PAYOUT_DAYS` (7, shown to the requester) and marks it
  (`economy-admin withdrawal-pay <id> [--note <reference>]`) or rejects it with a reason
  (`withdrawal-reject <id> --note …`, `WITHDRAWAL_REFUND` gives the cherries back). Request, payment and rejection
  are audited; the requester sees the status (`listMyCherryWithdrawals`, `getMyCherries.pendingWithdrawal`).
  `payoutDetails` is personal data: only its owner and the team see it.
- **Reads:** `getMyCherries` (balance, its value, held, earned all time / 7 / 30 days, commissions, the payout
  rules, the pending request), `listMyCherryLedger` (newest first; a gift row names the gift and the visible
  sender), `getMyAgency` (as a host: the agency, the leave deadline, the latest complaint; as an agent: code, rank,
  this month's rate, progress — active hosts x / 5, the hosts' month cherries vs the exception and the tier,
  qualified sub-agencies x / 3 — commissions this month / last month / total, the parent and the sub-agencies),
  `listMyAgencyHosts` (the agent's hosts: live days and hours in the window, active, this month's cherries).
- **Rate limits:** every route uses the per-user default (§7).
- **Task cherries (v1.53-social, D184, §10.46.1):** `TASK_REWARD` rows are part of the balance and the
  history, but not of `earnedTotal` / the agencies' month totals (no commission on them).
- **Not in phase 1 (next, CP-027 §6):** recharge agents «وكيل الشحن» (`coin0001` usernames, the KYC application
  with selfie review, employees and their hours, availability and payment methods), an agent's cherry → coin
  conversion *(owner: 93 220 coins per 1 000 000 cherries — 94 500 since D308 —, two-sided confirmation, daily cap)*, coin selling
  prices and website payments (B5), an admin UI (CLI only), automatic payouts.

#### 10.46.1 Task cherries locked for withdrawal *(v1.53-social, DRAFT — D184)*

Owner decision (2026-10-30, via the coordinator, **confirmed**): task cherries (§10.41.3) become withdrawable
once the person's lifetime received support — the gift cherries received since registration — is worth at
least **$50**. The rule is one function and one setting:

- **Locked amount:** while the rule has not passed, every `TASK_REWARD` cherry ever credited is locked
  (`lockedTaskCherries` = their sum); once it passes, 0. `withdrawableCherries` = `cherries` −
  `lockedTaskCherries`, never below 0. Task cherries are not tracked as a separate balance: the ledger's
  `TASK_REWARD` rows are the record.
- **The rule (`taskCherryLock` in `economy-math.ts`):** lifetime gift cherries received (`GIFT_RECEIVED`;
  an admin reversal, `GIFT_REVERSAL`, is subtracted) worth at least `TASK_CHERRIES_UNLOCK_GIFT_MINOR`
  (default 5000 = $50) minor units of `CHERRY_PAYOUT_CURRENCY` at `CHERRY_PAYOUT_RATE` (owner rate:
  ≈ 45 454 546 cherries); `0` = never locked. A reversal can lock them again. Commissions and task cherries do
  not count. The wire: `taskUnlock.unlocked`, `giftValueMinor`, `thresholdMinor`.
- **Withdrawal:** `requestCherryWithdrawal` holds only from the withdrawable part: the conditional update
  is `cherries − locked ≥ held` (the lock computed in the same transaction); otherwise 409
  `INSUFFICIENT_CHERRIES`, nothing held.
- **Wire:** `CherryWallet.taskRewardTotal`, `lockedTaskCherries`, `withdrawableCherries`, `taskUnlock`. The
  app shows the locked cherries with «تُفتح للسحب بعد تحقيق شرط الأرباح» (wording may change) and offers
  only `withdrawableCherries`.
- *(v1.57-social, D188, owner: «لمن يكون قيمة ما حصل عليه من دعم لا يقل عن 60 دولار»)* The threshold is
  **$60**: `TASK_CHERRIES_UNLOCK_GIFT_MINOR` default 6000 (≈ 54 545 455 gift cherries at the owner rate),
  replacing the $50. Same rule and wire; the app's locked line shows no amount (unchanged).

### 10.47 Profile fields, private accounts and follow requests *(v1.47-social, DRAFT — D175, CP-025)*

The owner's answers (2026-10-30, Arabic) to D168's questions a–g. Written as §10.43; numbered §10.47 at integration (§10.43 is D169's, §10.44 D170's,
§10.45 D171's, §10.46 D179's).

- **Gender** (`Gender`): `MALE`, `FEMALE`, `UNDISCLOSED` («ذكر / أنثى / أفضّل عدم الذكر»).
  - **Required at sign-up** (`RegisterRequest.gender`; missing → 400 `gender` / `required`, another value
    → `invalid_value`); kept on the pending registration and copied to the account at verify. Accounts
    made before v1.47 (and pending rows made before) have none (`Me.gender` null) until they choose.
  - `PATCH /me {gender}` changes it; it cannot be cleared (`UNDISCLOSED` is the "rather not say").
  - **Private by default** (owner): `showGender` (default false) decides whether others see it;
    `PublicProfile.gender` is `MALE` / `FEMALE` only when shown, else null (`UNDISCLOSED` shows nothing).
    `Me` always carries the caller's own value.
- **Account category** (`AccountCategory`, shown under the name): `SINGER` مغنٍّ, `MUSICIAN` موسيقي, `POET`
  شاعر, `PRESENTER` مقدّم برامج, `GAMER` لاعب ألعاب, `CONTENT_CREATOR` صانع محتوى, `ATHLETE` رياضي, `ARTIST`
  فنان, `BLOGGER` مدوّن, `PUBLIC_FIGURE` شخصية عامة, `OTHER` أخرى. Optional; `PATCH /me {category: null}`
  clears it. The app names the values in its own language; clients show an unknown value as nothing.
- **Profile links:** `PATCH /me {links}` replaces the whole set (0–3, in order; `[]` clears them).
  - Each `url` (raw ≤ 2 048 characters): `https://` only; no user name or password; no port (`:443` is
    the default and disappears); a host name — never an IP literal (any IPv4 spelling, e.g. `2130706433` or
    `0x7f.1`, or IPv6), `localhost` or a single label; letters, digits and `-` per label and an alphabetic or
    `xn--` last label; no spaces, controls, bidi or zero-width characters anywhere (`invalid_format`).
    Stored normalised: the WHATWG serialisation (lower-case punycode host, percent-encoding) without the
    fragment, at most **500** characters (`too_long`).
  - `label`: optional, one line, NFC, trimmed, ≤ 30 code points, §6 hygiene (`too_long`,
    `invalid_format`); empty → none.
  - More than 3 → `links` / `too_many`; the same normalised link twice → `links.<i>.url` / `invalid_value`.
  - `ProfileLink.platform` comes from the host: `INSTAGRAM` (instagram.com), `TIKTOK` (tiktok.com),
    `YOUTUBE` (youtube.com, youtu.be), `FACEBOOK` (facebook.com, fb.com), `X` (x.com, twitter.com) — the
    domain itself or any subdomain (`www.`, `m.`, …); anything else is `OTHER`. The app opens a known
    platform directly and shows a warning sheet «أنت تغادر Kabso» with the **full URL** before opening any
    `OTHER` link (owner).
  - Links are on the profile of private accounts too (the profile is public, §10.5).
  - **Reports:** `POST /reports {targetType: PROFILE_LINK, targetId: <ProfileLink.id>}` — a link on the
    profile of an ACTIVE user with no block either way, not the reporter's own (400 `targetId` /
    `invalid_value`); else 404. The report keeps a snapshot (`linkSnapshot`: username, url, label; admin
    views) because the owner may edit the link away; one OPEN report per reporter and link. Admin
    `REMOVE_TARGET` deletes the link from the profile (if it is still there).
  - A change of `gender`, `showGender`, `category` or `links` is audited `user.profile.update` with the
    field names only (§10.42).
- **Private account** (`PATCH /me/privacy {isPrivate}`, `PrivacySettings.isPrivate`, `Me.isPrivate`):
  - Posts, reels and stories of a private account are visible only to the account and its followers,
    **on every endpoint** (the §11.2 / §11.9 visibility rule, already enforced server-side since v1.5 and
    audited again for D175): the user's grid and reposts, `GET /posts/{id}` (and its comments, likes,
    like / comment / repost / share / save / report), the stories of the user, `GET /stories/{id}`,
    seen, the story tray, every feed (posts and reels, following and trending), search (posts **and,
    v1.47-social, hashtags**: a tag used only by posts the caller may not see is not listed), hashtag
    pages and counts, trending hashtags, saved posts, notifications pointing at such content, views (ignored).
    Anyone else gets the usual **404** (never 403); the app shows «هذا الحساب خاص» from `PublicProfile`
    (`isPrivate` and not `isFollowing`).
  - The profile (name, photo, bio, category, links, counts) stays public; follower / following **counts**
    stay visible; the lists stay followers-only (403, §10.6); **lives stay public** (§10.5).
  - Existing followers are kept when the account turns private.
  - Switching **private → public accepts every pending request** (each requester follows the account; the
    requests and their notifications go; requesters are not notified one by one). Audited
    `user.privacy.private` (`{isPrivate, requestsAccepted}`) when it changes; the switch locks the account
    like a follow does, so no follow request races it.
- **Follow requests:**
  - `PUT /users/{username}/follow` on a private account the caller does not follow creates a request (one
    per pair; repeating changes nothing) → 200 `{isFollowing: false, isRequested: true, followerCount}`,
    and the owner gets a `FOLLOW_REQUEST` notification (actor the requester, target `USER`; the `follows`
    setting). `PublicProfile.followRequested` and `FollowListItem.requestedByMe` show it.
  - `DELETE /users/{username}/follow` cancels it (the notification is withdrawn).
  - `GET /me/follow-requests`: newest first, keyset cursor bound to the caller, `limit` 1–50 (default 20),
    `total`; only ACTIVE requesters with no block either way.
  - `POST /me/follow-requests/{username}/accept` → 200 `{followsMe: true, followerCount}`: the follow is
    created, the request and its notification go, the requester gets `FOLLOW_REQUEST_ACCEPTED` (actor the
    owner). Already a follower → 200. No pending request → 409 `FOLLOW_REQUEST_NOT_PENDING`.
  - `POST /me/follow-requests/{username}/decline` → 204: deleted; the requester is not told and may ask
    again; idempotent.
  - Both: `username` malformed, unknown, suspended or deleted → 404; the caller's own → 400 `username` /
    `invalid_value`; 300 / hour per user, one bucket (§7).
  - A block deletes the requests both ways (and their notifications); deleting an account deletes its
    requests; removing a follower (`DELETE /me/followers/{username}`) lets them ask again.
- **Grid order:** unchanged — pinning up to 3 posts (§11.2) is enough (owner). The app's Edit profile
  shows the pin hint instead of a «قريباً» row.
- **CP frame on other people's profiles:** kept (owner; D112 / §10.24 unchanged).
- **Profile photos:** stay visible at once with reports (D91 / D168, owner). A moderator removes a
  violating photo with the server CLI `profile-admin remove-avatar <username> --reason <text>` (migration
  role, like the other admin CLIs): the profile goes back to the initial, the `AVATAR` asset row is
  deleted with the change and its files afterwards (the keys are printed when the CLI has no S3 settings),
  the user gets an `AVATAR_REMOVED` notification (system, no actor, no target; always on) and
  `admin.avatar.remove` is audited with the reason.

### 10.48 Recharge agents «وكلاء الشحن» — economy phase 2 *(v1.54-social, DRAFT — D185, CP-028)*

The owner's decisions of 2026-10-30 (CP-027 §6, CP-028). A recharge agent buys coins from the company
outside the app, keeps them as a **coin stock** and sells them to users, who pay the agent outside the app.
No payment gateway exists (B5): every payment in this section happens outside the app and is recorded by
people.

**Lifecycle.** `PENDING` (application) → `APPROVED` (by the team, waiting for the first top-up) or `REJECTED`
(with a reason; the person may apply again) → `ACTIVE` (the first top-up) ⇄ `SUSPENDED` (the team). Only the
`recharge-admin` CLI decides, tops up, suspends, reinstates and sets caps; every action writes an audit row in
its transaction. A user is at most one of: an applicant / agent, or an agent's employee.

**Application** (`applyForRechargeAgent`, «كن وكيل شحن»): the full four-part name (≥ 4 words), a phone
number in E.164 that has WhatsApp, a **photo of the agent** and a **face-confirmation selfie** (reviewed by a
person; no third-party liveness provider), selling locations (ISO country + 1–20 cities each) and payment
methods per country (a type and free text). The two pictures are uploaded with `createMediaUpload`
(`RECHARGE_AGENT_PHOTO`, `RECHARGE_AGENT_SELFIE`) and **never completed** (`completeMediaUpload` answers 404 for
these kinds): the application consumes the uploads — the image is checked and re-encoded like any image
(metadata stripped) and stored under `private/recharge-agents/<application id>/` with `Cache-Control:
private, no-store`, a prefix that is never public (§11.1: only `media/` is), and the raw upload is deleted.
No URL is ever returned for them.
- **Privacy:** the application data is read only by admins through `recharge-admin view <id>` (the CLI can save
  the two pictures to a local folder); every view writes `recharge.application.view`. The applicant gets back
  only the status, dates and a rejection reason (`RechargeApplicationState`). Logs never contain the fields.
- **Retention:** the pictures and the personal fields of a REJECTED application are deleted
  `RECHARGE_AGENT_KYC_RETENTION_DAYS` (90) after the decision, and those of any application whose account is
  deleted, by the module's sweeper (`RECHARGE_AGENT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 3600; `recharge-admin purge` runs
  the same step); the row keeps the status, dates and `purged_at`. An approved agent's application is kept
  while the agent exists (disputes, the law).

**Activation and top-ups** (`recharge-admin topup <agent> <coins> --paid <USD>`): the team records each
wholesale top-up paid outside the app — the coins, the owner's **price tier** and the USD paid:
`< 100 000 000` coins $12.15 per 1 000 000; `100 000 000 – 299 999 999` $12.10; `≥ 300 000 000` $12.00
(`RECHARGE_AGENT_PRICE_TIERS`, default `0:1215,100000000:1210,300000000:1200`; owner 2026-11-07, D306 — was
$12.00 / $11.95 / $11.90; a top-up already recorded keeps the tier and price stored with it); a USD amount different from the tier's price needs `--note`. The tier, price
per million, expected and paid amounts are stored with the top-up (`recharge_topups`). The **first** top-up
must be ≥ `RECHARGE_AGENT_ACTIVATION_MIN_COINS` (30 000 000 = $364.50 at $12.15) and activates the agent in the same
transaction: the agent gets the next **code** `coin0001`, `coin0002`, … from a counter row updated in that
transaction (sequential, never reused, never changed; beyond 9999 the number simply grows; a number whose
name an older account already uses — made before `coin` + digits was reserved — is skipped, the only gap). The
code is the agent's **recharge ID** in the directory, the entrance bar and the person card, and — owner
decision, same day, reversing CP-028 Q1 — it **becomes the agent's `@username`** (a special username, locked,
§10.48.1). The frame's plate shows the agent's display name.

**Stock and selling** (`sellRechargeCoins`): the stock changes only with a `recharge_stock_ledger` row
(`TOPUP`, `SALE`, `CHERRY_PURCHASE`); a CHECK keeps it ≥ 0 and amounts are integers. A sale — by the agent, or
by an employee during their hours — is one transaction: a conditional `UPDATE` of the stock (`stock ≥ coins`;
the row lock serializes concurrent sales), the stock ledger row, `recharge_sales` (unique per seller and
`Idempotency-Key`), the buyer's `wallet_ledger` `RECHARGE_PURCHASE` (`creditIn`), the audit row
`recharge.sale` and the buyer's `RECHARGE_COINS_RECEIVED` notification (actor the seller; target
`RECHARGE_SALE`: the sale and its coins). The buyer is a username or a user id; not the seller or the agent;
404 when unknown, inactive or blocked either way with the seller or the agent.

**Employees:** the agent adds existing users (not themselves, not an agent or applicant, not another agent's
employee; at most 20) with a weekly schedule (`WeeklySlot`: ISO days, `HH:MM` start inclusive, end exclusive,
`24:00` allowed; a night shift is two slots) in an IANA time zone, changes it or removes them (they stop at
once). An employee sells from the agent's stock only while «now», in their zone, is inside a slot (409
`RECHARGE_OFF_SHIFT`). *(v1.87-social, D287)* Employees also buy hosts' cherries for the agent and receive the
agent's coin orders, within their shift and per permission — §10.100. The agent sees per employee (and for themselves on the dashboard) the sales count and
coins today (LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE), in the last 7 and 30 days.

**Availability and the directory:** the agent sets weekly slots each with a WhatsApp number and a payment
method (public by the agent's choice) in their zone. `listRechargeAgents?country=XX` lists ACTIVE agents with
an active account who sell in the country — those with a slot containing «now» first, then by code — with the
code, the person (`UserSummary`), locations, the payment-method **types** of that country (never the details)
and the WhatsApp number and payment method available now (null when none). The app's «تواصل» opens
`https://wa.me/<digits>` with url_launcher after D175's «أنت تغادر Kabso» sheet (WhatsApp is not one of the
platforms opened directly); no button when nothing is available now.

**Hosts sell cherries to agents** (`createRechargeCherryRequest`, `answerRechargeCherryRequest`): a host sells
withdrawable cherries to an ACTIVE agent, who pays the host cash outside the app at `CHERRY_PAYOUT_RATE`
(owner $1.10 per 1 000 000). Either side creates the request (the host with the agent's code, the agent with the
host's username); the **other side confirms** (or declines; the creator may cancel); it expires after
`RECHARGE_AGENT_CHERRY_REQUEST_TTL_MINUTES` (30) — read as EXPIRED, never confirmable. One open request per host
and agent. Minimum `RECHARGE_AGENT_CHERRY_MIN` 1 000 000 cherries, in steps of `RECHARGE_AGENT_CHERRY_STEP`
100 000; the agent's stock receives floor(cherries × 94 500 / 1 000 000) coins (`RECHARGE_AGENT_CHERRY_RATE`;
*owner 2026-11-08, D308: 94 500, was 93 220*; with the step this is exact: 9 450 coins per 100 000). A conversion
already confirmed keeps the coins it gave (`recharge_cherry_requests.coins` is stored; nothing is recomputed). Confirmation is one transaction: the agent row is locked,
the day's confirmed cherries (LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE) plus this must stay within the agent's **daily cap**
(`RECHARGE_AGENT_CHERRY_DAILY_CAP`; owner follow-up «حد وكيل مفتوح»: **0 = no cap, the default**;
`recharge-admin set-cap <agent> <cherries | 0 | default>` per agent, 0 = none, `default` = the server's), the host's
cherries are debited with a conditional update that never touches the **locked task cherries** (D184,
§10.46.1) — `RECHARGE_SALE` in the cherry ledger — and the stock gets `CHERRY_PURCHASE`; audit
`recharge.cherry.confirm`. The other side gets a `RECHARGE_CHERRY_REQUEST` notification when a request is
created.

**Perks** (owner's Kabso assets: the Kabi mascot art, `apps/mobile/assets/recharge_agent/`, PROVENANCE): while
ACTIVE (and the account is active) the agent has the **agent frame** around their photo with their display name
written in its red plate (fitted, ellipsized; owner, same day), the **badge** beside the name on the profile and on the live person card, and the **entrance
bar** «دخل وكيل الشحن {code}» / "Top-up agent {code} joined" that crosses any live room for about 3.2 s (the
CP entrance's timing, §10.24) when they join — the `join` data message's `user` carries `rechargeAgent: {code}`
(an agent's join is not dropped by the one-line-a-second limit of D96). **Owner addition (same day):** a small
recharge-agent badge (the badge art, 16–18 lp like the level badges) next to the agent's name **everywhere the
name shows in a live room** — chat messages, the join line, the viewers list, seat / guest names, the person
card. It is carried by every `UserSummary` (`UserSummary.rechargeAgent`, present only while ACTIVE with an
active account; the room host's summary too), so it disappears with the other perks on suspension. The perks are derived from the
status, not granted as bag items: they have no expiry, cannot be sent, worn off or removed by the agent, and a
suspension (or the account's suspension or ban) removes all of them at once together with selling and the
listing; reinstating gives them back. `PublicProfile.rechargeAgent` carries the code.

**Admin CLI** `recharge-admin` (migration role, like `economy-admin`): `applications [--status]`, `view <id>
[--save <dir>]` (audited), `approve <id>`, `reject <id> --reason`, `topup <agent> <coins> --paid <USD>
[--note]`, `suspend <agent> --reason`, `reinstate <agent>`, `set-cap <agent> <cherries|default>`, `agents`,
`purge`. `<agent>` is a code, an email or a username. Suspending cancels the agent's open cherry requests.
Audit actions: `recharge.application.submit`, `.view`, `.approve`, `.reject`, `recharge.topup`,
`recharge.activate`, `recharge.suspend`, `recharge.reinstate`, `recharge.cap`, `recharge.sale`,
`recharge.employee.add` / `.update` / `.remove`, `recharge.availability`, `recharge.cherry.request` /
`.confirm` / `.decline` / `.cancel`, `recharge.purge`.

In the panel (§10.54.5 section 3) the same rules run behind capabilities. D275 (owner): the moderator «مشرف» reads the
agents list and the stock top-ups (`recharge.agents`, `recharge.topups.view`) but never tops up, suspends, reinstates
or changes a cap; its only coin movement is a recharge dispute's decision (§10.64.9).

#### 10.48.1 Special usernames «يوزر مميز» *(v1.54-social, DRAFT — D185, owner 2026-10-30)*

A general layer that the recharge agents use first and other sources reuse. A person has at most one **active
special username** (`special_usernames`: `username`, `base_username`, `source` `RECHARGE_AGENT` | `ADMIN_GIFT` |
`PURCHASE` — reserved, nothing sells it yet —, `granted_at`, `expires_at` (null = permanent), `locked`).

- **Shown everywhere:** while it is ACTIVE, `user_profiles.username` *is* the special username, so every payload,
  link, mention, search and room shows only it. The person's own **base username** is kept in the row and is
  visible only to the person (`Me.specialUsername`, own profile and settings) and to the team
  (`username-admin show`); it is **never** in `PublicProfile`, `UserSummary`, search, room payloads, data
  messages or mentions.
- **Locked:** `changeUsername` → 409 `USERNAME_LOCKED`; renting a premium username (§10.32) → 409
  `USERNAME_LOCKED`; a premium grant is refused, and a special username is not given while a premium username
  is rented (the team ends one first).
- **Ending** (expiry by the sweeper, `username-admin revoke`, a recharge agent's suspension): the base username
  is shown again at once; the special one stays **reserved for the person** (GRACE) for
  `SPECIAL_USERNAME_GRACE_DAYS` (30) and is then released — except `coin` + digits, which is never released or
  reused. Given back during the grace period (a gift again, an agent reinstated), the same row is ACTIVE again
  with the then shown username as base. The sweeper runs every `SPECIAL_USERNAME_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (300;
  cannot be 0 in production).
- **Uniqueness both ways** (usernames are canonical lower case, so case-insensitive): a name is unavailable to
  everyone else while it is another account's shown username, a base username behind an ACTIVE special one, a
  special one ACTIVE or in grace, or any `coin` name ever given (partial unique indexes plus the checks of
  `changeUsername`, registration, `username-availability`, premium names and grants). `coin` + digits (also
  with `.` / `_`) is **reserved** (§6): never a regular username, never a gift; only the system gives it.
- **Sign-in** (`login`): by email, the shown username, or the base username while a special one is ACTIVE. A
  special username in grace does not sign in. *(v1.84-live, D302)* A staff ID signs in its current holder (§10.96.12).
- **Old links and mentions:** a profile link, follow or other lookup by the base username (ACTIVE) or by a
  special username in grace leads to the person, and a mention written with one of those names links them; the
  response carries only the username shown now.
- **Recharge agents:** activation grants `coinNNNN` (`RECHARGE_AGENT`, permanent; refused — nothing is charged —
  while the person rents a premium username); suspension ends it (grace without an end); reinstatement gives it
  back. Any earlier gift is replaced (it goes to grace).
- **CLI** `username-admin` (migration role): `gift <user> <special> (--days N | --permanent) --reason`,
  `revoke <user> --reason`, `show <user>` (audited), `sweep`. `<user>` is an email, the shown or the base
  username. Audit actions `special_username.grant`, `special_username.end`, `special_username.view`.
- **Migration** `20270101110000_special_usernames` adds the table only; no existing username changes.

### 10.49 The active-host frame «إطار المضيف» *(v1.55-social, DRAFT — D186, CP-029)*

The owner's decisions of 2026-10-30 (CP-029). A free avatar frame for **active hosts**, worn from the bag
(§10.22, §10.45) like the support frames and taken back when the host is no longer active.

**Who.** An ACTIVE host of an agency (§10.46, `agency_hosts.status = ACTIVE`) with an ACTIVE account who
passes **D179's active-host test** — at least `AGENCY_ACTIVE_HOST_MIN_DAYS` (7) days with live time and at
least `AGENCY_ACTIVE_HOST_MIN_HOURS` (10) hours live in the last `AGENCY_ACTIVE_HOST_WINDOW_DAYS` (30) days,
from the host's own lives (`hostActivity`, the same arithmetic as the agency ranks; days in
`LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE`). A user who goes live without an agency is not an active host.

**Which frame.** Two catalogue items, category `AVATAR_FRAME`: `host_frame_blue` and `host_frame_pink`
(owner art, `apps/mobile/assets/host_frames/`). The gender (§10.47) chooses: MALE → blue, FEMALE → pink. With
no gender or `UNDISCLOSED` the host chooses (`setMyHostFrameStyle`, stored in `host_frame_choices`, any time,
changeable later; the app offers it from the bag); until they choose they own no host frame. A stated gender
always wins over a stored choice.

**The item.** Source `HOST_ACTIVE`, no expiry (`expiresAt` null), `transferable: false` (`sendMyBagItem` →
409 `BAG_ITEM_NOT_TRANSFERABLE`), given **not worn**; the host wears or removes it with `PUT /me/bag/equipped`
(one frame worn at a time with the support frames). At most one `HOST_ACTIVE` item per user. `bag-admin`
refuses to grant or revoke a host frame.

**Sync.** `syncHostFrames` makes each user's `HOST_ACTIVE` item match the rule, one transaction per user
(serialized per user): it is given when the host becomes active, taken back when they are not (a worn one is
taken off: nothing is worn in `AVATAR_FRAME` afterwards), given again when they are active again (not worn),
and swapped for the other colour when the style changes (a gender change in `PATCH /me` or a new choice; worn
stays worn). It runs after the rank evaluation in the agency sweeper (`AGENCY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 3600 by
default) and in `economy-admin agency-evaluate`; for the one host right after `joinAgency` (past live time
counts), `leaveAgency`, `economy-admin complaint-resolve`, a gender change and a style choice. A suspended or
banned account is not active (the next sweep takes the frame back). Audit actions (actor null, target the
user): `host_frame.grant` `{item}`, `host_frame.revoke` `{item, wasWorn, active}`, `host_frame.swap` `{from, to,
worn}`; `host_frame.choice` `{from, to, item}` (actor the host).

**Reads.** `getMyHostFrame` (`HostFrame`): `agencyHost`, `active` (computed at the call, so it may run ahead
of `frame` until the next sweep), `liveDays`, `liveSeconds`, `style`, `styleFrom` (GENDER / CHOICE),
`canChoose`, `frame` (`{code, assetKey, equipped}` or null) and the `rule`. The frame a user wears is public:
`PublicProfile.avatarFrame` (null when none) and `UserSummary.avatarFrame` (present only while one is worn; the
live room's host too), `AvatarFrame {code, assetKey}`. The app draws the frames it has art for around the photo
(the profile, the audio-room seats and the host's seat; no name under the frame) and ignores others. While the
person is an ACTIVE recharge agent, the agent frame (§10.48) is drawn on the profile instead (it carries the
agent code); while they are a host agent, the host-agent frame (§10.52) is. Precedence: recharge-agent frame >
host-agent frame > the worn frame > the CP frame.

### 10.50 Daily recharge badges «شارات الشحن اليومي» *(v1.56-social, DRAFT — D187, CP-030)*

The owner's decisions of 2026-10-30 (CP-030). A person who **receives** many coins from recharges in one day
shows a badge — one of the owner's five pieces of art — next to their name for 24 hours.

**What counts.** Only recharges credited to the person: a recharge agent's (or employee's) sale to them
(§10.48, the buyer's `RECHARGE_PURCHASE`) and, once it exists, a website top-up. Gifts, rewards (tasks, check-in,
lucky wins), admin credits, refunds and transfers never count. Every recharge path calls one function,
`recordRechargeIn` (`recharge/recharge-badges.ts`, source `AGENT_SALE` or `WEBSITE_TOPUP`), inside the
transaction that credits the coins; nothing else writes the two tables. **Recharge agents** (from approval on,
whatever their status) never get the badge — as buyers nothing is counted, as sellers nothing is credited — and
a badge is never shown for a person who has an agent row.

**The day and the tiers.** The day is the calendar day in `RECHARGE_BADGE_TIME_ZONE` (default `Asia/Riyadh`,
UTC+3: a sale at 23:59:59 and one at 00:00:00 Riyadh time are on two days). The day's total gives the tier
(`RECHARGE_BADGE_TIERS`, the minimum of tiers 1–5, default `1000000,10000001,20000001,40000001,70000001`):

| Tier | Coins received in one day (default) | Art |
| ---- | ----------------------------------- | --- |
| 1 | 1 000 000 – 10 000 000 | bronze coin pouch |
| 2 | 10 000 001 – 20 000 000 | silver-blue coin chest |
| 3 | 20 000 001 – 40 000 000 | gold-red coin chest |
| 4 | 40 000 001 – 70 000 000 | purple coin vessel |
| 5 | 70 000 001 and more | royal red crystal vault |

**How long.** When a recharge moves the day's total into a higher tier, the badge becomes that tier with
`until` = that moment + `RECHARGE_BADGE_HOURS` (24); a higher tier the same day replaces it and starts the 24
hours again; more coins within the same tier change nothing. A badge from an earlier day that is still showing
and is **higher** stays until it ends (a lower tier reached the next day does not replace it; an equal or higher
one does). After `until` nothing shows until a new tier is reached.

**Storage (cheap reads).** `recharge_daily_totals` (person, day: coins and the tier reached) is upserted in the
recharge's transaction (its row lock serializes the person's concurrent recharges); `recharge_badges` (one row
per person: `badge_tier`, `badge_until`, `badge_day`, `reached_at`) is read with every `UserSummary` (one
primary-key relation, no aggregation) and with the room host's summary.

**On the wire.** `RechargeBadge {tier, until}` — optional on `UserSummary` and `PublicProfile`, present only
while `until` is in the future. The app shows it next to the name like the level badge — in live rooms (chat
lines, the join line, viewers, seats, the host pill, the person card), on the profile and the Me hub card — and
hides it itself once `until` passes, without a refresh.

### 10.51 Task rewards rebalanced: real-money anchors, a monthly cap, the $60 unlock *(v1.57-social, DRAFT — D188)*

Owner (2026-10-30): the rewards of §10.41.3 came from wrong pricing — 300 000 cherries for a task and the
low «استقبل 1000 عملة» targets are absurd. Anchors: **1 000 000 coins = $12.50** (retail,
`COIN_RETAIL_USD_PER_MILLION` = 12.5, used to show money, never to charge) and **1 000 000 cherries =
$1.10** (payout, `CHERRY_PAYOUT_RATE`). Principle: free actions (watch, comment, follow, post, story,
message, hearts) get a small symbolic reward; tasks with real money behind them (spending or receiving
gifts) have **coin-value targets** counted from the stored gift rows (never reported by the app) and pay at
most about **1 %** of that value.

- **Defaults (band 1 · 2 · 3 · 4; migration `20261231130000_task_rewards_rebalance`, `seed-defaults`):**

  | Task | Target | Reward (cherries) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Free actions (`P_WATCH_LIVES`, `P_WATCH_MINUTES`, `P_AUDIO_ROOMS`, `P_LIVE_COMMENTS`, `P_LIVE_TAPS`, `P_FOLLOW`, `P_POST_COMMENTS`, `P_POST`, `P_REEL`, `P_STORY`, `P_DM_FRIEND`, `P_DM_VOICE`) | unchanged (§10.41.1) | 300 · 500 · 750 · 1 000 (reel —·500·750·1 000) |
  | Send gifts `P_SEND_GIFTS` (`GIFT_COINS_SENT`, now in band 1 too) | 10 000 · 25 000 · 50 000 · 100 000 coins | 1 000 · 2 500 · 5 000 · 10 000 |
  | Support a new host `P_NEW_HOST` | unchanged | 1 000 · 2 000 · 3 500 · 5 000 |
  | Host: live minutes `P_HOST_LIVE_30` | 60 · 80 · 100 · 120 min | 4 000 · 6 000 · 8 000 · 10 000 |
  | Host: gifts received `P_HOST_GIFTS` (`HOST_GIFT_COINS`, was a count) | 100 000 · 250 000 · 500 000 · 1 000 000 coins | 10 000 · 20 000 · 40 000 · 60 000 |
  | Host: accept a guest `P_HOST_GUEST` | unchanged | 2 000 · 3 000 · 4 000 · 6 000 |
  | Weekly host `HOST_LIVE_MINUTES` (per band) | 300 · 360 · 480 · 600 min in the ISO week | 180 000 · 190 000 · 220 000 · 250 000 |
  | Weekly host `HOST_GIFT_COINS` (per band) | 2 500 000 · 3 500 000 · 4 500 000 · 5 000 000 coins in the ISO week | 220 000 · 270 000 · 290 000 · 430 000 |

  **Follow-up (owner, same day: an active host should really reach about $5 a month):** the daily and
  monthly caps stay; the daily host tasks are ×2 and the weekly host tasks — outside the daily cap — carry
  one target and reward per level band (migration `20261231140000_task_weekly_host_bands`; a fixed
  `WEEKLY` task may now have `band_targets` / `band_rewards`, its `target` / `reward_cherries` mirroring
  band 4; `task-admin set <CODE> --targets … --rewards …`). The band is the caller's band of the day
  (today's assignment, else their level now); a band whose value is 0 does not get the task. A host who
  completes everything in a 31-day month: band 1 ≈ 2.26 M cherries ($2.49), band 2 ≈ 2.98 M ($3.28),
  band 3 ≈ 3.81 M ($4.19), band 4 ≈ 4.56 M — clipped at the monthly cap (4 545 454, $5.00). Each gift
  reward stays ≤ 1 % of its target's retail value (weekly band 4: 430 000 cherries on 5 000 000 coins,
  0.76 %).

  «Send a gift» `P_SEND_GIFT` (one gift of any price) is **switched off**: a single cheap gift cannot carry a
  reward within 1 % of its value; it becomes a coin-value template (1 000 · 2 500 · 5 000 · 10 000 coins →
  100 · 250 · 500 · 1 000) the team may switch on. D166's fixed daily tasks (off since D176) get 300 each and
  `SEND_GIFTS` becomes `GIFT_COINS_SENT` 10 000 coins → 1 000. Names that stated an amount no longer do
  («ابثّ مباشرة هذا الأسبوع (بالدقائق)», «استقبل هدايا هذا الأسبوع (بالعملات)»; the row shows x/y).
- **`GIFT_COINS_SENT`:** the sum of `live_gift_recipients.coins` of the caller's sends in the period paid
  with coins (`coins_charged > 0`: live and direct-conversation gifts; free quips and bag gifts do not count)
  to other ACTIVE people. `HOST_GIFT_COINS` (§10.41) is the coin value received, now also used daily.
- **Daily cap:** `TASK_DAILY_CAP_CHERRIES` = **50 000** (daily tasks).
- **Monthly cap:** `TASK_MONTHLY_CAP_MINOR` = **500** minor units of `CHERRY_PAYOUT_CURRENCY` ($5),
  converted at `CHERRY_PAYOUT_RATE` and floored → **4 545 454** cherries; `0` = none. It counts every task
  claim paid in cherries — daily and weekly — whose payment time falls in the current **calendar month of
  `LIVE_RANKINGS_TIME_ZONE`** (the programs' clock, like the days and weeks of §10.41; Asia/Riyadh in
  production). A claim pays at most what is left of both caps (a claim crossing the monthly cap pays the
  remainder), then 409 `TASK_MONTHLY_CAP_REACHED` (checked before `TASK_DAILY_CAP_REACHED`; weekly tasks
  too); it resets on the month's first day. The wire: `MyTasks.monthlyCapCherries` (0 = none) and
  `monthlyEarnedCherries`; the app shows «مكافآت الشهر: x من 4,545,454 كرزة» under the daily line. A band-4
  host who completes everything reaches it in a 31-day month (follow-up above).
- **Withdrawal unlock:** $60 of lifetime gift support (§10.46.1, `TASK_CHERRIES_UNLOCK_GIFT_MINOR` 6000).
- **Offers already made:** the migration re-prices the days' assignments (`task_assignments`, offers only)
  from their template and band, so an offer made under the old count target can never pay the old reward;
  claims already paid keep what they paid.
- **`task-admin`:** `list` and `set` print the money next to every reward (cherries × payout rate, e.g.
  `1000 (≈ $0.0011)`) and next to coin-value targets (coins × retail, e.g. `100000 coins (≈ $1.25)`).

### 10.52 Host-agent perks «وكيل مضيفين» *(v1.58-social, DRAFT — D189, CP-032)*

A host agent — the owner of a host agency (§10.46) — gets the same kind of perks as a recharge agent (§10.48). They
are **derived from the agency** (no bag items), like D185's.

- **Activation** (owner proposal a): `economy-admin agency-create` creates the agency and, in the same transaction,
  gives its owner the code `host` + the next number of `host_agent_counter`, at least two digits (`host01` …
  `host99`, `host100`, `host123`; `HostAgentCode`). The counter row is updated in that transaction, so concurrent
  activations get consecutive numbers; a number whose name is already used or held (an account named `host7`
  before the reservation, a pending registration, a premium or special name) is skipped. A code is never changed,
  given to another person or reused. Agencies created before v1.58 get theirs from the agency sweeper (oldest first;
  `AGENCY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`).
- **Special username** (§10.48.1, source `HOST_AGENT`): the code becomes the person's username — locked
  (`USERNAME_LOCKED`), permanent, the base username private to the person and the team, both signing in. `host` +
  digits is reserved (§6): never a regular username, never a gift (`username-admin`), held for its person forever
  (grace without an end, partial unique index `special_usernames_host_once`).
- **Perks:** `UserSummary.hostAgent` / `PublicProfile.hostAgent` (`HostAgentTag {code}`) while the agency exists, the
  team has not suspended its host agent and the account is active — **whatever the rank** (owner proposal b: NEW,
  AGENT, ADMIN and LAPSED alike). The app draws the host-agent badge exactly where the recharge-agent badge goes
  (profile, person card, inline next to the name in live rooms: chat, join line, viewers, requests, seats, host
  pill), the blue entrance bar «دخل وكيل المضيفين {username}» (the recharge bar's size, place and timing; a host
  agent's join is never dropped by the one-join-a-second limit) and the host-agent frame (photo in the round
  opening; no name). The room's host summary carries it too.
- **Suspension** (owner proposal b): `economy-admin agency-suspend <invite code> --note` removes every perk at once —
  the base username is shown again, frame, badge and entrance go — and keeps the code reserved for the person;
  `agency-reinstate` brings them back (the same code). Hosts, commissions and the rank are not touched. An account
  suspension (`AccountLifecycleService.suspend`) also gives the base username back; the derived perks already
  follow the account status. Audit `host_agent.activate`, `host_agent.suspend`, `host_agent.reinstate`.
- **Both a recharge and a host agent** (owner proposal c): both badges show. Only one special username is active:
  the code **activated first** stays the username and the other is held for the person (a GRACE row without an
  end) and shown in the agency dashboard (`OwnAgency.hostAgent.usernameShown` false). When the shown role is
  suspended, the other live code becomes the username; when it comes back, the first-activated rule applies again.
  The rule is `AGENT_USERNAME_RULE` in `users/agent-usernames.ts` (one place; also `RECHARGE_FIRST` / `HOST_FIRST`).
- **Frame precedence** (owner proposal d) on the profile and the person card: recharge-agent frame > host-agent
  frame > a frame worn from the bag (§10.49) > the CP frame (`agentFrameKindFor` in the app); the live ring still
  wins while the person is live. The recharge agent's entrance bar wins when a person is both.
- **Dashboard:** `OwnAgency.hostAgent` (`OwnHostAgent`): `code` (null only until the sweeper gives an older agency its
  code), `active` (not suspended), `usernameShown`.
- **Migrations** `20270103090000_host_agent_perks_enums` (the enum value), `20270103100000_host_agent_perks`
  (columns, counter, index); no username changes in SQL.

### 10.53 Card top-ups on the Kabso website «الشحن بالبطاقة» *(v1.59-social, DRAFT — D190, CP-033)*

Coins are bought by card **only on the Kabso website**, never inside the app (store rules). The website is three
small pages the API serves itself (`GET /topup`, `/topup/success`, `/topup/cancel`, outside `/api/v1`; Arabic RTL by
default, English with `?lang=en`; plain HTML/CSS/vanilla JS from the same origin, CSP `script-src 'self'`, no inline
script, nothing framed; the access token lives in the tab's `sessionStorage` only). The seller is **Kigofi LLC**,
30 N Gould St #7354, Sheridan, WY 82801, USA; the card statement shows **KABSO LIVE**.

- **Off by default.** All three of `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `TOPUP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` are needed
  (a partial set refuses to boot); without them every top-up operation is 503 `TOPUP_UNAVAILABLE` (no `Retry-After`)
  and the page says «الشحن بالبطاقة غير مفعّل». Production refuses a test key (`sk_test_` / `rk_test_`) unless
  `STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_KEYS_IN_PRODUCTION=true`, and needs an `https` base URL. The keys are set by the owner on the
  server only — never in git or chat. Hosted Checkout needs no publishable key. **v1.64-social (D196):** the OWNER
  may instead enter the two secrets (and the options below) in the admin panel «الدفع (Stripe)» — they override the
  env and need only `TOPUP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` on the server (§10.53.1).
- **Prices are the server's.** `TOPUP_PACKAGES` (default 100 000, 500 000, 1 000 000, 5 000 000, 10 000 000,
  50 000 000 coins; id = the amount) priced from `COIN_RETAIL_USD_PER_MILLION` (owner: 1 000 000 = **$12.50**), USD
  cents, each a whole number of cents ≥ 50. A checkout sends only `packageId` (a price or any other field is 400
  `unknown_field`). **No per-purchase limit; no hold on the host cherries the coins later make.**
- **Terms first.** `createTopupCheckout` needs `termsAccepted: true` and the current `termsVersion`
  (`TOPUP_TERMS_VERSION`); it stores the acceptance of «العملات رقمية وغير قابلة للاسترداد» (statement as shown,
  version, locale, time, IP, user agent) and the order **before** creating the Checkout session.
- **Checkout session:** `mode=payment`, one line at the order's price, `payment_method_options.card.
  request_three_d_secure=any` (3-D Secure always requested), receipt to the account's email, metadata
  `kabso_order_id` / `kabso_user_id`, optional `STRIPE_STATEMENT_DESCRIPTOR_SUFFIX`, 30-minute expiry, Stripe
  idempotency key per order. Radar runs with its default rules. A Stripe failure is 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (the
  order is marked FAILED; nothing charged).
- **Bank transfers** (`STRIPE_BANK_TRANSFER_ENABLED`, **on by default** — owner answer CP-033 Q3; Kigofi LLC is a US
  LLC): `customer_balance` with `bank_transfer` funding
  (`STRIPE_BANK_TRANSFER_TYPE`, default `us_bank_transfer`) next to the card where the Stripe account supports it;
  the buyer gets a Stripe customer once (`stripe_customers`). The order waits (`AWAITING_FUNDS`) and is credited on
  `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`.
- **Coins come ONLY from the signed webhook** (`POST /payments/stripe/webhook`, raw body, `Stripe-Signature`, 5-minute
  tolerance; a bad signature is 400): `checkout.session.completed` with `payment_status=paid` (amount and currency
  equal to the order's) or `async_payment_succeeded`, **exactly once per order** (`CARD_TOPUP`, reference the order,
  under the order's row lock; the ledger's unique key backs it). In the same transaction the D187 hook
  `recordRechargeIn(…, WEBSITE_TOPUP)` counts the coins for the daily recharge badge. The success page polls
  `getTopupOrder`; the redirect itself credits nothing.
- **Every Stripe event is applied once** (`stripe_events`, the event id; a replay or a concurrent delivery answers 200
  and changes nothing). A Stripe call an event needs (the automatic refund, the dispute evidence) runs after its
  database step; if it fails the webhook answers 503, Stripe retries, the database step is a no-op the second time.
- **Refund** (`charge.refunded`, cumulative `amount_refunded`), **early-fraud warning**
  (`radar.early_fraud_warning.created`) and **dispute** (`charge.dispute.created` / `closed`): the coins owed are
  recomputed from the order's facts — the refunded share plus an open or lost dispute's share, each rounded up; all
  of them after an early-fraud warning — and the difference is taken back (`CARD_TOPUP_REVERSAL`; **the balance may
  go below 0**, a debt the next coins pay first) or given back (`CARD_TOPUP_RESTORE`, a won dispute,
  `warning_closed`, `prevented`). The buyer is **frozen** (`topup_freezes`; 403 `TOPUP_ACCOUNT_FROZEN` on a new
  checkout) only by what Stripe or the card holder started — a dispute, an early-fraud warning (with its automatic
  refund), a `charge.refunded` Kabso did not ask for (owner answer CP-033 Q2). A **team refund** (`payments-admin
  refund`, e.g. goodwill) is recorded on the order (`team_refunded_minor`, `team_refund_reason`) before the Stripe
  call and carries `kabso_initiated=true` + `kabso_reason` in the refund's metadata (the automatic refund too): its
  coins are reversed **without a freeze**; audit `topup.admin_refund` and `topup.reverse` carry `initiatedBy` and the
  reason. When the event lists the charge's refunds, their marker decides; otherwise the recorded amount does.
  Whatever froze or not: while the balance is below 0 every gift send (live or conversation, coins or bag) and bag
  transfer is 403 `TOPUP_ACCOUNT_FROZEN`; once it is back to ≥ 0 gifts work again (owner answer CP-033 Q1) while
  card buying stays frozen until the team or a won dispute lifts it; and coin spending fails anyway (`INSUFFICIENT_COINS`). An early-fraud warning is
  **refunded automatically** through the API (`reason=fraudulent`, idempotency key per order; never after a dispute
  or a full refund) — the later `charge.refunded` takes nothing more and opens no second case.
- **Host cherries are never taken back automatically.** Each refund / warning / dispute opens an admin case
  (`topup_cases`, once per Stripe object) with the **FIFO attribution**: the coins held before the purchase are spent
  first, then the purchase's; the case lists every send the purchase paid for (gift, place, coins from the purchase,
  recipients and the cherries each got, whether already reversed) — the team decides with `economy-admin
  reverse-gift` (D179). `payments-admin` lists orders and cases, shows a case, closes it, unfreezes a buyer and asks
  Stripe for a team refund (the coins then come back through the webhook; no freeze).
- **Dispute evidence** on `charge.dispute.created` (submitted at once unless `STRIPE_DISPUTE_AUTO_SUBMIT=false`):
  `access_activity_log` (the buyer's sign-ins with IP and device, the terms acceptance, the credit, what the coins
  were used for — no recipient), `customer_email_address`, `customer_name`, `customer_purchase_ip`,
  `product_description`, `refund_policy`, `refund_policy_disclosure` (the ticked statement with time, IP, UA),
  `service_date`, `uncategorized_text`, and a one-page receipt PDF (`receipt`). **Never another user's personal
  data.** A **won** dispute gives the coins back, closes the case and lifts the freeze when none of the buyer's
  purchases still has coins taken back or a fraud warning; a lost one keeps both.
- **Chargeback Protection** (Stripe's product) may be switched on by the owner in the dashboard; nothing here
  depends on it.
- **The app** never takes a card payment. `RechargePackages.websiteTopupUrl` is `${TOPUP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/topup`
  only while `TOPUP_APP_LINK_ENABLED=true` (**on by default**, owner answer CP-033 Q4; a per-environment server switch;
  store payment rules reviewed before release, PP-35) and top-ups are on; the wallet then shows
  «الشحن من الموقع», which opens the browser. **v1.109-social (D344, §10.143):** it opens in an in-app browser tab,
  already signed in through a one-time code; the link is also per store (`TOPUP_APP_LINK_PLATFORMS`); the website
  prices include Stripe's fee (§10.143.2).
- **Migrations** `20270104090000_card_topups_enums` (the three ledger reasons), `20270104100000_card_topups` (tables,
  CHECKs, the wallet and ledger ranges below 0, the reason-sign rule), `20270104110000_topup_team_refunds` (the team
  refund columns).

#### 10.53.1 The Stripe keys from the admin panel «الدفع (Stripe)» *(v1.64-social, DRAFT — D196)*

The OWNER enters the Stripe keys in the panel instead of the server environment (owner D196). Section «الدفع
(Stripe)», capability **`payments.settings` (OWNER only)**; every route is behind the panel's cookie session + CSRF
(§10.54.2); without `ADMIN_TOTP_KEY` it answers 503 `ADMIN_PANEL_UNAVAILABLE` like the rest of the panel.

- **What it sets:** the Stripe **secret key or restricted key** (`sk_…` / `rk_…`), the **webhook signing secret**
  (`whsec_…`), an optional **publishable key** (`pk_…`; public by design, shown in full; hosted Checkout does not use
  it; it must have the secret key's mode), and the options **bank transfers** on/off, the **statement descriptor
  suffix**, **dispute evidence auto-submit** on/off and the **app link** «الشحن من الموقع» on/off — each null = the
  server's env value (`STRIPE_BANK_TRANSFER_ENABLED`, `STRIPE_STATEMENT_DESCRIPTOR_SUFFIX`,
  `STRIPE_DISPUTE_AUTO_SUBMIT`, `TOPUP_APP_LINK_ENABLED`; a suffix `""` = explicitly none). `TOPUP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`,
  `STRIPE_BANK_TRANSFER_TYPE`, `TOPUP_PACKAGES` and `STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_KEYS_IN_PRODUCTION` stay server settings; the
  base URL is shown read-only.
- **Secrets are write-only.** No response, log or audit row ever carries the secret key or the webhook secret:
  `getAdminPaymentSettings` returns `PaymentKeyInfo` per key — `kind` (`secret` / `restricted` / `webhook`),
  `mode` (`live` / `test`), `last4`, `source` (`panel` / `env`), `setBy` and `setAt` — for the keys in use, the
  panel's and the env's (`Cache-Control: no-store`). At rest (`payment_settings`, one row, migration
  `20270111100000_payment_settings`) each secret is **AES-256-GCM** sealed (`v1.<iv>.<tag>.<ciphertext>`, the column
  name as additional data) with a key derived by HKDF-SHA-256 from `ADMIN_TOTP_KEY` with its own info string
  **`payment-settings/v1`** (not the TOTP secrets' key); only the prefix (`rk_live`) and the last 4 characters are in
  clear. In the process the values are wrapped so JSON, string conversion and `util.inspect` print `[redacted]`; the
  log redaction also masks `sk_/rk_/whsec_` values and the `secretKey` / `webhookSecret` / `totpCode` fields. A new
  `ADMIN_TOTP_KEY` makes the saved keys unreadable: they are then ignored (`panelKeysIgnored: unreadable`, the env
  keys apply) until the OWNER enters them again.
- **Every change** (`updateAdminPaymentSettings`, PATCH: only the fields sent; `clearAdminPaymentKeys`) needs the
  **authenticator code again** (`totpCode`, §10.54.3: 400 missing, 403 `ADMIN_TOTP_INVALID` wrong or used, counted
  towards the lockout) **and a reason**, and writes `payment.settings.update` / `payment.settings.clear` in its
  transaction with before / after as **masked fingerprints** (`rk_live_…AbCd`, `whsec_…wxYz`, `pk_live_…`), the
  options, `changed`, `connectionTest` (`stripe` / `skipped`), the reason and `via: panel`. The first keys come as a
  pair (one alone: 400 `required` on the other); later either may be rotated alone.
- **«اختبار الاتصال»** (`testAdminPaymentKey`) and **every save of a new secret key** first call Stripe with that key
  (`balance.retrieve`, nothing read is shown; a restricted key without the balance permission still passes as
  `restricted`). Refused by Stripe → 409 `ADMIN_ACTION_REFUSED` (`secretKey` `stripe_rejected`), Stripe unreachable →
  503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; nothing saved. The test is audited `payment.settings.test` (the fingerprint and the
  outcome). `skipConnectionTest: true` saves without the call **only for a test key and only when NODE_ENV is not
  production** (else 409 `connection_test_required`). A test key in production is refused (409
  `test_key_in_production`) unless `STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_KEYS_IN_PRODUCTION=true` — **env only**, never a panel switch; a
  saved test key is also ignored at run time in production without it. The panel checks the code before it asks
  Stripe anything.
- **Source of truth:** the panel's keys when both are saved and readable, else the env keys
  (`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, still a pair, still needing `TOPUP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`), else none
  (503 `TOPUP_UNAVAILABLE`). Existing env deployments keep working unchanged. `PaymentSettingsStore` is the one
  reader (top-ups, the wallet's `websiteTopupUrl`, the website switch): it re-reads the row at most every 5 seconds
  (the instance that saved at once) and keeps one Stripe client per key — **a new key is used by the next request,
  no restart**. `clearAdminPaymentKeys` removes the panel's keys (409 `nothing_to_clear` when there are none): the
  env keys apply again, or top-ups are off. `payments-admin refund` uses the panel's key when `ADMIN_TOTP_KEY` is
  passed to it, else `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`.
- **Webhook rotation:** the webhook verifies with the current signing secret and, for **10 minutes** after a change
  (a new webhook secret, or a clear that ends the panel's), also with the one in use before
  (`previousWebhookSecretValidUntil`), so deliveries Stripe signed before the change still apply.
- **The webhook to configure in Stripe** is shown with a copy button: `webhookUrl` =
  `${TOPUP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/api/v1/payments/stripe/webhook` and `webhookEvents` — `checkout.session.completed`,
  `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`, `checkout.session.async_payment_failed`, `checkout.session.expired`,
  `charge.refunded`, `radar.early_fraud_warning.created`, `charge.dispute.created`, `charge.dispute.closed`.
- **The website's switch:** `updateAdminSiteSettings` refuses to turn `topupEnabled` **on** while there are no keys
  (409 `ADMIN_ACTION_REFUSED`, `topupEnabled` `stripe_keys_missing`, «enter them in «الدفع (Stripe)» first»); a
  switch already on is not touched by a later clear (the website then shows «الشحن بالبطاقة غير مفعّل»).

### 10.54 The admin panel «لوحة الإدارة» *(v1.60-social, DRAFT — D191, CP-034)*

A web panel for the team at `https://admin.<domain>` (`apps/admin`, React + TypeScript + Vite, a static build served
by Caddy, which proxies `/api/*` to the API on the same origin). It calls only the `admin-panel` operations below and
`/admin/auth/*`; it has no data of its own. Arabic RTL first with an English toggle, light and dark.

#### 10.54.1 Roles and capabilities

The panel's roles are **values of the existing admin permissions** (`admin_permission`, CP-005 §9.8) held by an
account whose `users.role` is `ADMIN`: `OWNER`, `MODERATION` (the moderator «مشرف»), `SUPPORT` «دعم», `FINANCE`
«مالية». They are granted and revoked with the CLI `admin-admin grant|revoke <email> <role>` (`MODERATOR` is
accepted for `MODERATION`), which writes an audit row; a grant makes the account an admin when it is not one yet
(how the first OWNER is bootstrapped). `admin-admin list` shows the panel admins; `admin-admin reset-2fa <email>`
clears a lost authenticator (the next sign-in enrols again). Revoking the last panel role ends the person's panel
sessions. **Since D197 / D271 the OWNER also manages roles in the panel** («الموظفون والصلاحيات», capability
`team.manage`, OWNER only; §10.60.6, §10.96.5) with the same rule functions (`admin-roles.ts`), each change with a
reason and the OWNER's authenticator code again; the CLI stays the bootstrap of the first OWNER (and accepts
`@username` for `<email>` since D271). Neither the panel nor the CLI revokes the **last active OWNER** (D271: grant
OWNER to another account first).

Every panel route names one capability and the server checks it on **every request** against the roles held at that
moment (a revoked role or a suspended account applies at once; 403 `AUTH_FORBIDDEN`). The panel only hides what the
session's `capabilities` do not include.

| Capability | OWNER | MODERATION | SUPPORT | FINANCE |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| `dashboard.view`, `users.view` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `users.balances` (a profile's balances, read-only; owner 2026-10-31: the moderator too) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `users.ledger` (the latest coin and cherry ledger rows in a profile; D275: the moderator too, read-only) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `users.ban`, `users.avatar`, `reports.view`, `reports.act` | ✓ | ✓ | | |
| `users.special_username`, `recharge.applications` (private fields and pictures), `recharge.decide`, `recharge.status` | ✓ | | ✓ | |
| `recharge.agents` (the agents list and the exchange rates, read; D275: the moderator too, with no action) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `recharge.topups.view` (D275: the top-up records, read-only — the agents' top-ups «شحن الوكلاء» and the users' card orders, and their CSV — owner «نعم», audited `admin.export.csv`) | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ |
| `recharge.topup`, `recharge.cap`, `withdrawals.view`, `withdrawals.decide` | ✓ | | | ✓ |
| `site.settings` | ✓ | | | |
| `payments.settings` (v1.64-social, D196: the Stripe keys and top-up options, §10.53.1) | ✓ | | | |
| `storage.settings` (v1.75-social, D222: the media storage R2 / S3 keys, buckets and switch, §10.72) | ✓ | | | |
| `kyc.settings` (v1.80-kyc, D227: the Didit API key, webhook secret, workflows, daily limit and switch, §10.77) | ✓ | | | |
| `fx.settings` (v1.81-social, D245: the paid exchange-rate provider, its API key and switch «مزوّد أسعار الصرف», §10.87.4) | ✓ | | | |
| `kyc.view` (v1.80-kyc, D227: a person's identity check — name, birth date, document country, duplicates — and the short-lived image fetch, each audited, §10.77) | ✓ | | ✓ | |
| `verification.view` (v1.90-social, D293: the verification badges' thresholds, their defaults, the last recompute and the holders per badge, §10.105.4) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `verification.settings` (v1.90-social, D293: change the thresholds — a reason and the code again; everyone recomputed at once, §10.105.4) | ✓ | | | |
| `recharge.disputes` (v1.69-social, D204: «نزاعات الشحن» — a disputed order, its chat and pictures, «الإدارة» lines, §10.64.9; D275: the moderator too) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `recharge.disputes.resolve` (v1.69-social, D204: a dispute's decision, the code again; D275: the moderator too) | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ |
| `recharge.rates` (v1.69-social, D204: editing the exchange rates) | ✓ | | | ✓ |

**The moderator and money (D275, owner).** «المشرف يمكن ان يكون لديه سجل شحن للوكلاء والمستخدمين بحيث يعرض المعاملة فقط
دون تعديل او حذف» — «يمكنه ايضاً مشاهدة نزاعات الشحن والحكم فيها لكن لا يمكنه ارسال اي عملات او سحب الا من النزاعات
الحكم فيها». MODERATION reads the recharge agents and the exchange rates (`recharge.agents`), the agents' top-ups and
the users' card orders (`recharge.topups.view`, with their CSV export, audited — owner «نعم»; not the Stripe cases or the financial report), a
user's coin and cherry ledger (`users.ledger`), and views and decides the recharge disputes (`recharge.disputes`,
`recharge.disputes.resolve`, the authenticator code again, §10.64.9). It never holds `recharge.topup`,
`recharge.cap`, `recharge.status`, `recharge.rates`, `withdrawals.*`, `finance.view`, `finance.refund`,
`users.balance_adjust`, `referrals.decide` or `payments.settings`: **a dispute decision is the only coin movement a
moderator can cause.** The panel shows the moderator these pages with no other action button.

An account holding a panel role can be banned, unbanned or otherwise acted on only by an OWNER; nobody acts on their
own account (409 `ADMIN_ACTION_REFUSED`).

#### 10.54.2 Sign-in, session, CSRF, lockout

- **Separate sign-in** — the app's tokens open nothing here. `adminLogin` (`POST /admin/auth/login` `{email,
  password}`; *(v1.84-live, D302)* `email` may be the staff ID of its current holder, §10.96.12) checks an existing account's password (Argon2id, as `login`); an unknown email, a wrong password, a
  non-admin, a suspended account and an admin without a panel role all get the same 401 `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`.
  It sets a **pending** session that allows only the second factor for `ADMIN_PENDING_SECONDS` (300).
- **Mandatory TOTP** (RFC 6238: SHA-1, 30 s, 6 digits, ±1 step). First sign-in: `startAdminTotpEnrolment` returns a
  new secret and its `otpauth://` URI (the panel draws the QR code itself); `confirmAdminTotpEnrolment` checks a code
  and returns **ten recovery codes, shown once** (`xxxxx-xxxxx`; only their SHA-256 is stored; each works once).
  Later sign-ins: `verifyAdminTotp` with `{code}` or `{recoveryCode}`. A code's time step is consumed: the same code
  never works twice (also across concurrent requests). The secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted with a key derived
  (HKDF-SHA-256, `admin-totp/v1`) from **`ADMIN_TOTP_KEY`** (server env, ≥ 32 bytes, strength-checked in
  production). Without `ADMIN_TOTP_KEY` every panel route answers 503 `ADMIN_PANEL_UNAVAILABLE`. Changing the key makes
  enrolled authenticators unreadable (`admin-admin reset-2fa`).
- **Session**: the cookie `__Host-kabso_admin` — HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, no Domain (only
  admin.<domain>); a 256-bit random value of which only the SHA-256 is stored (`admin_sessions`). The second factor
  ends the pending session and starts a new one (new cookie: no fixation). Idle expiry `ADMIN_SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS`
  (1800, sliding), absolute `ADMIN_SESSION_MAX_SECONDS` (28 800). `getAdminSession` returns who is signed in, the
  roles, the capabilities and the **CSRF token**; `adminLogout` ends the session.
- **CSRF**: every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE of a panel session needs `X-CSRF-Token` = the session's token (an HMAC of the
  cookie, HKDF `admin-csrf/v1`; never stored) — else 403 `ADMIN_CSRF_INVALID`. With SameSite=Strict and the same
  origin this is defence in depth.
- **Lockout**: `ADMIN_LOCKOUT_ATTEMPTS` (5) failed passwords for an email lock that email for `ADMIN_LOCKOUT_SECONDS`
  (900) — counted the same way for every email, so the lock reveals nothing. The same number of failed codes (sign-in,
  enrolment, recovery or a financial re-entry) locks the admin account (`admin_credentials.locked_until`) and **ends
  all its panel sessions**. Both answer 429 `ADMIN_LOCKED` with `Retry-After`. A right code resets the count.
- **Rate limits** (§7): `RATE_LIMIT_ADMIN_LOGIN_IP` (30 / 15 min per IP) on sign-in and the second factor,
  `RATE_LIMIT_ADMIN_IP` (1200 / 15 min per IP) on every other panel route; both replace the public default.
- **Logs**: no password, code, secret, cookie or CSRF token is logged or audited; audit rows carry ids, roles and
  reasons only.

#### 10.54.3 Audit, reasons and the financial re-entry

Every change from the panel writes an `audit_logs` row in its transaction with the admin as `actor_user_id`, the
request IP and request id, the target, and `metadata.via = "panel"`, the reason and a before/after summary where
there is a state change. Reasons are **required** for: ban, unban, avatar removal, special-username gift and revoke,
application rejection, agent suspension, reinstatement and cap, withdrawal rejection, warn and ban from a report
(`note`). Views of private data are audited too: `admin.user.view` (a profile: base username, balances),
`recharge.application.view` (an application's private fields) and `recharge.application.photo_view` (each picture).
Sign-in events: `admin.login.password|success|failure|locked`, `admin.totp.enrol|failure`,
`admin.recovery_code.used`, `admin.logout`; roles: `admin.role.grant|revoke`, `admin.totp.reset` (CLI).

**Financial actions need the authenticator code again** (`totpCode` in the body): `topUpAdminRechargeAgent`,
`payAdminWithdrawal`, `rejectAdminWithdrawal` (it refunds the held cherries); v1.64-social (D196):
`updateAdminPaymentSettings` and `clearAdminPaymentKeys`, which also need a reason (§10.53.1); v1.75-social (D222):
`updateAdminStorageSettings` and `clearAdminStorageSettings`, with a reason too (§10.72); v1.81-social (D245):
`updateAdminFxSettings` and `clearAdminFxSettings`, with a reason too (§10.87.4). A missing code is 400; a wrong or used
one 403 `ADMIN_TOTP_INVALID` (counted towards the lockout); nothing changes.

#### 10.54.4 One rule for the CLI and the panel

The panel does not reimplement admin rules: it calls the same functions as the CLIs, which take an `AdminVia`
(`{via: 'cli' | 'panel', actorUserId, ip}`) and write the same audit row (only `via` and the actor differ):
`recharge-core.ts` (`recharge-admin` approve / reject / topup / suspend / reinstate / set-cap), `withdrawal-admin.ts`
(`economy-admin withdrawal-pay | withdrawal-reject`, moved out of the CLI), `avatar-admin.ts` (`profile-admin
remove-avatar`), `special-usernames.ts` (`username-admin gift | revoke`). Ban / unban use `AccountLifecycleService`
(`suspendIn`, new `unsuspendIn`: live ended, seats freed, agent username synced); report actions use
`SafetyService.act` (DISMISS, REMOVE_TARGET). A refusal of a shared rule is 409 `ADMIN_ACTION_REFUSED` with the rule's
own message.

#### 10.54.5 The sections (phase 1)

1. **Home** `getAdminDashboard`: today's new users (the **Asia/Riyadh day**, owner 2026-10-31; server setting
   `ADMIN_DASHBOARD_TIME_ZONE`, default `Asia/Riyadh`, the recharge badges' day rule), coins sold by recharge agents (and the number of sales),
   gifts sent (and their coin value), lives live now, and the pending counts (applications, withdrawals, open reports)
   — real aggregates. Website top-ups appear when D190 merges.
2. **Users** `searchAdminUsers` (`q`: a UUID, an email prefix, or a username — shown, base or special, also as a
   prefix), `getAdminUser` (profile, special username, panel roles, balances and the 20 latest coin and cherry ledger
   rows by capability, recharge-agent / host-agent / agency-host status, reports against); actions ban / unban,
   remove the profile photo, give / take back a special username.
3. **Recharge agents** `listAdminRechargeApplications` (no private field), `getAdminRechargeApplication` (private
   fields, audited), `getAdminRechargeApplicationPhoto` (the WebP bytes streamed by the API with
   `Cache-Control: private, no-store` — never a storage URL; audited per view; the panel fetches a picture only when
   asked), approve / reject; `listAdminRechargeAgents` (with the owner's `pricing`), top-up (tier price and paid USD,
   a different amount needs a note; code again), suspend / reinstate, cap. D275: the moderator «مشرف» reads the agents
   list (`recharge.agents`) with none of these actions.
4. **Withdrawals** (D179) `listAdminWithdrawals` (PENDING oldest first), mark paid with a payment reference (kept as
   the decision note `ref: … — note`), reject with a reason (the cherries go back). Stripe cases appear when D190
   merges.
5. **Reports** `listAdminPanelReports` (every target kind with `preview`: text, picture, the author and whether it is
   already gone) and `actOnAdminPanelReport`: DISMISS, REMOVE_TARGET, **WARN** (the author gets the new system
   notification `MODERATION_WARNING`, target the post when there is one) and **BAN** (the author is suspended); WARN
   and BAN need `note` and close every open report on the target as ACTIONED.
6. **Website settings «إعدادات الموقع»** (OWNER) — §10.54.6.
7. **Payments «الدفع (Stripe)»** (OWNER; v1.64-social, D196) — §10.53.1.
8. **Storage «التخزين (R2 / S3)»** (OWNER; v1.75-social, D222) — §10.72.
9. **Exchange-rate provider «مزوّد أسعار الصرف»** (OWNER; v1.81-social, D245) — §10.87.4; the rates themselves are
   «أسعار الصرف» (OWNER / FINANCE edit, every recharge role reads; §10.64.1, §10.87).

Lists are keyset-paginated (`cursor`, `limit` ≤ 100; reports use the `listAdminReports` cursor).

#### 10.54.6 The public website's settings (D191 + D192: one module, table and contract)

Table `site_settings` (migration `20270104100000_admin_panel`; module `site-settings`; keys `socials`, `topupEnabled`;
a missing key is its default). The website (D192, §10.55) and the panel both use it:

- `getSiteSettings` (`GET /site/settings`, public, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`) returns `{socials: {instagram,
  tiktok, whatsapp}, topupEnabled}`. `getAdminSiteSettings` reads the same for the panel's form.
- **One value form**, stored and served: a full https URL or null (the website hides the icon) —
  `https://www.instagram.com/<handle>`, `https://www.tiktok.com/@<handle>`, `https://wa.me/<digits>` (8–15 digits, no
  leading 0). Input may be `https://(www.)instagram.com/<handle>`, `https://(www.)tiktok.com/@<handle>`, a
  `https://wa.me/<digits>` link or the number in international form (`+966 50 000 0000`); it is normalized to that
  form. Other hosts, schemes or shapes are 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` (`socials.<name>` `invalid_value`), nothing
  changed. A stored value is re-checked when read (one that no longer passes is served as null). The website's
  `common.js` accepts exactly these shapes.
- **One write route:** `updateAdminSiteSettings` (`PUT /admin/site-settings`, the panel's cookie session + CSRF,
  capability `site.settings` = OWNER) replaces the whole document (an empty link clears it; optional `reason`),
  audited `site.settings.update` with before, after, `reason` and `via: panel`. A bearer token opens nothing here
  (401). v1.64-social (D196): turning `topupEnabled` on without Stripe keys is 409 (`stripe_keys_missing`, §10.53.1). There is no separate admin permission for it: OWNER is the website's editor.

#### 10.54.7 Serving (Caddy)

`admin.{$KABSO_DOMAIN}` serves `infra/deploy/admin/` (the build, SPA fallback to `index.html`) and proxies `/api/*`
to the API; `/internal/*` 404. Headers: a strict CSP (`default-src 'self'`; `img-src 'self' data: https:`;
`frame-ancestors 'none'`; `form-action 'self'`; `base-uri 'none'`), HSTS, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `nosniff`,
`Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. An optional IP allowlist (`KABSO_ADMIN_ALLOW_IPS`, space-separated
CIDRs; unset = everyone, an empty value blocks everyone) answers 403 to other addresses. DNS: an A record `admin.<domain>` (DEPLOYMENT §11.6).

### 10.55 The public website kabsolive.com *(v1.61-social, DRAFT — D192, CP-035)*

The root domain serves the owner's coming-soon page and the legal pages from `infra/deploy/site/` (static files,
Caddy). Nothing on it is a product screen; it never shows user content.

- **Waitlist «أبلغني عند الإطلاق»** (replaces the store buttons; small non-link «قريباً» badges for App Store and
  Google Play stay): `POST /waitlist {email, locale}` — public, the email trimmed + lowercased (the registration
  rules' `emailSchema`), `locale` `ar`|`en` (the language the website shows). One row per email in
  `waitlist_signups` (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`): a repeated sign-up keeps the first row and gets **the
  same 202 `{status: "accepted"}`** — the answer never reveals whether an email was listed. 10 / hour per client IP
  (§7). No e-mail is sent now (the launch mailing is a later step, after the owner's approval). The e-mails are read
  only with `waitlist-admin list [--limit N]` / `export [--locale ar|en]` (CSV, formulas neutralised), each run
  audited `waitlist.view` {op, count} without addresses. No IP or user agent is stored with a sign-up.
- **Settings:** the footer's social links and the top-up switch are D191's `site_settings` (§10.54.6, one module,
  table and contract): the website reads `GET /site/settings`; the OWNER changes them in the panel «إعدادات الموقع».
- **The website** fetches `/api/v1/site/settings` at load (kept 5 minutes in `sessionStorage`); on any error the
  social icons stay hidden and the top-up link stays off. The footer shows Instagram / TikTok / WhatsApp icons only
  for the links set. The header shows «شحن العملات» → `https://<domain>/topup` (D190's page) only while
  `topupEnabled` is true.
- **Legal pages** `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/contact` (Arabic and English on one page each): written from what the
  product does (accounts, profiles, media, lives, DMs, gifts and coins, cherries, withdrawals, recharge-agent KYC with
  its 90-day retention, push). The legal entity and contact come from `infra/deploy/site/config.json`
  (`companyLegalName`, `address`, `country`, `governingLaw`, `supportEmail`, `minAge`, `legalReviewed`,
  `lastUpdated`); an empty field renders «سيُضاف قريباً» / "To be added" and `/contact` lists only the filled ones;
  every legal page shows the banner «مسودة — تحتاج مراجعة قانونية» while `legalReviewed` is false; `update.sh`
  prints a warning listing empty fields. Minimum age 18 (owner, confirmed).
- **Language:** Arabic RTL by default; `?lang=en` or the toggle (kept in `localStorage`, read in try/catch) switches
  every text and `dir`.
- **Caddy root block:** `/api/v1/waitlist` and `/api/v1/site/settings` go to the API (same origin, so no CORS);
  `/topup*` is a 302 to `https://api.<domain>` + the same path (D190's pages, `TOPUP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, their own CSP
  and their same-origin `/api/v1` calls); everything else is static, with `Content-Security-Policy` (`default-src 'self'`; Google Fonts for the
  owner's Cairo/Inter; no inline script), `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`,
  `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, HSTS (one year) and clean URLs (`/privacy` →
  `privacy.html`). `www.<domain>`
  redirects permanently to the apex.
- **Migration** `20270106100000_website` (`waitlist_signups`; `site_settings` is created by D191's
  `20270104100000_admin_panel`).

### 10.56 Account deletion «حذف الحساب» *(v1.62-social, DRAFT — D193, CP-036)*

The person deletes their own account inside the app (Apple App Store Review Guideline 5.1.1(v); Google Play's
account-deletion requirement), with a **30-day grace period** during which they can change their mind. The rules
live in `users/account-deletion.ts` (shared by the API, the sweeper and the `account-admin` CLI).

- **Flow (app):** Settings › Account › «حذف الحساب» → (1) an explanation — what is deleted, what is kept, the
  grace period, that coins, cherries, bag items and premium time are forfeited — with what must be settled first
  (`getAccountDeletionInfo.blockers`); (2) the password again (re-authentication; a forgotten password is reset by
  email first — `forgotPassword` also works during the grace period); (3) the confirmation word «حذف» (or `DELETE`);
  (4) `requestAccountDeletion` → 202.
- **Blockers** (409 `ACCOUNT_DELETION_BLOCKED`, checked again inside the request's transaction): `recharge_agent` (a
  recharge agent, §10.48, not suspended, or with coins left in the stock — the team settles the stock and suspends
  it), `host_agency` (the owner of a host agency, §10.46/§10.52, not suspended by the team or still with hosts),
  `pending_withdrawal` (a cherry withdrawal waiting to be paid), `pending_cherry_sale` (a cherry sale to a recharge
  agent still open), `negative_balance` (a negative coin or cherry balance — a reversal or a dispute, checked
  generically).
- **At the request** (one transaction): `users.status` → `PENDING_DELETION`; a PENDING `account_deletion_requests`
  row with `purge_after` = now + `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS`; every session revoked (`revoked_reason`
  `ACCOUNT_DELETION`) with its push token; out of every live room (seats, requests, invitations, moderator roles).
  Every `status = 'ACTIVE'` filter hides the account at once, as for a deactivated one: search, profile (404), follow
  and member lists, live rooms (a LIVE room of theirs is hidden by the ACTIVE-host filter and ended by the room
  sweeper), and the access-token guard refuses its tokens. Nothing else is removed yet. A notice is mailed
  (`requested`, with the date) when mail is configured. Audit `account.deletion.requested`.
- **During the grace period:** `login` with the right password answers 409 `ACCOUNT_DELETION_PENDING` (detail
  `purgeAfter`; a wrong password still gets 401, so nothing is revealed); the app shows «طلب حذف قيد التنفيذ —
