  إلغاء الحذف؟». `login` with `cancelDeletion: true` cancels: ACTIVE again with everything it had (follows, content,
  balances), the request CANCELLED, a notice mailed (`cancelled`), audit `account.deletion.cancelled`, and the
  person is signed in.
- **Purge** (the sweeper, every `ACCOUNT_DELETION_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, once `purge_after` passed; or
  `account-admin purge-now`): the account becomes a **tombstone** — the same random user id, status DELETED,
  `deleted_at` set, no personal data. Idempotent (a DELETED account is skipped).
  - **Deleted:** email (→ `deleted+<id>@deleted.invalid`), password, profile fields (name → «مستخدم محذوف»,
    username → `deleted.` + 16 hex digits, bio, photo, country, gender, category, links), settings, sessions,
    verification and push tokens; posts and reels (with their likes, comments, media and reports — except reported
    items under a legal hold, below), stories,
    comments on others' posts (soft-deleted, text removed), likes, saves and reposts of others' posts (counters
    adjusted), views and share events, mentions; direct messages they wrote (gift messages stay — they show the
    gift), live-chat, family-chat and CP-confession messages they wrote, paid bullet texts (→ `·`), their
    notifications and their part in others'; follows, follow requests, blocks and mutes both ways; their media
    assets and uploads (files deleted from object storage after the commit; without storage settings the CLI prints
    the keys, as `profile-admin remove-avatar` does); KYC data of recharge-agent applications (name, phone, photo,
    selfie, places, payment methods; files deleted); hosting permission, schedule, featured slot, watch
    suggestions; the family membership (a leader hands the family to the longest-serving deputy, else member; a
    leader alone disbands it) and the CP couple (ended); a recharge-agent employment and an agency-host link end.
  - **Kept, under the tombstone id, without personal data** — accounting, tax and fraud (records of money that
    moved must stay complete and balanced: every ledger row has a `balance_after` chain; chargeback and
    dispute evidence) and the security audit: wallets and the coin, cherry, family, CP and level ledgers; gifts sent
    and received (others' gift history: the sender shows as «مستخدم محذوف», `senderDeleted`); lucky draws and the
    18+ statement; boosts, bag items and transfers; premium-username leases and payments; recharge sales, stock and
    cherry requests; agency rows, earnings and months; cherry withdrawals (the payout details cut to their last 4
    characters, to match bank records); task, check-in and event rewards; live-room history and statistics; reports
    made and about the person; special usernames; the deletion request (PURGED); the audit log (append-only). All of
    it for `DELETED_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS` (owner: **7 years**, 2557 days) after the purge — below.
  - **Audit log at the purge:** every row whose actor or target user is the account loses its **IP address (set to
    NULL — dropped rather than truncated: a truncated /24 or /48 still narrows a home connection down, and nothing
    needs it once the account is gone)** and the person's identifiers in its metadata (`username`, `email`,
    `identifier`, `from`, `to`, `baseUsername`, `regularUsername`, `displayName`, `name`, `phone`, `fullName`
    removed). `audit_logs` is append-only for the runtime role, so this is the `SECURITY DEFINER` function
    `account_deletion_scrub_audit` (only for a DELETED account). The snapshots of DM reports about their messages lose
    `senderUsername`, those of profile-link reports carry the tombstone username.
  - **Legal hold of reported content** (owner, 2026-10-31): before anything is deleted, every item of theirs with an
    **OPEN or ACTIONED** report — a post or reel, comment, story, live-chat, family-chat or CP-confession message, a
    direct message (from the report's snapshot) or a profile link — is copied into `legal_holds`: a snapshot of the
    content (text, dates, kind, media metadata and keys; never the author's name, username or email) linked only to
    the **tombstone id** and to its reports (`reports.legal_hold_id`; every report of that item, whatever its status;
    the target id of a post, comment, story or chat message moves to the hold, `legal_holds.target_id`). The original
    rows are deleted (a comment stays soft-deleted with its text removed) as for unreported content; the files of
    held items (media, the DM report's own copy) stay in storage. **No user can see it** — no app or API operation
    returns `legal_holds`; the moderation queue (`GET /admin/reports`) keeps listing the reports with `targetId` and
    can act on them (closes every report of the hold; nothing left to remove). Admins read the content only with
    `account-admin holds` / `hold-show` (migration role), and **every view is audited** (`account.deletion.hold_viewed`,
    with the reason; the list too). The DM sweeper leaves held DM snapshots alone. After `REPORT_LEGAL_HOLD_DAYS` (90)
    the sweeper deletes the hold **with its reports and files** (`account.deletion.hold_expired`). Content whose
    reports are all DISMISSED, and unreported content, is deleted at the purge with its reports.
  - **Retention end** (`DELETED_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS`, 2557, after `account_deletion_requests.purged_at`; the same
    sweeper, one transaction per tombstone): **deleted** — `audit_logs` rows whose actor or target user is the
    tombstone (function `account_deletion_end_retention`), `account_deletion_requests` (the record of the deletion),
    `lucky_gift_age_confirmations` (the 18+ statement); **anonymised** — `cherry_withdrawals.payout_details` → `…`
    and `decision_note` → NULL, `points_ledger.reason` → NULL (`—` on ADMIN rows, which must keep one). These five
    tables are all the job changes. **Left in place as anonymous accounting** (amounts, dates and counterparties
    only, under a random id that no longer leads to anything about the person; deleting them would break other
    people's `balance_after` chains, gift histories and the books): every other row under the tombstone id — the
    *Kept* list above, i.e. `wallets`, `wallet_ledger`, `cherry_wallets`, `cherry_ledger`, `points_ledger`,
    `level_history`, `user_level_states`, `family_points_ledger`, `cp_gifts`, `cp_points_ledger`, `cp_check_ins`,
    `cp_task_claims`, `live_gifts`, `live_gift_recipients`, `lucky_gift_draws`, `live_boosts`, `user_bag_items`,
    `bag_transfers`, `premium_username_leases`, `premium_username_payments`, `recharge_sales`,
    `recharge_cherry_requests`, `agencies`, `agency_hosts`, `agency_earnings`, `agency_months`, `cherry_withdrawals`
    (amounts), `special_usernames` (system codes held for ever), reward, medal and live-room history rows, `reports`
    made or about the person; the `users` row stays the tombstone. One audit row per sweep,
    `account.deletion.retention_ended` (a count; no id).
  - **Usernames:** the regular username (the base one behind a special or premium username) is **quarantined**
    for `ACCOUNT_DELETION_USERNAME_QUARANTINE_DAYS` (90; owner confirmed 2026-10-31) — nobody can register or take it (only its SHA-256 is
    kept, `deleted_usernames`, with no link to the tombstone) — then the sweeper frees it. `coin…` / `host…` system
    codes are **never** released or reused (§10.48.1, §10.52: held for the tombstone forever); other special
    usernames end with their usual grace; a premium lease ends (its name returns to the pool by the D146 rules).
  - Audit `account.deletion.purged` (no username or email in it).
- **Without the app** (Google Play needs a web path): the person writes to `SUPPORT_EMAIL` (info@kabsolive.com)
  from the account's email address; the team checks it and runs `account-admin request <email> --reason …` (the
  same grace period and notices; planned web page `https://kabsolive.com/delete-account` with these steps).
- **CLI** `account-admin pending [<user>] | request | cancel | purge-now <user> --reason <text>` (migration role,
  audited with the reason, `via: cli`). `request` and `purge-now` refuse while a blocker stands. `holds --reason` and
  `hold-show <hold|report> --reason [--save <dir>]` read the legal holds (each view audited).
- **Settings:** `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS` (30, 1–90), `ACCOUNT_DELETION_USERNAME_QUARANTINE_DAYS` (90, 0–3650),
  `ACCOUNT_DELETION_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (3600; 0 off — refused in production), `SUPPORT_EMAIL`,
  `RATE_LIMIT_ACCOUNT_DELETION_USER` (5/900), `REPORT_LEGAL_HOLD_DAYS` (90, 1–3650), `DELETED_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS`
  (2557, 1–36500).
- **Migrations** `20270110090000_account_deletion_enums` (`user_status` `PENDING_DELETION`),
  `20270110100000_account_deletion` (`account_deletion_requests`, `deleted_usernames`),
  `20270110110000_account_deletion_retention` (`legal_holds`, `reports.legal_hold_id` and the `reports_one_target`
  rule for held reports, functions `account_deletion_scrub_audit` and `account_deletion_end_retention`).

### 10.57 The level ladder repriced; carried points keep every level *(v1.63-social, DRAFT — D194)*

Coins are cheap (retail 1 000 000 coins = $12.50, i.e. 80 000 coins per dollar), so the owner repriced the ladder
(option B). Multiplier 0.1 is unchanged (1 point per 10 coins); the step between one level and the next, per band:

| levels | coins per level | points per level | cumulative coins at the band's end | ≈ USD |
| ------ | --------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----- |
| 2–10 | 45 000 | 4 500 | 405 000 | 5.06 |
| 11–20 | 200 000 | 20 000 | 2 405 000 | 30.06 |
| 21–30 | 1 000 000 | 100 000 | 12 405 000 | 155.06 |
| 31–40 | 3 600 000 | 360 000 | 48 405 000 | 605.06 |
| 41–50 | 11 000 000 | 1 100 000 | 158 405 000 | 1 980.06 |
| 51–60 | 32 000 000 | 3 200 000 | 478 405 000 | 5 980.06 |
| 61–80 | 136 000 000 | 13 600 000 | 3 198 405 000 | 39 980.06 |
| 81–99 | 590 000 000 | 59 000 000 | 14 408 405 000 | 180 105.06 |
| 100 | 5 600 000 000 | 560 000 000 | 20 008 405 000 | 250 105.06 |

Level 100 = 2 000 840 500 points (BIGINT holds 9.2 × 10^18). The ladder serves the four categories — all four are
coin-valued (`valueUnit: COIN`): Charm (gifts received), Support (gifts sent), Wizard (lucky gifts sent), Gaming
(game spend). Charm's live-tap credit (§10.18, 1 point per 10 counted taps, at most 1 000 per viewer per live) is
not coin-valued and is unchanged; on the new ladder it is small.

- **Publication.** Publishing stays an admin action (CP-005 §4); because the owner ordered this ladder, migration
  `20270104090000_level_ladder_d194` publishes it **once** in every category as an audited system change
  (`audit_logs` `levels.version.create` + `levels.version.publish`, actor NULL, `via: migration`,
  `decision: D194`). The previous published version is archived; the on/off switch is not touched; open drafts stay
  drafts (listed as `openDrafts` in the audit row — a draft cannot be archived). `levels:admin draft-preset` and
  `publish-charm` write this ladder from now on.
- **Levels are kept (§10.43).** `user_level_states.carried_points` (BIGINT ≥ 0, not in the ledger) is set at every
  publish: with *n* the kept level, `carried = max(0, new(n) + inside − total)` where `inside` = the points the user
  had already made inside *n* on the old ladder (`total + old carried − old(n)`, clamped to 0 … new step − 1), and 0
  for whoever already reaches *n* on the new ladder. The level and the progress are measured on **level points =
  total + carried**; `total_points` stays Σ ledger.
- **Progress for a kept level.** The bar measures from the kept level's new threshold: level points − new(n) over
  new(n+1) − new(n); `pointsToNext` = new(n+1) − level points. Right after the switch someone at level 50 with 410
  points inside it shows 0.0 % and needs 3 200 000 − 410 points (32 000 000 coins − 4 100). A reversal below the
  carried base keeps the level and shows 0 % (as before).
- **Fraud.** A fraud deduction (§10.43) lowers the level to what the level points reach and takes the same share of
  the carry: `carried × after / before` (floored); a deduction of everything leaves nothing carried.
- **Contract.** `LevelSummary.carriedPoints` (PointsAmount, required, "0" while UNAVAILABLE or on another version).
  `points` is unchanged. The app shows level points and compacts amounts from a million (`15.8M`, `5.6B`;
  `15.8 مليون`, Latin digits, DESIGN_SYSTEM §3.3), a need rounded up.
- **Unchanged by design.** Support tiers and their 21 frames, charm medals, the room level and the task bands (the
  higher of Support and Charm, D176/D188) stay keyed to level numbers, so with the kept levels nobody loses a band
  or a frame; each tier is now worth more.

### 10.58 PK 1 v 1 «PK ثنائي» — battles between two hosts, the four boosters *(v1.43-live, DRAFT — D195, CP-038)*

Owner (2026-10-31, Arabic): «فعّل PK ثنائي ولا تنسَ التربل والدبل». Two hosts of **SOLO video** lives battle;
viewers of each room see both hosts side by side with the PK score bar (`KabsoPkBar`, D73). Every number
below is an **owner-confirmable default** (server config; D195 lists them).

- **Who.** A LIVE `SOLO` room of the caller with a fresh heartbeat whose host is present (not away, D170) —
  "eligible". `MULTI`, `AUDIO` and `PK`-mode rooms cannot start one (409 `PK_UNAVAILABLE`); `PK_ENABLED`
  (default true) switches new PKs and booster gifts off (409 `PK_UNAVAILABLE` / `PK_BOOSTER_UNAVAILABLE`).
  Room mode stays `SOLO` during a PK (the hub is unchanged in v1.43-live).
- **Starting.** (a) **Invite** (`inviteLivePk`): a host picks another live host (`listLivePkCandidates`:
  eligible, invitations on, not busy — v1.48-live (§10.70): a host waiting in the random queue is listed and
  may be invited — no block either way; `q` searches, otherwise the busiest lives). The
  invitation is open **`PK_INVITE_TTL_SECONDS` = 15**; the invited host accepts or declines; the inviter
  may cancel; **`PK_INVITE_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` = 10** between two invitations of a host (409
  `PK_INVITE_COOLDOWN`, `Retry-After`); rate limit 30 / 10 min. A host may switch invitations off
  (`setMyLivePk`, default on). (b) **Random** «مطابقة عشوائية» (`joinLivePkRandom`): one serialized queue;
  the host who waited longest with an eligible room and no block either way is paired at once, otherwise
  the caller waits **`PK_RANDOM_WAIT_SECONDS` = 60**. "Busy" (409 `PK_HOST_BUSY`): a BATTLE / RESULT match,
  an open invitation either way, or the random queue (the caller's own wait; since v1.48-live not the invited
  host's, §10.70). Blocked hosts (either way) are never listed, invited
  (404) or paired.
- **The match** (`PkMatch`): `BATTLE` for **`PK_BATTLE_SECONDS` = 300**, then `RESULT` for
  **`PK_RESULT_SECONDS` = 60** (the win / lose / draw animation and the top three supporters per side),
  then `CLOSED`. Side A is the inviter (or the host who waited longest). At most one open match per room
  (partial unique indexes plus advisory locks). End reasons: `TIME` (the higher score wins; equal → a
  **draw**), `FORFEIT` (a host ends early with `endLivePk`, or ends the live), `DISCONNECT` (the host's
  heartbeat stale, out of the media session, or the room ended otherwise, for
  **`PK_ABSENCE_GRACE_SECONDS` = 30**), `AWAY` (D170 away for 30 s) — the other side wins; both absent → a
  draw; `ADMIN` (a moderator, `pk-admin end <matchId> --reason`, audited `live.pk.admin_end`): **void** — no
  winner, not counted. `endLivePk` during `RESULT` closes it. Every change bumps `seq`.
- **Records.** `pk_host_records` (wins / losses / draws of finished, non-void matches) and the last 20
  matches with scores, duration, result and top supporters (`getLivePkHost`). Rewards are non-monetary and
  deferred.
- **Score = PK points**: the **real coin value** of every paid gift sent in that room during the battle
  (`live_gifts.total_coins`, any recipient — the host or a seated guest; lucky gifts their coin value; a free
  quip 0) × the side's **active booster multiplier**, stored per send in `pk_gift_points` (one row per
  send, so a retried send is never counted twice), the side's total in `pk_matches.score_a|b`, and per
  supporter in `pk_supporters`. **Multipliers affect only PK points**: the wallet charge, host earnings and
  cherries (D179), the live score, popularity boards, Contribution, charm and levels are written by the
  send exactly as without PK — from the real value. Gifts after `battleEndsAt` (before the tick ends the
  battle) count for nothing.
- **Boosters** (`PkBoosterKind`), each activated by **its own catalogue gift** (`Gift.pkBooster`,
  `gift-admin --pk-booster`, never LUCKY or QUIPS, never free; `gift-admin pk-boosters-seed` adds the four
  with the suggested prices):

  | Booster | Multiplier | Active | May start | Uses / side / match | Suggested gift price |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | «دبل» `DOUBLE` | ×2 | 30 s | any time | 2 | 5 000 coins (≈ $0.06) |
  | «دبل تيربو» `DOUBLE_TURBO` | ×3 | 20 s | last 120 s | 2 | 20 000 coins (≈ $0.25) |
  | «تربل» `TRIPLE` | ×5 | 20 s | last 60 s | 2 | 50 000 coins (≈ $0.63) |
  | «تربل تيربو» `TRIPLE_TURBO` | ×10 | 10 s | last 60 s | 2 | 150 000 coins (≈ $1.88) |

  (`PK_BOOSTER_MULTIPLIERS` `2,3,5,10`, `PK_BOOSTER_SECONDS` `30,20,20,10`, `PK_BOOSTER_WINDOWS` `0,120,60,60`,
  `PK_BOOSTER_LIMITS` `2,2,2,2`; prices are the gifts' own, `gift-admin update`.) A booster gift is sent to
  the host alone, quantity 1 (400 otherwise), during a battle; its own coin value counts as normal points
  (×1) and its multiplier applies from the next send for its duration. **One active booster per side**; a
  new one replaces the active one only when it is **higher** (the lower one ends at that moment). Refusals
  roll the whole send back, nothing charged: 409 `PK_BOOSTER_UNAVAILABLE` with detail `giftCode` /
  `no_match` (no battle, or PK off), `too_early` (outside its window), `limit_reached`, `active_higher`
  (an equal or higher one is active). Both rooms see «فعّل فريق X تربل ×5!» and a countdown chip on that
  side of the bar (`PkSideState.boost.endsAt`). The other owner tools (Fog, Freeze, Shield, Extra time,
  MVP, Quick strike, Steal, Crit) are **not** in v1.43-live and are not shown.
- **Real time.** Media data messages on topic **`pk`** to both rooms: `{type: "pk-match", event:
  started|score|boost|ended|closed|mute, match: PkMatch, boost?: {roomId, kind, multiplier, endsAt}}` (v1.55-live,
  D242: also `rematch-offer`, `rematch-cancelled`, `rematch-declined`, `rematch-expired` and `rematch`, §10.85) —
  state changes at once, score changes at most every **`PK_SCORE_BROADCAST_MS` = 500**; `{type:
  "pk-invite", invite}` to the invited host (and to the inviter when it is answered, cancelled or expires);
  `{type: "pk-queue", status: "EXPIRED"}` to a host whose wait ran out. Apps keep the highest `seq` and read
  `getLivePk` after joining, reconnecting or on a gap; the countdowns use `serverTime`. The server is the
  only authority; a **PK tick** (`PK_TICK_MS` = 1000, refused 0 in production) expires invitations and waits,
  ends battles (TIME and absences), closes result phases and announces moderator ends; every step is
  idempotent under the rows' state guards.
- **Media (design).** No new LiveKit room and no server-side forwarding: each viewer — and each host —
  opens a **second, subscribe-only, hidden connection to the other room's media session**
  (`createLivePkMediaToken`; identity `pk:<matchId>:<userId | guest:<guestId>>`, `canPublish` false). So
  each room keeps its own chat, gifts, seats and viewer list (the media webhook never records `pk:`
  identities as viewers: no count, no "joined" line; they are disconnected when the match closes or is not
  open), viewers hear both hosts, and the hosts hear each other through the same connection. The app
  ignores the other room's data messages on that connection. **Mute opponent** (`muteLivePkOpponent`):
  the host turns the other host's sound off for their own room (`PkSideState.mutesOpponent`; the app does
  not play it). Cost: one more participant per viewer in the other room (LiveKit participant minutes).
- **PK guests.** The SOLO seats 1–3 (D174) are the PK guests: the same request / accept / mute / remove
  flow; a 4th request → 409 `LIVE_SEAT_UNAVAILABLE`. `PkSideState.guests` lists them; the app draws them as
  small circles at the bottom of their host's half, glowing while they speak (the other room's guests come
  through the PK connection).
- **Not in v1.43-live:** PK 2 v 2, the other PK tools, rewards, a PK mark on the hub's cards, an admin
  HTTP route (the CLI only).

### 10.61 Privacy: data export, consents and legal documents *(v1.66-social, DRAFT — D198, CP-040)*

Kabso Live is a **global** app (owner): the EU/UK GDPR, California CCPA/CPRA, Brazil LGPD and the UAE and Saudi PDPL
apply. The controller is Kigofi LLC (Wyoming, USA), contact info@kabsolive.com. Code: `apps/api/src/modules/privacy/`
(`legal.ts` and `data-export.ts` are plain functions shared with the CLIs).

#### 10.61.1 «تنزيل بياناتي» — the personal-data export (GDPR Art. 15/20, CCPA right to know)

- **App:** Settings › Privacy › «تنزيل بياناتي» → what the copy holds, the 24-hour rule, the single 7-day download →
  the password again (`requestDataExport`, 403 `REAUTH_FAILED`, audited) → 202 PENDING. One export per
  `DATA_EXPORT_MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS` (24) per account, counted from the last non-FAILED request (429
  `DATA_EXPORT_LIMIT` + `Retry-After`, audited `privacy.export.limited`); two parallel requests make one job (advisory
  lock). Also allowed while consent is required (§10.61.2).
- **Job:** built after the response (`BackgroundTasks`) and, after a restart, by the sweeper
  (`DATA_EXPORT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 300; picks PENDING and RUNNING older than 15 min; three attempts, then FAILED,
  audited). The ZIP (in memory, DEFLATE, our own writer — no new dependency) holds `README.txt` (Arabic then English),
  `manifest.json` (sections and counts, rows cut at 50 000 per section are named) and `data/*.json`: `profile`,
  `settings`, `posts` (posts and reels, media as their public links), `stories`, `comments`, `messages` (sent and
  received while still kept — DMs expire after 24 h; the other person by public username only; attachments flagged, not
  included), `follows`, `blocks` (blocked and muted), `coins`, `cherries`, `levels` (ledgers), `gifts` (sent and
  received; counterparties by public username or «deleted»), `withdrawals` (payout details `…` + last 4; no admin
  note), `topups` (D190 orders without Stripe ids), `recharge_agent` (own KYC fields; the photo and selfie as
  `files/recharge-agent/<id>/*.webp` read from private storage), `consents` (incl. D190's terms text and the lucky
  gifts' 18+ date) and `devices` (sessions with the person's own IPs and user agents, push devices without tokens, the
  sign-in history from the audit log — action, time, IP only). Stored at `private/data-exports/<user>/<export>.zip`
  (`private, no-store`; the `private/` prefix is never public).
- **Never in it (tested):** the password hash, refresh-token hashes, verification and push tokens, TOTP secrets and
  recovery codes, admin notes and ids, payment-provider ids, fraud flags, early-fraud warnings, disputes, freezes,
  cases, audit metadata, other people's emails, ids or private data.
- **Ready:** READY with `expires_at` = ready + `DATA_EXPORT_LINK_DAYS` (7); a `DATA_EXPORT_READY` system notification (push
  «نسخة بياناتك جاهزة للتنزيل») and a mail. Like D193's notices the mail has **no link** (a phished copy must not hand
  over the data): it names the app path and the last day.
- **Download:** `createDataExportLink` mints a single-use token (only its SHA-256 kept; a new one replaces the old) →
  `GET /me/data-exports/{id}/file?token=` with the owner's bearer token: the token is consumed atomically (status
  DOWNLOADED) before the bytes are read, so a second request — even a racing one — gets 410
  `DATA_EXPORT_LINK_INVALID` (audited `privacy.export.download_refused` with the reason). The app saves the file to its
  own folder (Android: the app's external files folder; iOS: Documents).
- **Clean-up:** the sweeper marks READY exports past `expires_at` EXPIRED (audited) and deletes the files of
  DOWNLOADED, EXPIRED and FAILED jobs. D193's purge deletes the account's export rows and files.
- **Team (verified emailed request):** `privacy-admin exports [<user>]` (audited `privacy.export.admin_view`, never
  content) and `privacy-admin export <user> --reason <text>` (queues a job `via ADMIN`: the person gets the notification
  and mail and downloads in the app) or `… --save <dir>` (builds it now into a 600-mode file for the team to send by a
  secure channel; recorded as delivered). The 24-hour limit applies.

#### 10.61.2 Legal documents, consents and the 428 gate

- **`legal_documents`** (kind TERMS|PRIVACY, version, `effective_at`, `content_hash` = SHA-256 of the published page,
  url, summary ar/en). Written only by `legal-admin publish terms|privacy --version --effective --file --summary-ar
  --summary-en [--url]` (migration role, audited `legal.document.publish`; a version is never changed or removed). The
  version **in force** is the latest whose `effective_at` has passed (a future date is enforced from then on).
  `getLegalDocuments` (public, cached 60 s) lists them; the website shows the version and date from its
  `config.json` `documents.<kind>` (set to the same values when publishing).
- **`user_consents`** (user, document TERMS|PRIVACY|AGE_18|TOPUP_TERMS, version, accepted_at, `ip_truncated` — IPv4 /24,
  IPv6 /48 — user agent, method REGISTRATION|IN_APP|TOPUP_WEBSITE|LUCKY_GIFT). Recorded: at sign-up (`RegisterRequest.legal`
  kept on the pending registration, written at `register/verify`: AGE_18 `18+` and each named published version), on
  the consent screen (`acceptConsents`, audited), at each D190 top-up checkout (TOPUP_TERMS, the existing
  `topup_terms_acceptances` row is unchanged) and at the lucky gifts' first 18+ statement (AGE_18). D193's purge clears
  `ip_truncated` and `user_agent`; the rows are deleted with the tombstone's trail when its 7-year retention ends.
- **The gate** (`ConsentGuard`, a global guard after authentication and the rate limit): a signed-in caller who has not
  accepted every version in force gets **428 `CONSENT_REQUIRED`** (`details[]` per document) on every route except
  `@ConsentExempt()` ones — `getMyConsents`, `acceptConsents`, `logout`, `listSessions`, `revokeSession`, `getMe`,
  `DELETE /me/push-token`, `/me/account-deletion`, `/me/data-exports*`. Public routes, guests and the admin panel's
  cookie routes are not affected. Versions in force are cached 30 s per process and a user's "accepted" answer 10 min
  (positive answers only, keyed by the documents' ids), so a new version is enforced within 30 s and an acceptance at
  once. **Until the owner publishes the first versions nothing is required.**
- **App:** after a sign-in or restore the app reads `getMyConsents`, and any 428 sets the same flag: the router then
  keeps the person on «حدّثنا الشروط وسياسة الخصوصية» (each document's version, date, summary, «قراءة النص الكامل»,
  «أوافق وأتابع»; ways out: «تنزيل بياناتي», «حذف الحساب», «تسجيل الخروج»). Sign-up has a required checkbox «عمري 18
  عاماً أو أكثر، وأوافق على شروط الاستخدام وسياسة الخصوصية» with links to both pages.

#### 10.61.3 The website's privacy policy and cookies

`infra/deploy/site/privacy.html` (AR + EN) covers the controller, the EU/UK Art. 27 representative (`config.json`
`euRepresentative`, empty → «سيُضاف قريباً»), data categories, purposes and GDPR Art. 6 legal bases, processors
(Stripe, hosting — `hostingProvider`, LiveKit self-hosted, email — `emailProvider`, Firebase Cloud Messaging),
transfers to the USA (SCCs + UK Addendum / DPF), retention (account + 30-day grace; financial records anonymised 7
years; reported content 90-day legal hold; rejected KYC 90 days; waitlist until launch or unsubscribe), D193's
deletion paragraph, rights by region (GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA incl. «we do not sell or share», LGPD, UAE/Saudi PDPL)
and how to exercise them, children (18+ only), security, cookies and versioning. `/delete-account` is the web page
Google Play's Data-safety form needs. The site sets **no tracking cookies** (localStorage for the language, sessionStorage
for the settings: strictly necessary), so there is no banner; CI job `site` (`scripts/check-site-no-tracking.sh`) fails
when a tracker, cookie or third-party script is added — that needs a consent banner and a new policy version first.
The «مسودة — تحتاج مراجعة قانونية» banner stays until `legalReviewed` is true.

### 10.62 The PK Setting page, best of three, auto-start and auto match *(v1.44-live, DRAFT — D199)*

Owner «طبق تصميم 100%» (the PK sheet's gear → «PK Setting»). Extends §10.58; nothing there changes unless said here.

- **Settings** (`GET` / `PUT /me/live-pk`, `MyLivePk`; one row per host, no row = the defaults). `PUT` takes any of
  the fields (at least one, 400 otherwise); audited `live.pk.settings` with the fields that changed.
  | Field | Values (default) | Effect |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `mode` | `SINGLE` («Single Round PK») / `BEST_OF_THREE` (`SINGLE`) | see best of three below |
  | `roundMinutes` | 3 / 5 / 10, or null (null = `PK_BATTLE_SECONDS`, 300) | one round's time |
  | `autoStart` | on (on) | off: the match starts `CONNECTED` |
  | `randomGender` | `BOTH` / `MALE` / `FEMALE` (`BOTH`) | random queue only |
  | `randomRegion` | `GLOBAL` / `SAME_COUNTRY` (`GLOBAL`) | random queue only |
  | `autoMatch` | on / off (off) | the tick queues the host while live and idle |
  | `recommendable` | on / off (on) | off: left out of other hosts' suggestions |
  | `invitesEnabled` | (§10.58) | |
- **Whose settings.** `mode`, the round time and `autoStart` are copied into the match when it is created. Equal on
  both hosts → those (`settingsFromRoomId` null). Different → one host's, picked at random (crypto random), and
  `settingsFromRoomId` names that host's room (the app shows the owner's note «إذا اختلفت إعدادات المضيفَين يُختار
  إعداد أحدهما عشوائياً»).
- **Auto-start off → `CONNECTED`.** The hosts are connected (each room watches the other as in a battle: the media
  token and `pk:` watchers work) but there is no timer and no PK points; booster gifts are refused (`no_match`).
  `POST /live/rooms/{roomId}/pk/start` (either host; idempotent once running) starts round 1. `battleEndsAt` is the
  start deadline (`PK_CONNECT_SECONDS`, 300) while `CONNECTED`. A host's End, a host gone (the §10.58 absence rules)
  or the deadline → `CLOSED` at once with `endReason` `CANCELLED`: void, no result phase, never counted, not in the
  history. Data message events: `connected`, then `started`.
- **Best of three.** Each round lasts the round time and has its own scores (`score`), booster uses (limits per
  round) and multipliers (a running booster ends with its round). At the round's end the higher score wins it
  (equal: nobody). Two rounds won ends the match; after round 3 more rounds won, then more total points
  (`totalScore`, all rounds), else a draw. Between rounds the next one starts at once (event `round`). A forfeit,
  disconnect or absence in any round loses the whole match (§10.58). The supporters are the match's (all rounds).
- **Effective PK.** A finished match counts in the hosts' records only when both sides' PK points of every round
  together reach `PK_EFFECTIVE_MIN_POINTS` (default **3000 PK points**). Unit: PK points = gift coin value ×
  booster. The owner's reference says «charm value ≥ 3000»; Kabso's charm grows 1 : 1 with the coin value
  received, so with no booster 3000 PK points = 3000 charm. ADMIN and CANCELLED never count. `PkMatch.effective`,
  `PkHistoryItem.effective` (matches before D199: counted unless ADMIN). Shown on the page: «PK فعّال: نقاط
  الطرفين ≥ 3000».
- **Random queue preferences.** Both hosts' preferences must hold, each way. Gender: D175 `user_profiles.gender`; a
  host with no gender or `UNDISCLOSED` matches any preference. Region: D133 `country_code`; a host with
  `SAME_COUNTRY` and no country of their own is treated as `GLOBAL`; a partner with `SAME_COUNTRY` needs the caller's
  country to equal theirs.
- **Auto Match.** Every PK tick: hosts with `autoMatch` on whose SOLO video live is eligible (§10.58) and idle — no
  open match, no open invitation, not waiting, no PK of theirs closed in the last `PK_AUTO_MATCH_REST_SECONDS` (30)
  — join the random queue as with «مطابقة عشوائية». Turning it off leaves the queue.
- **Friends.** `listLivePkCandidates?friends=true`: only mutual follows (each follows the other: two `follows`
  rows; a pending follow request to a private account is not a follow). `recommendable` off hides a host from
  the suggestions (no `q`, no `friends`), not from a search. v1.48-live (§10.70): a friend waiting in the random
  queue is listed too.
- **Data Center** (`LiveRoomStats.giftGivers`): different people other than the host who sent a gift in the live.
  The app's live-data page reads `getLiveRoomStats` for the running live: «وقت البث» `durationSeconds`, «المشاهدون»
  **unique viewers** (`viewers.unique`; the peak is shown under it), «كرز جديد» `score.total` (the live's
  cherries), «الداعمون بالهدايا» `giftGivers`, «متابعون جدد» `newFollowers`.
- **The host's «تارجت»** (owner). `GET /live/hosts/{username}/targets` (anyone who can see the host; guests per
  IP): today's (Riyadh) cherries received from gifts against a cherries target, the coin value of lucky gifts
  received against a lucky target, and today's top three supporters — today only, never longer totals. The
  cherries target = the band target of «استقبل هدايا في بثك» (`P_HOST_GIFTS`, coins) × `CHERRIES_PER_COIN`
  (10) × the POPULAR host share (65 %), floored: 100 000 coins → 650 000 cherries. The lucky target = the
  band target of the new fixed daily host task «استقبل هدايا الحظ» (`HOST_LUCKY_COINS`, metric
  `HOST_LUCKY_COINS`: the coin value of received sends that have a stored lucky draw): bands 20 000 / 50 000
  / 100 000 / 200 000 coins, rewards 1 000 / 2 000 / 4 000 / 6 000 cherries (owner-confirmable; ≤ 0.5 % of
  the money behind the target, D188), inside the unchanged daily and monthly caps. The band: today's
  assignment's, else the level's now. A task switched off → target 0. `GET /me/host-gift-stats?period=DAY|
  WEEK|MONTH|ALL` is the caller's own: cherries (the ledger's `GIFT_RECEIVED` + `GIFT_REVERSAL`), gift
  sends, givers, top three and a bar series; lucky value, sends, givers and top three; DAY adds the targets.
- **D214 (owner): the chip is always shown.** Once `getLiveHostTargets` has answered (not while it loads; a 404
  — not a host, hidden — still shows nothing), every live (video, multi, audio, podcast; the host's screen and the
  viewer's) shows the «تارجت» chip beside «ترتيب الغرف» with both faces turning — 🍒 the cherries and the wizard
  hat the lucky value received today, «0» when nothing was — also when no target is set today (`target` 0). The
  check and the glow only when a target exists and is reached. The sheet shows the targets block only for a
  target that exists (no progress bar against 0). App only; no contract change.
- **The «تارجت» sheet as a ranking (D199b, owner «مطابق ١٠٠٪»).** The sheet becomes a contribution ranking, so the
  lists grow and carry what a row shows. Additive (older clients ignore the new fields):
  - `HostSupporter` gains `cherries` (the cherries the host got from that person's sends in the period: the
    ledger's `GIFT_RECEIVED` + `GIFT_REVERSAL` rows whose `reference_id` is the send) and `supportLevel` (their
    `SUPPORT` level number, null while that category is unavailable; the same rule as `LiveChatAuthorBadges`).
  - Every supporters list holds up to **20** (was 3). A cherries list (`topSupporters`) is ordered by
    `cherries` desc, then `coins` desc, then id; a lucky list (`lucky.topSupporters`, `luckySupporters`) by
    `coins` desc, then id.
  - `LiveHostTargets` gains `endsAt` (the end of the Riyadh day: the countdown), `luckySupporters` (today's
    lucky list) and `me`: for a signed-in caller who is not the host, their own place today in each list
    (`{cherries: {rank, amount}, lucky: {rank, amount}}`; `rank` null and `amount` 0 when they sent nothing;
    `amount` is cherries in the cherries list, coins in the lucky list); null for guests and for the host.
  - `HostGiftStats.to` is the end of the period (already sent): the host's countdown (none for ALL).

#### 10.62.1 Both targets in cherries: «هدف الهدايا» and «هدف هدايا الحظ» *(v1.69-live, DRAFT — D277)*

Owner (D277): the lucky target counts only lucky gifts, including those the host sends themself, and is measured in
cherries («لذلك اجعل الاهداف اكبر»). The cherries target becomes the gifts target «هدف الهدايا»: gifts outside the
lucky category, in cherries. The badges are replaced with art the owner will send. This supersedes the cherries and
lucky rules of §10.62 above.

- **What is counted.** Both targets read the cherry ledger: the host's `GIFT_RECEIVED` and `GIFT_REVERSAL` rows whose
  `reference_id` is the send, by the send's time, from ACTIVE senders. They count what was really credited (each send
  floored, net of reversals), never an estimate.
  - **«هدف الهدايا»** (`LiveHostTargets.gifts`; task `P_HOST_GIFTS`, metric `HOST_GIFT_CHERRIES`): every send OUTSIDE
    the lucky category (no stored lucky draw: normal, quips, event, fun…) from other people. The host's own sends do not
    count.
  - **«هدف هدايا الحظ»** (`LiveHostTargets.lucky`; task `HOST_LUCKY_COINS`, metric `HOST_LUCKY_CHERRIES`): lucky sends
    only, **the host's own sends to themself included**. D128 allows a host or a seated person to gift themself, a
    lucky gift too, under the same gates (coins, 18+, region); the API is unchanged. At the default
    `LUCKY_GIFT_HOST_SHARE_PERCENT` 10 %, a lucky coin gives the host 1 cherry.
- **Targets stored in cherries.** The band targets are now cherries and are compared as stored (no `cherriesForCoins` at
  read time). Migration `20270313090000_host_targets_cherries` converted the old coin targets at the default shares:
  `P_HOST_GIFTS` × 6.5 (100 000 / 250 000 / 500 000 / 1 000 000 coins → 650 000 / 1 625 000 / 3 250 000 /
  6 500 000), and the days' offers of it the same way. `HOST_LUCKY_COINS` × 1 (20 000 / 50 000 / 100 000 / 200 000;
  the code is kept because claims are keyed by it). Both were renamed «هدف الهدايا (بالكرز)» / «Gifts target
  (cherries)» and «هدف هدايا الحظ (بالكرز)» / «Lucky gifts target (cherries)». Rewards and caps are unchanged. The Task
  Center's progress for both tasks is the same number as the chip's.
- **Contract (additive).** `LiveHostTargets.gifts` (new); `cherries` is deprecated and is now the same as `gifts`. `lucky`
  keeps its name; its unit is now cherries (the same numbers at 10 % except for self-sends). `me.gifts` (new), with
  `me.cherries` the same and deprecated. `HostGiftStats.lucky.cherries` (new). `HostGiftStats.cherries` (received, sends,
  givers, list, series) is now «هدف الهدايا»'s: gifts outside the lucky category from other people.
  `ProgramTask.metric` gains `HOST_GIFT_CHERRIES` and `HOST_LUCKY_CHERRIES`; an older app shows them as unknown metrics.
  `AdminTasks.data[].targetUnit` is `COINS`, `CHERRIES` or null; a cherries target's `targetUsd` is at the payout rate.
  The panel labels the unit «كرز» / «عملة».
- **Supporters lists.** They rank other people only and never the host. The gifts list (`topSupporters`) ranks by the
  cherries of their non-lucky sends; the lucky list ranks by the coins of their lucky sends, as before. A host's own
  lucky sends count toward the lucky target but put nobody on a list.
- **App.** The chip and sheet say «هدف الهدايا» / «هدف هدايا الحظ» (tab «الهدايا» | «هدايا الحظ»). Each target's
  badge is drawn from a fixed asset slot: `assets/host_targets/gifts_target.png` and `lucky_target.png`. Until the owner's
  art arrives, they hold stand-ins (the Kabso cherry and the D199 wizard hat), with a PROVENANCE note; replacing a file
  swaps the badge with no code change. A missing file falls back to the same art drawn in code. The app reads `gifts`,
  or `cherries` from an older server.

#### 10.62.2 Smart daily targets «الأهداف الذكية»: three levels, a generated catalogue, a profit-share reward *(v1.71-live, DRAFT — D281)*

Owner (D281): a huge, varied catalogue of host targets (more than 100 000, generated from templates × parameters);
three targets per host per day — easy / medium / hard («سهل / متوسط / صعب») — chosen automatically from the host's own
data; the reward is SEPARATE from the Task Center: a share of the PLATFORM PROFIT the target produced (1.5 % / 2.5 % /
4 %), paid in locked task cherries, so a big reward only appears when the host made very good profit. The owner asked
«كيف يتم تقسيم المهام والاهداف للشخص اوتماتيكياً بحيث ان النظام ذكي يقرأ بيانات ثم يوزع»: the answer is the algorithm
below. This replaces §10.62.1's two fixed band targets from the engine's first day (below); §10.62.1 still describes the
day of the switch and the amounts `gifts` / `lucky` received.

- **The catalogue (generated, never hand-written rows).** A target is *kind × amount × window of the day × (one gift /
  one category)*, with the code `T.<kind>.<subject|*>.<amount>.<from>-<to>` (minutes of the host's day):
  - kinds — `GIFT_CHERRIES` (cherries credited for gifts outside the lucky category from other people, «هدف
    الهدايا»), `LUCKY_CHERRIES` (cherries of lucky gifts, the host's own sends included, «هدف هدايا الحظ»),
    `GIFT_COUNT` (how many of ONE gift: «استقبل 100 هدية من المحارب»), `CATEGORY_COUNT` (how many gifts of one
    category), `SUPPORTERS` (different people who sent a gift), `GIFT_SENDS` (gifts received), `COMBO` (the biggest
    combo of one send streak) and `GIFT_COMBO` (the biggest combo of one gift). The host's own sends count only for
    `LUCKY_CHERRIES` (D277); senders must be ACTIVE; everything is read from stored sends and the cherry ledger;
  - amounts — cherries: 15 round steps a decade from 1 000 to 900 000 000 (90); counts: 40 steps 1 … 10 000;
    supporters: 20 steps 1 … 100; combos: 20 customary sizes 5 … 9 999;
  - windows — the whole day + every window of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 8 hours starting on the hour (147), e.g. «tonight
    20:00–24:00»;
  - gifts and categories — the ENABLED paid gifts of enabled categories, read at each assignment: a gift added or
    switched off adds or removes its targets at once (the catalogue version changes).
  Size: 38 220 targets without gifts + 8 820 per paid gift + 5 880 per category — **235 200** for 19 gifts in 5
  categories, 149 940 for 10 gifts. The panel shows the live counts.
- **The assignment («يقرأ بيانات ثم يوزع»).** At the host's first read of the day (the chip, the sheet, the panel never)
  the server reads their last `history_days` days (default 30; not today), per day: cherries and coins from gifts and
  from lucky gifts, gifts received, different supporters, the biggest combo, minutes live and cherries per hour, gifts
  by code; their usual live hours; average viewers; their band (the Task Center's level band); how many of their
  targets of the last `history_days / 2` days were completed; the codes of the last `no_repeat_days` days. Then,
  deterministically for the host and the day (a seeded generator — the same picks on every read and server):
  1. **New host** (fewer than 3 active days): the band's defaults — easy «gifts received», medium «different
     supporters», hard «cherries from gifts» (band 1…4: 20 000 / 60 000 / 150 000 cherries … 600 000 / 2 000 000 /
     5 000 000).
  2. **Candidates** from what the host's data supports, each with its value on every active day: cherries from gifts
     (weight by its share of their cherries), cherries from lucky gifts, the same in their usual hours (when ≥ 60 % of
     their cherries come in a 2–4 hour window), the gifts they get on ≥ 30 % of active days (a count of that gift), their
     top category, supporters (when they average ≥ 2), combos (median ≥ 5), gifts received.
  3. **Kinds mixed:** HARD is always a cherries target (the biggest share of profit only for real profit); MEDIUM and
     EASY are drawn by weight from the other kinds (a kind not drawn yet first).
  4. **Calibration:** each level aims at a percentile of the candidate's daily values — **easy ≈ the 50th** (a typical
     day), **medium ≈ the 75th** (a good day), **hard ≈ the 90th** (their best days) — moved by the completion rate:
     with ≥ 3 targets in the look-back, (rate − 0.5) × 2 × `completion_shift` points (default ±10: always finishing →
     +10, harder; never → −10, easier). The value is snapped UP to the kind's ladder; two levels of the same kind grow
     strictly.
  5. **No repeat:** a code given in the last `no_repeat_days` (default 7) moves one ladder step (easy tries one down
     first).
  6. Stored in `host_target_assignments` with the reasons («لماذا هذا الهدف»: the percentile used, the completion rate
     and adjustment, the host's value at the percentile, 7- and 30-day averages, the best day, a sentence in Arabic and
     English) and the catalogue version. Fixed for the day; the knobs change only later days.
- **The economics (one unit-tested function, `platformProfitUnits`, from the configuration).** Per send (the recipient's
  part): **a normal gift** — the coins PAID (`coins_charged` share; a bag gift or a free quip earns nothing now) at
  `COIN_RETAIL_USD_PER_MILLION` − the host's cherries at `CHERRY_PAYOUT_RATE`; **a lucky gift** — the coins paid − the
  expected payout (`LUCKY_GIFT_RTP_PERCENT` × the coin value) − the host's cherries. Exact integers (micro-cents ×
  the payout rate's cherries). At the owner's numbers (1 000 000 coins = $12.50, 1 000 000 cherries = $1.10, 10 cherries
  a coin, shares 65 % / 50 % / 10 %, RTP 75 %): 1 000 000 coins of normal gifts → $12.50 − $7.15 = **$5.35**; of quips →
  $12.50 − $5.50 = $7.00; of lucky gifts → $12.50 − $9.375 − $1.10 = **$2.025**. Agency and parent commissions (extra
  cherries to the agencies, §10.46: 15–16 % + 3 % of the host's cherries by default) are not subtracted — the owner's
  formula; with them the platform still keeps ≈ $3.99 (normal) and ≈ $1.82 (lucky) per 1 000 000 coins, far above the 4 %
  share.
- **The reward.** Shown before completion on each target (`HostDailyTarget.rewardCherries`): the level's share
  (`reward_bps`: 150 / 250 / 400) of the profit the NOMINAL amount stands for — a cherries target's coins at the highest
  normal share (or the lucky share), a count target's coin value (the gift's price; the host's own coins per supporter /
  per gift for the others). *Worked example:* hard «3 000 000 cherries from gifts» → 461 538 coins = $5.769 in, $3.30 to
  the host → profit **$2.469** → 4 % = $0.0988 = **89 790 cherries** (easy 1.5 % would be 33 671, medium 2.5 % 56 118). A
  lucky «200 000 cherries» → 200 000 coins: $2.50 − $1.875 − $0.22 = $0.405 → 4 % = 14 727 cherries (at RTP 85 %: $0.155 →
  5 636). **Guard (owner):** the payment is `min(shown, the level's share of the ACTUAL profit of the sends the target
  counted)` — never of the nominal; a loss pays 0.
- **Payment.** When a read (the host's, a viewer's, a guest's) sees a target reached, it is paid at once, once: the
  assignment row is locked, `completed_at`, `progress`, `profit_microcents`, `paid_cherries`, `paid_at` are set and a
  cherry ledger row `HOST_TARGET_REWARD` (reference `HT:<level>@<day>`, unique per host) is written in the same
  transaction, audited `host_targets.reward` {host, day, level, code, progress, profitUsd, shown, paid}. The next read
  also settles yesterday's targets reached after the last read. The reward is **locked like task cherries** (§10.46.1:
  not withdrawable, not spendable in the store or sellable until the unlock rule passes; counted in
  `CherryWallet.lockedTaskCherries`). It is outside the Task Center's daily and monthly caps (its own cap is the profit).
- **The switch.** Migration `20270315090100_host_target_engine` leaves `engine_from` empty; the API's first read sets it
  to the NEXT day. Today keeps D277's two targets with their progress and Task Center rewards; from the next day the
  smart engine runs, the fixed «هدف هدايا الحظ» task (`HOST_LUCKY_COINS`) and the pool's `P_HOST_GIFTS` are no longer
  Task Center tasks, and `LiveHostTargets.daily` holds the three targets.
- **Contract (additive).** `LiveHostTargets.daily` (`HostDailyTarget`: `level`, `code`, `kind`, `title` in the caller's
  `Accept-Language`, `amount`, `progress`, `reached`, `rewardCherries`, `rewardBps`, `paidCherries`, `locked`, `window`,
  `gift` (`TaskGift`: code, name, assetKey, imageUrl), `category`); from the engine's first day `gifts.target` /
  `lucky.target` are the whole-day cherries targets among the three (else 0), for older apps. `CherryLedgerReason`
  `HOST_TARGET_REWARD`. Panel (OWNER only): `getAdminHostTargetSettings` / `updateAdminHostTargetSettings` (the
  percentiles 50 / 75 / 90, the shares 150 / 250 / 400 bps ≤ 2 000, `noRepeatDays` 7, `taskNoRepeatDays` 3,
  `historyDays` 30, `completionShift` 10; easy < medium < hard kept; a reason; audited `host_targets.settings.update`
  with before / after), `getAdminTargetCatalogue` (targets by kind, tasks by template), `getAdminHostTargets` (a host's
  day with «لماذا هذا الهدف»; audited `host_targets.view`). Capabilities `host_targets.view` / `host_targets.edit`.
- **App.** The chip turns through the three targets («سهل / متوسط / صعب», progress) and the sheet lists them with the
  level, the progress, the reward («+89,790 🍒 مقفل») and, when paid, «تم ✓». A gift target shows the gift's picture and
  name; cherries targets keep the gift-box badge (`assets/host_targets/gifts_target.png`) and lucky ones the lucky badge.

- **D281b (owner, on the sheet's golden): two tracks of three.** «هذه كلها اهداف هدايا ولا يوجد اهداف لهدايا الحظ»:
  every host now has **six** targets a day — three on «الهدايا» (track GIFTS) and three on «هدايا الحظ» (track LUCKY),
  each easy / medium / hard, each track assigned by the same algorithm from **its own** history (P50 / P75 / P90 ± the
  completion shift of that track's targets, no repeat in 7 days, new-host defaults per track). The GIFTS track counts only
  gifts outside the lucky category from other people (`GIFT_SENDS`, `SUPPORTERS`, `COMBO` no longer count lucky gifts);
  the LUCKY track has its own kinds — `LUCKY_CHERRIES`, `LUCKY_GIFT_COUNT` (one lucky gift), `LUCKY_SENDS`,
  `LUCKY_SUPPORTERS` (never the host), `LUCKY_COMBO`; the host's own lucky sends count as in D277 (except as a
  supporter). HARD is always the track's cherries kind. The reward is the same 1.5 / 2.5 / 4 % of the **lucky** profit
  (after the expected payout, `platformProfitUnits`) with the same guard, locked cherries; ledger reference
  `HT:LUCKY:<level>@<day>` (the gifts track keeps `HT:<level>@<day>`). Catalogue (12 kinds): 49 980 targets without gifts
  + 8 820 per paid gift outside the lucky category + 5 880 per paid lucky gift + 5 880 per category — 229 320 for 15 + 4
  gifts in 4 categories. `HostDailyTarget.track`; `LiveHostTargets.daily` holds six (gifts, then lucky). Migration
  `20270315090200_host_target_tracks` (`track` column, primary key `(user_id, day, track, level)`, the kinds CHECK).
  - **Marks** (owner, corrected the same day «اجعله يعرض صورة الهدية ان كان الهدف هدف هدية محددة»): a target about ONE
    gift (a gift count or combo of it, either tab) shows that gift's **current hosted art** (`gift.imageUrl` from the
    catalogue); every other «الهدايا» target the gift-box badge (`assets/host_targets/gifts_target.png`); every other
    «هدايا الحظ» target the lucky badge (`lucky_target.png`).
  - **Chip:** it turns through all six (the three gift targets, then the three lucky ones — each face's mark tells its
    tab), so the host sees both without opening the sheet; under reduced motion one compact face per tab (its badge and
    how many of its three are reached, «1/3»). **Sheet:** the active tab's three.
- **Real prices (owner: «الاسعار التي قمنا بوضعها وهمي وقليلة»).** Today's gift prices are placeholders and low. Nothing is
  tied to them: the ladders are log-scaled and far above them (cherries 1 000 … 900 000 000, counts 1 … 10 000, combos
  to 9 999); amounts come only from the host's own history (cherries and counts), so they move with prices by
  themselves; a gift count is also capped by the coins the host gets on such a day at the gift's **current** price
  (fewer of an expensive gift, more of a cheap one; the reason shows `priceCap`), and its expected coins use that price;
  rewards are profit-based. The **new-host defaults** (hosts with fewer than 3 days on a track) are OWNER-editable in the
  panel (`newHostDefaults`: per kind `GIFT_SENDS`, `SUPPORTERS`, `GIFT_CHERRIES`, `LUCKY_SENDS`, `LUCKY_SUPPORTERS`,
  `LUCKY_CHERRIES`, per band 1…4: [easy, medium, hard], easy ≤ medium ≤ hard; audited; null = the code's values): raise
  them when the real prices are set.

### 10.63 The host's live tools: two cameras, music and the clip recorder *(v1.45-live, DRAFT — D201)*

Owner: the D199 Room Tools «كاميرتان», «موسيقى» and «التسجيل» stop being «قريباً». Nothing in §10.58 / §10.62 changes.

- **Second camera («كاميرتان»).** A second phone or tablet of the **same account** publishes a second camera into
  the host's LIVE **SOLO** video live.
  - *Pairing.* On the main device `createLiveSecondCameraCode` gives a 6-digit code, **single use**, valid
    `LIVE_SECOND_CAMERA_CODE_SECONDS` (120), bound to the account (only `HMAC(account:code)` is stored, the code is
    never logged); a new code replaces the open one; one open code per live (partial unique index). On the second
    device the host opens «الانضمام ككاميرا ثانية» and enters it: `redeemLiveSecondCameraCode`. Unknown, expired,
    used, replaced and other-account codes all answer 422 `SECOND_CAMERA_CODE_INVALID`; every refusal is audited
    `live.second_camera.refused` with the reason (`unknown` / `expired` / `used` / `unavailable` / `busy`).
  - *Token.* Identity `cam2:<hostUserId>`; joins that room only; `canPublishSources` camera and microphone (the app
    starts with the microphone off); `canSubscribe` false; no data; 600 s to connect. The participant attribute
    `kabso.mainFeed` (`HOST` / `SECOND`) is the default main feed (`setLiveSecondCameraMain`, audited).
  - *One at a time, not during a PK.* A second redemption while a camera is active → 409 `SECOND_CAMERA_BUSY`
    (partial unique index); a code or redemption during a PK (a match not CLOSED) → 409 `SECOND_CAMERA_UNAVAILABLE`;
    a PK starting while a camera is on ends it (`end_reason` PK) at the next media reconciliation and removes the
    second device; the app ends it at once on the main device.
  - *Never a viewer.* The webhook (and the reconciliation) treat `cam2:` like `pk:`: no `live_room_viewers` row, no
    visit, no join announcement, no viewer count. A `cam2:` participant is removed unless it is the live's host's
    redeemed camera in a LIVE SOLO room without a PK. It leaving ends the camera (`LEFT`) — *(D243)* unless the
    media server still lists that identity (a reconnect replaced the old session), and a camera that left
    (`LEFT`, never `REVOKED` / `EXPIRED` / `PK`) is open again when the same identity joins within 60 s and no other
    camera was paired meanwhile (LiveKit's full reconnect: the old session's `participant_left` first); ending the
    live ends the code and the camera (`ROOM_ENDED`, the media room is closed); `endLiveSecondCamera` (either
    device) ends both (`REVOKED`) and removes the second device. A redeemed camera that never connected expires after 600 s.
  - *Layout (the app).* Viewers and the host see the main feed full screen and the other camera as a small
    draggable picture; tapping it swaps them **on that screen only**; the default follows `kabso.mainFeed`. During a
    PK the stage shows the host's camera only. When the second device leaves, the small picture disappears.
    *(D243)* The small picture carries a swap icon. The second device keeps its screen on while it joins and is on
    air, holds the live's foreground service (type microphone, as a seated guest) and, while the app is in the
    background, mutes its camera the LiveKit way (the small picture goes; never a frozen frame) and restarts it on
    return; a LiveKit reconnect is not an end.
- **Music («موسيقى»).** The host picks audio files on the phone; the app mixes them **into its own microphone track**
  (after echo cancelling and noise suppression, at the music volume, lowered while the host speaks), so viewers
  hear voice + music from the one track — no new source or token change. Before the first music the app shows the
  rights notice «تأكد أنك تملك حقوق تشغيل الموسيقى. يُمنع تشغيل موسيقى محمية بحقوق النشر بدون ترخيص.» and stores the
  acceptance once per account: `acceptMyLiveMusicRights` (`noticeVersion` 1; `live_music_rights_acceptances`; audited
  `live.music.rights_accept` the first time). Nothing plays by itself. The server never receives the files.
- **Clip recorder («التسجيل»).** The host's phone records its own published camera and microphone for at most
  **60 s** (nothing is uploaded unless the host posts it as a reel, §11.14). While recording the app calls
  `setLiveRecording` `{active: true}`: the host's participant attribute `kabso.recordingUntil` = now + 61 s, so
  every viewer shows «يتم التسجيل» until then or until `{active: false}` removes it. Audited `live.recording.start` /
  `.stop`. An AUDIO room → 400.

### 10.64 Recharge orders with escrow «طلبات الشحن» *(v1.69-social, DRAFT — D204)*

The owner's flow (2026-10-31) on top of D185's direct selling, which stays as it is: the **buyer** asks an agent for
coins, the agent sends where to pay, the buyer pays **outside the app** and says so with the transfer's screenshot,
and the agent confirms. From the payment details until the agent's «استلمت» (or an admin's decision) the coins are
**frozen** from the agent's stock, so the buyer never pays for coins the agent no longer has. No money passes
through Kabso (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS). Statuses:

```
REQUESTED ──details──▶ AWAITING_PAYMENT ──«قمت بالإرسال»──▶ PAID ──«استلمت»──▶ COMPLETED
   │ cancel (either)         │ cancel (buyer) / 60 min            │ «نزاع» (agent any time,
   │ 30 min ▶ EXPIRED        ▼   ▶ CANCELLED / EXPIRED (released) │  buyer after 15 min)
   ▼                                                              ▼
CANCELLED                                               DISPUTED ──admin──▶ COMPLETED_BY_ADMIN | REFUNDED_TO_AGENT
```

PAID never expires and never releases by itself: only «استلمت» or an admin's decision moves its coins.
`RECHARGE_ORDERS_ENABLED=false` → 503 `RECHARGE_ORDERS_UNAVAILABLE` (`RechargeRules.orders.enabled` tells the app,
which then hides the order entry; direct selling is not affected). The app also hides the agent flow in store builds
(D150, `KABSO_STORE_BUILD`), until legal confirms.

#### 10.64.1 The price and the exchange rates

`coins` × the **retail** price (`COIN_RETAIL_USD_PER_MILLION`, owner $12.50 per 1 000 000) in US cents rounded half
up; the agent's wholesale tiers (§10.48) are never the buyer's price. When OWNER / FINANCE set an exchange rate for
the country (`recharge_exchange_rates`: currency, units per 1 USD × 1 000 000, decimals 0–3; panel «أسعار الصرف» or
`recharge-admin set-rate`, audited with before/after and the reason) the local amount is shown too, rounded half up
in the currency's decimals; without a rate the country is USD only. USD is always shown. The price — USD, currency,
rate and local amount — is **stored with the order at creation**; a later rate change never touches it.
`RECHARGE_ORDER_MIN_COINS` (10 000) … `RECHARGE_ORDER_MAX_COINS` (1 000 000 000) per order.

*v1.81-social (D245):* a row of `recharge_exchange_rates` is now the **manual** rate «يدوي»; without one the country
uses the **automatic** rate of its currency (§10.87). Clearing a manual rate is «إعادة إلى التلقائي».

#### 10.64.2 Creating an order

The buyer picks the country (default `Me.country`), an ACTIVE agent there (`listRechargeAgents?country=`), the
coins and one of the agent's payment-method **types** for that country. Refused: yourself, an employee of that agent,
a block either way (404), a type the agent does not offer there, a stock that does not cover the coins now (a hint;
the authoritative check is at the details), and a second open order for the same buyer and agent (unique partial
index; 409 `RECHARGE_ORDER_OPEN_EXISTS`). `Idempotency-Key` per buyer. The order starts REQUESTED with
`expiresAt` = now + `RECHARGE_ORDER_REQUEST_TTL_MINUTES` (30).

#### 10.64.3 The order's chat

Every order has its own thread `recharge_order_messages` — not a direct conversation (§11.13): it is evidence and is
never edited or deleted by a participant (it goes only with the order). Kinds: TEXT (≤ 1000, line breaks kept),
IMAGE and TRANSFER_PROOF (a private `RECHARGE_ORDER_IMAGE` upload consumed into
`private/recharge-orders/<order>/<message>.webp`, re-encoded with the metadata stripped, `private, no-store`; read
only through `getRechargeOrderMessageImage` by the buyer, the agent and the agent's employees, and through the panel
by admins — each admin view audited), PAYMENT_DETAILS (method + details) and SYSTEM lines for every state change
(`event`). The order is `seq`-ordered. Roles: BUYER, AGENT, EMPLOYEE, ADMIN («الإدارة»: no name, no author), SYSTEM.
Writing is closed on CANCELLED / EXPIRED orders; it stays open on DISPUTED and decided ones. Each event and message
updates one unread `RECHARGE_ORDER_UPDATE` notification per order and person (system type: a block never hides an
order's state), pushed through the outbox (§11.12).

#### 10.64.4 The payment details freeze the coins

The agent, or an employee **on shift** (§10.48: else 409 `RECHARGE_OFF_SHIFT`; employees read at any time; *v1.87-social,
D287*: the first person of the agent's side to act owns the order — §10.100), sends
`method` (one of the agent's types there) and `details`. In one transaction on the locked order: the order's coins
leave the stock (`recharge_stock_ledger` `ORDER_HOLD`, conditional UPDATE: 409 `RECHARGE_STOCK_INSUFFICIENT` and
nothing changes when the stock is short), `held_coins` = coins, AWAITING_PAYMENT, `expiresAt` = now +
`RECHARGE_ORDER_PAYMENT_TTL_MINUTES` (60). An ACTIVE agent only.

#### 10.64.5 The protection notice and «قمت بالإرسال»

The app shows the buyer the owner's notice as a prominent card that must be acknowledged
(`acknowledgeRechargeOrderNotice`, recorded once with a system line) before «قمت بالإرسال» is enabled (409
`RECHARGE_ORDER_NOTICE_REQUIRED` otherwise):

> «يرجى أخذ لقطة شاشة وتسجيل فيديو للشاشة منذ لحظة مغادرة المحادثة وحتى وصول الحوالة إلى المعلومات التي قدّمها
> الوكيل، لحمايتكم من أي خطأ أو احتيال. عند التحويل أرسل لقطة شاشة للحوالة واحتفظ بفيديو الشاشة حتى تصلك العملات.»
>
> "Please take a screenshot and record a screen video from the moment you leave this chat until the transfer reaches
> the details the agent gave you, to protect you from any mistake or fraud. When you transfer, send a screenshot of
> the transfer and keep the screen video until your coins arrive."

«قمت بالإرسال» needs the transfer's screenshot (`proofUploadId`) → PAID, `paidAt`, no expiry; `disputeOpensAt` =
`paidAt` + `RECHARGE_ORDER_DISPUTE_AFTER_MINUTES` (owner 15). Both sides see the countdown to it.

#### 10.64.6 «استلمت»

On PAID, the agent's side (with a confirmation in the app): the frozen coins go to the buyer's wallet
(`wallet_ledger` `RECHARGE_ORDER`, reference the order; the daily recharge badge counts them, §10.50) → COMPLETED.
The stock already left at the hold, so no stock row is written here; the hold row and the credit row share the
order's id. Idempotent (COMPLETED again → 200, nothing moves).

#### 10.64.7 «نزاع»

On PAID: the agent at any time («لم يصلني»), the buyer from `disputeOpensAt` (409
`RECHARGE_ORDER_DISPUTE_TOO_EARLY` before) → DISPUTED (`disputedBy`). The coins stay frozen, both sides keep adding
evidence, and admins may now open the order. Again → 200, no change.

#### 10.64.8 Cancellations, expiries and races

The buyer cancels REQUESTED or AWAITING_PAYMENT, the agent's side REQUESTED only; after the details the hold goes
back (`ORDER_RELEASE`, once per order — unique `(agent, reason, reference)`). A sweeper
(`RECHARGE_ORDER_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 60; 0 refused in production; `recharge-admin expire-orders`) expires due
REQUESTED / AWAITING_PAYMENT orders (releasing the hold); every read and action applies a due expiry first. Every
transition locks the order row (`FOR UPDATE`) and re-checks the status, so of confirm, dispute, cancel, expiry and an
admin's decision exactly one wins; the loser gets 409 `RECHARGE_ORDER_STATE_CHANGED` and nothing moves. A CHECK keeps
`held_coins` ∈ {0, coins} and > 0 exactly in AWAITING_PAYMENT / PAID / DISPUTED.

#### 10.64.9 The panel «نزاعات الشحن»

Capabilities (§10.54.1): `recharge.disputes` (OWNER, SUPPORT, FINANCE; MODERATION since D275) — the queue (DISPUTED oldest first; decided
newest first), the order with its whole chat and pictures (each view audited `recharge.order.admin_view` /
`recharge.order.image_view`, actor, IP, `via: panel`), and «الإدارة» lines in the chat (`recharge.order.admin_message`;
users never see the admin's name); `recharge.disputes.resolve` (OWNER, FINANCE and, D275 (owner), MODERATION — the moderator's only coin movement) —
the decision with a reason and the authenticator code again (§10.54.3): `CREDIT_BUYER` → COMPLETED_BY_ADMIN (wallet
`RECHARGE_ORDER`) or `REFUND_AGENT` → REFUNDED_TO_AGENT (stock `ORDER_RELEASE`), through `resolveDisputeIn` — the rule
of `recharge-admin resolve` — audited with before/after, the reason, actor, IP and `via`; both sides notified. The same
decision again → `changed: false`; any other → 409 `ADMIN_ACTION_REFUSED`. An order that was never disputed is 404 in
the panel. `recharge.rates` (OWNER, FINANCE) changes the exchange rates; `recharge.agents` reads them.

### 10.65 «افتح وكالة»: a self-opened host agency, its ID check and the 7-day probation *(v1.70-social, DRAFT — D206)*

Owner decisions (2026-10-31, Arabic, via the coordinator) are marked *(owner)*; every number is server config with the
owner's value as default. Nothing in §10.46 / §10.52 changes for the agencies the team makes.

- **Who and what** *(owner)*. In «الوكالة», a person in no agency keeps «انضم إلى وكالة» and gets «افتح وكالة» under
  it. Opening is **free**. The form: the agency's name (2–40 characters), the country (ISO alpha-2), a contact method
  (`WHATSAPP` / `TELEGRAM` / `PHONE` / `EMAIL` / `OTHER` + 3–100 characters), the expected number of hosts (1–10 000), a
  short bio (≤ 300, line breaks allowed) and the **mandatory identity check** — a photo of the ID card and a selfie,
  as the recharge agents' D185 flow exactly: pending private uploads of kinds `RECHARGE_AGENT_PHOTO` (the ID card) and
  `RECHARGE_AGENT_SELFIE`, consumed by `openAgency` into `private/agency-applications/{applicationId}/…` (`private,
  no-store`, never a public URL), never completed, never in a response or the audit trail.
- **Created at once** *(owner)*. No approval: `openAgency` makes the agency with the same step as `economy-admin
  agency-create` (`createAgencyIn`): an invite code, the owner's host-agent code `hostNN` (§10.52: the username, frame,
  badge, entrance — a refused grant, e.g. a rented premium username, keeps the code reserved), rank `NEW` with the D179
  grace (evaluated from the month start two months after the creation month), no parent; `origin` `SELF`, the `name`
  and `probationEndsAt` = now + `AGENCY_PROBATION_DAYS` (7). The application row (`agency_applications`) is kept with
  the agency for the team. The owner gets `AGENCY_OPENED`. `Idempotency-Key`: the same key with the same body → 200
  (nothing new), with another body → 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.
- **Refusals** — 409 `AGENCY_OPEN_NOT_ALLOWED` with the reason (`MyAgency.openRule` shows it before): `OWNS_AGENCY`
  (an open agency, in probation or not), `HOST_OF_AGENCY` (an ACTIVE host of an agency — leave it first),
  `REOPEN_COOLDOWN` (the person's agency closed less than `AGENCY_REOPEN_COOLDOWN_DAYS` (30, *proposal*) ago),
  `ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE`; rate limit `RATE_LIMIT_AGENCY_OPEN_USER` (5 per 24 h, refused attempts count).
- **Activated host — the one rule** *(owner: «يفعل ٣ مضيفين … فتح لايف و استلام هدايا»)*. At an instant `at`, a host is
  activated when one of their links to the agency was a membership at `at` (`activated_at < at`, not ended before
  `at`) and, in that link's window `[activated_at, at)`, they **started a live of their own** (`live_rooms.started_at`)
  **and received a gift** (a `GIFT_RECEIVED` cherry-ledger row with no `GIFT_REVERSAL` for it). Lives and gifts before
  joining never count. A probation is judged at `min(now, probationEndsAt)`: **anything at or after `probationEndsAt`
  — a join, a live, a gift — does not count**, and a sweep that runs late decides exactly as an on-time one.
- **Passing.** As soon as `AGENCY_PROBATION_MIN_HOSTS` (3) hosts are activated the probation passes — at the next sweep
  or on any `getMyAgency` of the owner (the same locked step) — `probationPassedAt`, `AGENCY_PROBATION_PASSED`. From
  then on the D179 rank and grace rules apply unchanged.
- **Probation and the NEW grace.** The probation (7 days) lies inside the NEW grace (≥ 1 month). While it runs the
  rank evaluator leaves the agency alone (it stays `NEW`, not even promoted); after it passes the agency is evaluated
  like any other from its `evaluateFrom` (counted from the creation, not from the passing). The probation is the only
  test in its first days; the grace is the only protection after.
- **Failing** *(owner)*. A sweep at or after `probationEndsAt` with fewer activated hosts closes the agency: status
  `CLOSED`, `close_reason` `PROBATION_FAILED`, the count kept (`probation_activated`). Its ACTIVE hosts are
  **released free** (`RELEASED`, as if they had left; an open complaint resolved) and each gets
  `AGENCY_HOST_RELEASED`; the owner gets `AGENCY_CLOSED` with the count — the push says the owner's sentence
  «أُغلقت وكالتك لأنها لم تفعّل ٣ مضيفين (بثّ واستلام هدايا) خلال ٧ أيام» with the numbers from config and the count
  reached. **Commission already earned stays with the owner** (nothing is reversed). The host-agent perks go while it
  is closed (the code stays the person's). 24 h before the end (`AGENCY_PROBATION_REMINDER_HOURS`), still below the
  count, the owner gets `AGENCY_PROBATION_REMINDER` once (again after an extension). The closing is idempotent (one
  conditional `UPDATE … WHERE status = 'OPEN'` under the row lock) and audited `agency.close`.
- **A closed agency** is never found (`getAgencyByCode` 404), joined, listed as the owner's dashboard, rank-evaluated,
  counted as a parent's qualified sub-agency, or paid a commission (its own or as a parent). Its row stays (the
  earnings history; `agencies_owner_once` unchanged). `getMyAgency` returns `ownAgency: null` and `closedAgency` (the
  reason, the date, the count, `reopenAt`). Its owner may join another agency as a host. After the cooldown
  «افتح وكالة» opens **the same row** again (same invite and host code, the new name, rank `NEW` with a new grace, a new
  probation; released hosts do not come back). The team's `agency-create` refuses the owner of a closed agency
  (`agency-reopen` instead).
- **The team** — panel (`agencies.probation`, OWNER, reason + the authenticator code again) and `economy-admin`:
  extend a running probation by 1–90 days (from its end, or from now when it already passed without a sweep), close an
  open agency (reason `ADMIN`; the same release and notifications, no count), reopen a closed one (a self-opened
  agency whose probation had not passed gets a new full probation from now; the owner gets `AGENCY_OPENED`). Every
  action is audited (`agency.probation.extend`, `agency.close`, `agency.reopen`, `via` cli / panel / sweeper). The
  agencies list filters `state=probation|closed` and `origin`; an agency's page shows the probation, its hosts and
  the applications; an application's fields and pictures (`agencies.applications`: OWNER, SUPPORT) are read one at a
  time, each view audited (`agency.application.view`, `agency.application.photo.view`), the pictures streamed by the
  API. Account deletion purges the contact, the bio and the pictures (the name, country and dates stay); the data
  export includes the person's applications and pictures (`agency_applications`).

### 10.67 The admin panel's account controls «تحكم كامل» *(v1.72-social, DRAFT — D208)*

The owner's request of 2026-10-31 («حاول دراسة لوحة الادمن واجعله يملك صلاحية لكل شيء مثل قفل حساب شخص او حظره او
تغير كلمة المرور والخ»). The audit of every area (what a user can do, what the panel and the CLIs can do, the gaps with
P1 / P2 / P3) is `docs/admin/ADMIN_CAPABILITY_AUDIT.md`; this section is the P1 contract. Everything runs behind the
§10.54 cookie session, CSRF header, rate limits and per-request capability check; every operation's description starts
with `(v1.72-social, D208`. The rules live in `apps/api/src/modules/users/account-control.ts`, shared by the panel and
the `control-admin` CLI (`via: cli`, no actor), so both write the same rows.

#### 10.67.1 Capabilities

| Capability | OWNER | MODERATION | SUPPORT | FINANCE |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| `users.control_view` (the state: locks, restrictions, password / email, deletion, adjustments) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `users.lock` (lock for a while, unlock) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| `users.restrict` (chat mute, no live, no gifts, no posting; lift) | ✓ | ✓ | | |
| `users.password` (reset email, temporary password ⚿, forced change) | ✓ | | ✓ | |
| `users.email` (change ⚿ — marking it verified OWNER only —, resend verification) | ✓ | | ✓ | |
| `users.profile_edit` (name, username, bio, country, gender) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| `users.content` (hide / restore posts, reels, stories; remove comments; delete for good ⚿) | ✓ | ✓ | | |
| `users.balance_adjust` (coins and cherries ⚿; «allow negative» OWNER only) | ✓ | | | ✓ |
| `users.delete` (the D193 deletion ⚿ and its cancel) | ✓ | | | |

⚿ = the authenticator code again (`totpCode`, §10.54.3): destructive or money. Every change needs a `reason` (1–500)
and writes one audit row with the actor, the IP, `via: panel`, the reason and `before` / `after`. Never on one's own
account; a panel admin's account only by an OWNER (403). Passwords, tokens and full addresses are never audited
(addresses masked `a***@domain`).

#### 10.67.2 Lock and restrictions (`account_restrictions`)

- **Kinds:** `LOCK` «قفل الحساب», `CHAT_MUTE` «كتم الدردشة» (every live chat, bullets, comments, direct messages),
  `NO_LIVE` «منع البث» (`startLiveRoom`; a current live ends with reason ADMIN), `NO_GIFTS` «منع الهدايا» (live, direct
  and bag gifts), `NO_POSTING` «منع النشر» (posts, reels, stories).
- **Duration:** `days` (the panel offers 1 / 3 / 7 / 30) or `until` (in the future, ≤ 365 days). A row is active while
  `lifted_at` is null and `starts_at ≤ now < ends_at` — it ends by itself, no sweeper. A new one of the same kind
  replaces the open one (`lift_reason = 'replaced'`). Lifting early: `unlockAdminUser` / `liftAdminUserRestriction`.
- **The reason is shown to the person** (the dialogs say so): in `login`'s 403 `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` details and in the
  `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` notification's `text`.
- **LOCK** ends every session (and push token) when it starts, ends a live and frees seats; `login` with the right
  password answers 403 `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` `[{lockedUntil}, {reason}]` until the end. Only an ACTIVE account. It is
  **not the ban**: the ban (`banAdminUser`, D191) is `users.status = SUSPENDED`, permanent until unbanned; a lock never
  changes the status. **The ban now asks for the authenticator code too** (`banAdminUser` `{reason, totpCode}`, owner
  2026-10-31; `unbanAdminUser` keeps the reason only). A banned account cannot be locked (409); unbanning leaves a lock that is still running; the
  D193 deletion is refused for a non-ACTIVE account as before.
- **Enforcement:** 403 `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` `[{restriction: kind}, {until}]` before anything is stored or charged (an
  idempotent replay of an earlier send still answers as before).
- **Notifications** (system, no actor): `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` and `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION_LIFTED` with the target
  `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION` (`restriction`, `endsAt`, `text` = the reason).

#### 10.67.3 Password and email

- **Reset email** «إرسال رابط إعادة تعيين»: the existing `forgotPassword` email (D24 rules); the admin never sees the link.
- **Temporary password** «تعيين كلمة مرور مؤقتة» ⚿: 4 groups of 4 characters without look-alikes (≈ 91 bits), generated
  by the server, returned ONCE (`Cache-Control: no-store`), stored only as its Argon2 hash; every session ends, open
  reset links stop working, and `users.password_change_required_at` is set.
- **Forced change** «فرض تغيير كلمة المرور في الدخول القادم»: sets the same flag (`endSessions`, default true, signs
  out now). While it is set, `login` with the right password answers 403 `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED`; the same request
  with `newPassword` (§6 rules; equal to `password` → 400 `same_as_current`) sets it, clears the flag, ends the other
  sessions and signs in (audited `auth.password.changed_at_sign_in`). The order of `login`'s answers after the right
  password: deletion pending (409) → suspended (403) → locked (403) → password change (403).
- **Email** ⚿: the new address (another account's → 409) gets the existing verification email; `markVerified` (OWNER
  only) marks it verified instead. Every outstanding verification and reset link ends. `resendAdminUserVerification`.

#### 10.67.4 Profile, content, money, deletion, timeline

- **Profile:** `displayName` (§6, reserved terms), `username` (the D146 regular rule — 400 for a premium shape; 409
  `USERNAME_TAKEN` when reserved, `coin`/`host` codes, another account's, pending, held or quarantined; 409 while a
  special or premium username is shown), `bio`, `country`, `gender` (the active-host frame follows, D186). There is
  no profile cover or background in the app (the photo: `removeAdminUserAvatar`). The person gets
  `PROFILE_EDITED_BY_TEAM`. **The old username stays held for the person** for `ADMIN_USERNAME_RENAME_HOLD_DAYS`
  (30; 0 = no hold; owner 2026-10-31) with the special-username hold (a GRACE `special_usernames` row, source
  `ADMIN_GIFT`, `end_reason = RENAMED`, `grace_until` = the end): nobody else may take it (409 `USERNAME_TAKEN`), old
  @mentions and links still lead to the person, the person may take it back (`changeUsername`), and the special-
  username sweeper releases it at the end. A second team rename extends the same hold. Audited `oldUsernameHeldUntil`.
- **Content** (`moderateAdminContent`): `hide` a post / reel (`moderation = REMOVED`) or story (`removed_at`) —
  restorable with `restore`; `hide` a comment removes it with its replies (not restorable); `delete` ⚿ a post or story
  for good (`deleted_at`, as the author's own delete). Hide and delete close the item's OPEN reports (ACTIONED) and
  send `CONTENT_REMOVED`. `listAdminUserContent` lists stories and comments (posts and reels: `listAdminUserPosts`).
- **Money** ⚿: `adjustAdminUserBalance` `{currency, direction, amount}` writes `admin_balance_adjustments` and one
