| Kind | Size (exact shape ±1 %, at least) | Formats | Max file | Max length | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `banner` | 1 500 × 300 (5:1 — the carousel's real shape, D248b; not D124's 3:1) | PNG, JPEG, WebP; animated WebP / GIF | 2 MB still, 5 MB animated | 10 s | text in the centred 900 × 240 px |
| `banner_video` | 1 500 × 300 | MP4 / MOV, H.264 or HEVC, muted | 30 MB | 30 s | + a `banner` still as poster; Live home only |
| `background` | 1 080 × 1 920 (9:16) | PNG, JPEG, WebP; animated WebP / GIF | 3 MB still, 8 MB animated | 10 s | top 0–480 px: title art; 520–1 920 px: cards |
| `background_video` | 1 080 × 1 920 | MP4 / MOV, H.264 or HEVC, muted, looping | 20 MB | 15 s | + a `background` still as poster |
| `title` | 1 080 × 480 | PNG, WebP, transparent | 1 MB | — | over the background's top |
| `overlay` | — | SVGA 2.x or Lottie JSON | 2 MB | 10 s a loop | falling coins / sparkles over the page |
| `badge` | 512 × 512 | PNG, WebP, transparent | 1 MB | — | one per medal level |

Pictures are re-encoded to WebP at the spec size (metadata dropped); videos and overlays are stored unchanged. An
event names its art (`backgroundKey`, `backgroundPosterKey` — required exactly with a video background —,
`titleKey`, `overlayKey`; each must be stored); `EventDetail.art` returns the URLs and kinds. A banner for an event
is a `banner` / `banner_video` upload named in `createAdminBanner` with `eventId`.

**The page (app, this pass):** the background still (a picture; an animated picture plays; a video shows its poster —
the video itself is not played yet), darkened, with the title art on top; the Lottie overlay looping (paused with
reduced motion and when the page is hidden; an SVGA overlay is not drawn yet); semi-transparent gold-framed cards with
gold headings (`ProgramGoldFrame`); a countdown to the start / end; a tab per board; the board reloads every 30 s
while shown and running; Kabso's own crowns on ranks 1–3; a sticky «مركزي» bar (the place and points, and the points
to the next rank or to the minimum); a tap on an event gift explains it is sent from a live's gift panel and opens
the lives; a tap on a prize previews it; pull to refresh. *Not yet:* a share link, the preselected gift panel from
inside a live, playing a video background, an SVGA overlay. The panel previews the page with the uploaded art before
publishing.

*Owner decisions recorded (D303 follow-ups):* `events.manage` OWNER only; cherry prizes withdrawable at once; event
bag items not transferable; reversed sends don't count; banner video 30 s / 30 MB on the Live home only; medals as
prizes with levels; RECEIVERS includes creators (overrides D295 for gift events only), AGENCIES host agencies; the
money per board (supporters coins; hosts, creators cherries; agencies either; CP per partner's role); items and medals
may be permanent, VIP never.


### 10.115 The global strips «شريط الهدايا» and «شريط الألعاب» *(v1.85-live, DRAFT — D305)*

Owner (2026-11-07, with two owner-made strip artworks): «هذا شريط الهدايا والآخر شريط الألعاب، يظهر في جميع الغرف من
الجانب الى المنتصف ويخرج من الجهة الأخرى، ويبقى في المنتصف ثانيتين. شريط الهدايا: يكتب داخله «ارسل (اسم المرسل) الى (اسم
المستلم) هدية (اسم الهدية)» وصورة مصغرة لها؛ يظهر للهدايا التي سعرها ٥٠٠ ألف كوينز وأكثر. شريط الألعاب: يكتب داخله «فاز (اسم
الفائز) بجائزة قيمتها (قيمة الجائزة بالتذاكر)» وصورة مصغرة للعبة؛ يظهر للجائزة التي قيمتها ١ مليون وأكثر»; then «يمكن
للمستخدم الغاء شريط الهدايا من اعدادات اي غرفة وايضاً الغاء شريط الألعاب»; then (D305b) «اجعل حجم الشريط اصغر وشريط الألعاب
يكون موقعه فوق شريط الهدايا», and the owner's decisions: the threshold is the price of ONE gift; the strip shows in the
origin room too; the tap as built; both thresholds editable in the panel; each future game's catalogue entry has a
thumbnail.

- **One channel, two kinds.** Both strips are LiveKit data messages on topic `gift` to every LIVE room (≤ 5 000, the
  origin room first, then the newest lives), sent by `LiveGiftTickerService` (D178's global gift strip, extended). Each
  message has a `kind`; old apps read only `type` (they ignore `kind` and unknown types, §10.23).
- **Gifts strip — `gift-ticker`, `kind: "GIFT"`.** Unchanged shape (D178): `{"type":"gift-ticker","kind":"GIFT",
  "gift":LiveGift,"room":{"id","title","host":UserSummary}}`. Sent when the gift's **unit price** (`LiveGift.unitPrice`, the price of
  ONE gift — **owner decision**, replacing D178's send total `totalCoins`: 10 × 50 000 does not qualify) is at least the
  threshold **`giftMinCoins`**: the OWNER's (panel, below), else `GIFT_GLOBAL_TICKER_MIN_COINS`, default **500 000** (was
  1 000). The text may still say ×N.
  Quips excluded (as before). **Now also to the send's own room** (owner «في جميع الغرف»): the in-room gift strip and
  chat line (§10.23, D178) are a different, smaller thing at the side, so the big centred strip does not duplicate them.
  Apps before v1.85-live drop a `gift-ticker` of their own room, so nothing changes for them there.
- **Games strip — `game-win-ticker`, `kind: "GAME_WIN"`.** `{"type":"game-win-ticker","kind":"GAME_WIN","win":
  {"id","game":{"code","name","imageUrl":string|null},"winner":UserSummary,"tickets":int,"roomId":string|null,
  "createdAt"},"room":{"id","title","host"}|null}` for a game prize of at least **`gameMinTickets`** tickets (the OWNER's, else
  `GAME_WIN_TICKER_MIN_TICKETS`, default 1 000 000; tickets = the game cards of D182). `room` is the live the game was played in while it is LIVE,
  else null (`win.roomId` null too).
- **The game hook (no game exists yet — D173 «الألعاب قريباً»; none is invented).** A game calls
  `LiveGiftTickerService.offerGameWin({id, gameCode, gameName, gameImageUrl, winnerId, tickets, roomId, createdAt})`
  once per prize, **after** the transaction that credits the winner's tickets has committed, never on an idempotent
  replay, through `BackgroundTasks.run` (a strip never delays or fails a game). `id` is the prize's own id: a repeated id
  is ignored for 24 h (`gift:ticker:game-seen:{id}`). Below the threshold or an unknown winner: nothing.
  **Game catalogue (owner):** when games are added, each game's catalogue entry must provide a **square thumbnail**
  (`gameImageUrl`, a transparent PNG or WebP, **128 × 128 px**; the strip draws it ≈ 25 pt, ≈ 75 px at 3x) — the strip
  uses that thumbnail; null shows the strip's own trophy art only.
- **Pace (D178, per kind — D305b).** At most one strip of each kind every **3 s** for the whole service: gifts keep
  D178's Redis gate `gift:ticker:gate` and waiting slot `gift:ticker:pending`; game wins have `gift:ticker:game:gate` /
  `gift:ticker:game:pending`. One waiting per kind (≤ 12 s), a newer one replaces it (newest first). The two kinds are
  two lanes in the app (owner «شريط الألعاب يكون موقعه فوق شريط الهدايا»), so a gift strip and a games strip may show at
  the same time. The app shows a strip for ≈ 2.9 s (enter 0.45 s, **hold 2 s** in the centre, exit 0.45 s), inside the
  gap.
- **Per-account switches.** `NotificationSettings.giftStrip` and `gameStrip` (`GET` / `PATCH /me/notification-settings`,
  default true, migration `20270405090000_global_strip_settings`): «إظهار شريط الهدايا» / «إظهار شريط الألعاب» in every
  live's settings sheet (viewer and host) and in the app's notification settings. Off: that person's app does not show
  the kind, in every live, on every phone signed in to the account. The server keeps sending (one message per room, not
  per person). Guests (no account): always on.
- **App.** One strip at a time per lane over the room's upper part (it takes taps only on itself): slides in from the
  reading-start side (Arabic: from the right) to the centre, holds 2 s, leaves by the other side; with reduced motion it
  fades in and out and still holds 2 s. Waiting strips: at most 3 per lane, the newest first, none older than 30 s. A strip from
  another live opens that live on a tap (D178); in its own live (or without a live) a tap opens the sender's / winner's
  card. Blocked senders, winners and hosts are not shown (D178).
- **Thresholds in the panel (owner).** `getAdminGlobalStrips` / `updateAdminGlobalStrips` (`GET` / `PUT
  /admin/global-strips`, panel session + CSRF, capability `site.settings`: OWNER, as D254's level banner):
  `{giftMinCoins (1 … 10⁹), gameMinTickets (1 … 10¹²)}`, both required on PUT, optional `reason`; stored as the
  `site_settings` row `globalStrips` (CHECK extended by the same migration); audited `site.settings.update`
  (`metadata.key` = `globalStrips`, before / after / reason). The configuration is the fallback when no row (or an
  invalid value). The API reads it through a **30 s** cache: a change applies without a restart within 30 s.
- **Size and lanes (D305b, app).** Each strip is ≤ **270 pt** wide (75 % of the first 360), ≈ 78 pt tall with the crown
  and wings (glass bar ≈ 32 pt); words 11 pt at text scale 1 (cap 1.15), two lines at most. Two lanes, one under the
  other under the room header: the **games lane on top**, the **gifts lane 4 pt under it**; each lane keeps its place
  (a gift strip never moves up when no game strip shows) and its own queue (≤ 3 waiting, newest first, none older than
  30 s) and timeline.
- **Not in this version:** per-room switches (owner: per account).

### 11.1 Media upload

- Server config `MEDIA_UPLOADS_ENABLED` (default `false`, B12) gates `createMediaUpload` and
  `completeMediaUpload`: off → 503 `MEDIA_UPLOADS_UNAVAILABLE` (no `Retry-After`, like
  `LIVE_HOSTING_UNAVAILABLE`). Storage is S3-compatible (`S3_*`; MinIO locally, R2 in the cloud).
  *(v1.75-social, D222)* The OWNER's «التخزين (R2 / S3)» in the admin panel, when on, replaces both (the switch, the
  buckets, the public base URL) without a restart; with two buckets, `uploads/` and `private/` live in the private one
  and only `media/` in the public one (§10.72).
- Accepted types: JPEG, PNG and WebP (the bytes decide, not the declared type: both must agree).
  HEIC/HEIF is refused at `createMediaUpload` (the app converts it to JPEG on the device).
- Objects go to `uploads/{userId}/{uploadId}` (private). Completing verifies the object (HEAD
  size equals `byteSize`, magic bytes match `contentType`, decodes, ≤ 8 000 px per side,
  ≤ 50 MP), strips every metadata block (EXIF, GPS, XMP, ICC kept as sRGB), writes
  `media/{mediaId}/1080.webp` and `media/{mediaId}/320.webp` and a blurhash, and deletes the
  upload object. Failure → 422 `MEDIA_INVALID`; the slot is closed.
- *(CP-008)* `STORY_IMAGE` uploads follow the same checks; their large variant is
  `media/{mediaId}/1920.webp` (at most 1 920 px on the long side) and attaches only to a story,
  as a `POST_IMAGE` asset attaches only to a post (otherwise 400 `mediaId` / `invalid_value`).
- *(CP-015)* `LIVE_COVER` uploads follow the same checks; both variants are centre-cropped
  squares, never enlarged: `media/{mediaId}/640.webp` (at most 640 × 640) and `320.webp`. They
  attach only as the host's live cover (§10.13).
- *(v1.21-live, CP-018)* `FAMILY_EMBLEM` uploads are processed like `LIVE_COVER` (centre-cropped
  squares, 640 and 320 px) and attach only as a family's emblem (§10.21).
- *(v1.25-live, CP-022)* `FAMILY_COVER` uploads are processed like `POST_IMAGE` (at most 1 080 px
  on the long side, and 320 px) and attach only as a family's cover (§10.25).
- *(v1.26-live, D124)* `HOME_BANNER` uploads are cover-cropped around the centre to exactly 3:1,
  enlarged when smaller: `media/{mediaId}/1500.webp` (1 500 × 500) and `320.webp` (320 × 107).
  Only the `banner-admin` CLI attaches them, as a home banner's picture (§10.26).
- *(v1.19-live, CP-017)* `LIVE_CHAT_IMAGE` uploads follow the same checks and sizes as
  `POST_IMAGE` and attach only to a live chat message. `LIVE_CHAT_VOICE` uploads are voice clips:
  `audio/mp4` (AAC in an MPEG-4 container, `.m4a`), at most 1 MiB (else 400 `byteSize` /
  `too_big`; an image type for this kind, or `audio/mp4` for another kind → 400 `contentType` /
  `invalid_value`). Completing checks the container — an `ftyp` box first, the movie length from
  `moov/mvhd`, every track a sound track — and refuses a clip longer than 30 s (up to 30.5 s of
  encoder padding is accepted and reported as 30 000 ms) with 422 `MEDIA_INVALID`; the audio is
  not decoded or re-encoded. The bytes are stored unchanged as `media/{mediaId}/voice.m4a`
  (`audio/mp4`). The asset is `type: AUDIO`, `width`/`height` 0, `blurhash` null, `thumbUrl` =
  `url`, plus `durationMs`. Both kinds attach only to a live chat message and are deleted 60 s
  after it was sent (§10.19).
- *(v1.40-social, D155)* `DM_IMAGE` uploads are processed like `POST_IMAGE`, and `DM_VOICE` uploads
  like `LIVE_CHAT_VOICE` (`audio/mp4`, ≤ 1 MiB, ≤ 30 s); both attach only to a direct message and are
  deleted with it (24 hours after it was sent, §11.13).
- *(v1.41-social, D162)* `POST_VIDEO` and `REEL_VIDEO` uploads are videos (`video/mp4`,
  `video/quicktime`), checked and stored as §11.14 says; `VIDEO_POSTER` uploads are processed like
  `POST_IMAGE` and are consumed by the video they are the poster of.
- *(v1.45-social, D168)* `AVATAR` uploads are processed like `LIVE_COVER` (centre-cropped squares,
  640 and 320 px) and attach only as the uploader's profile photo (§10.42).
- *(v1.76-social, D218)* `PROFILE_COVER` uploads are processed like `POST_IMAGE` (never cropped) and
  attach only as the uploader's profile cover (§10.73.3).
- Asset URLs are served from `MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (a CDN or bucket domain). An asset is
  attachable once, only by its owner, within 24 hours; unattached assets and expired slots are
  deleted by a sweeper.

### 11.2 Posts

- `text`: NFC, trimmed, ≤ 2 200 code points, the free-text hygiene rules of §6 (no control,
  bidi-override or zero-width characters except ZWNJ/ZWJ between joining letters; line breaks
  allowed, at most 30). A post needs `text` or at least one image. *(v1.41-social, D162)* or a
  video; a reel (`format: REEL`) needs its video (§11.14).
- `location`: free text ≤ 80 code points (places arrive with M6), same hygiene.
- `status`: `PUBLISHED` (default), `DRAFT`, or `SCHEDULED` with `publishAt` in
  [now + 5 min, now + 30 days]; a worker publishes due posts within a minute. Drafts and
  scheduled posts are visible only to the author.
- Visibility of a published post to a caller: not removed; author ACTIVE; no block in either
  direction; author public, or the caller is the author or follows the author; `moderation`
  `VISIBLE` unless the caller is the author. Anything else → 404 (never 403).
- **Moderation:** *(v1.42-social, D162a, owner: «جميعها تظهر فوراً»)* every post — text, photos,
  a video or a reel — is `VISIBLE` at once, like stories (D91); safety relies on reports and
  moderators' `REMOVE_TARGET`. `PENDING` stays a valid value (a future moderation provider or an
  admin hold): a `PENDING` post is visible only to its author and absent from feeds, search and
  other people's grids. *(Until v1.41-social, CP-006 Q2 held posts with images `PENDING`.)*
  Switching on a provider is a config change, not a contract change.
- Settings default from the author's privacy settings (§11.7); `hideLikeCount` makes
  `likeCount` null and the likers list 403 for everyone but the author.
- Pins: at most 3 published posts; a 4th → 409 `PIN_LIMIT_REACHED`. Profile grids list pinned
  posts first (newest pin first), then the rest newest first.
- Reposts: of visible public posts by someone else; a repost puts the post (with `repostedBy`)
  in the reposter's followers' Following feed and on the reposter's Reposts tab. Deleting or
  removing the original removes it everywhere.
- `Idempotency-Key` on `createPost`: kept 24 h per user; same key + same body → the first
  response (status 201); same key + different body → 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.

### 11.3 Feeds and cursors

- All lists use signed keyset cursors (§5) bound to the list, its filters and the caller.
- *(v1.41-social, D162)* `GET /feed/posts` lists `format: POST` posts only; reels have their own
  feed (§11.14).
- `following`: published, visible posts and reposts of followed accounts, newest first by
  `publishedAt` (for a repost: its repost time); a post appears once (its newest entry).
  Muted authors (and reposts by muted accounts) and hidden posts are left out.
- `trending`: the first page ranks visible public posts published in the last 7 days by
  `(likes + 2·comments + 3·shares + 2·saves + 1) / (hoursSincePublished + 2)^1.5` (weights are
  server config), excluding the caller's own, muted and hidden posts, at most 2 per author in
  any 10. The ranked ids (≤ 500) are frozen for 10 minutes; later pages read the snapshot, so
  they never repeat or skip. An expired or foreign snapshot → 400 `cursor` / `invalid_value`.
- *(v1.76-social, D218)* `mixed`: 1 `following` entry, then 2 `trending`, again and again, as one
  frozen list — the app's home feed (§10.73.1). *(v1.92-social, D294)* `GET /feed/reels?tab=mixed`: the same
  over reels — the app's reels page (§10.107).

### 11.4 Views

`recordViews`: a view counts when `watchedMs ≥ 1 000`, once per user, post and rolling 24 h,
never for the author, and only for posts the caller may see; anything else is ignored. The
count is eventually consistent (≤ 1 min).

### 11.5 Comments

- `text`: NFC, trimmed, 1–500 code points, §6 hygiene, ≤ 5 line breaks.
- Who may comment: `commentsEnabled` and `whoCanComment` (`EVERYONE`; `FOLLOWERS` = people who
  follow the author; `NOBODY`); the author always may. Refused → 403 `AUTH_FORBIDDEN`. Blocked
  users never see the post (404).
- One level of replies: `parentId` of a reply resolves to its top-level comment. Deleting a
  top-level comment deletes its replies. `canDelete` is true for the comment's author and the
  post's author.
- Order: the pinned comment, then by `likeCount` desc, then newest. One pinned comment per post,
  top-level only (a reply → 400 `commentId` / `invalid_value`).

### 11.6 Hashtags, mentions and search

- `#tag`: `#` followed by 1–100 letters, marks, digits or `_` (any script), not preceded by a
  letter or digit; stored in NFC lower case; at most 30 distinct per post (extra ones are plain
  text). Hashtag pages list visible posts; `top` uses the trending score over 30 days.
- `@username`: a valid, existing, ACTIVE username (§6 pattern); at most 20 per post or comment.
  A mention of someone whose `whoCanMention` forbids it (or who blocked the author) stays plain
  text and is not linked.
- `search`: case-insensitive prefix match — users on username and display name, hashtags on the
  tag, posts on caption words (visible posts only). Blocked users never appear. Results are
  ranked by exact match, then followers / post count / recency.

### 11.7 Block, mute, hide, reports and privacy

- **Block** is symmetric in effect: neither side sees the other's posts, comments, profile
  content, likes lists or search entries, and follows both ways are deleted (not restored by
  unblock). While a block exists in either direction, `followUser` between the two → 404 (the
  existing "not found" answer; follow and block writes are serialized). Blocking yourself → 400.
  Their existing comments on your posts are hidden from you.
- **Mute** is one-way and silent: the muted account's posts, reposts and (CP-008) stories leave
  the caller's feeds and stories tray, and (CP-009) it cannot notify the caller; profile, search and direct links still work. The caller sees their mutes in
  `GET /me/mutes` (newest first, every muted account, like `GET /me/blocks`) and on profiles as
  `PublicProfile.isMuted`; the muted account is never told (CP-007).
- **Hide**: the post leaves the caller's feeds and hashtag pages.
- **Reports**: one OPEN report per reporter and target; a repeat → 200 with the existing
  report. Admins with permission `MODERATION` list and act; `REMOVE_TARGET` removes the post or
  comment (soft, audited) — *v1.24-live:* or a CP confession (`targetType: CP_CONFESSION`, one the
  reporter can read and did not write, §10.24) — *v1.25-live:* or a family chat message
  (`targetType: FAMILY_CHAT_MESSAGE`, in the reporter's family, not their own, §10.25) — *v1.40-social:* or a
  direct message the reporter received (`targetType: DM_MESSAGE`, kept as a snapshot because
  messages are deleted after 24 h, §11.13) — *v1.47-social:* or a profile link (`targetType: PROFILE_LINK`,
  kept as a snapshot, §10.47) — or, for a user, records the decision only (suspension stays a separate
  admin tool); every OPEN report on that target closes with the same outcome. Acting on a closed
  report → 409 `REPORT_ALREADY_RESOLVED`. *(v1.78-live, D288, §10.101)* The panel's queue is shared by OWNER,
  MODERATION and SUPPORT; «تم حله» closes one report for everyone; a new report alerts them (`STAFF_REPORT_NEW`). *(v1.93-social, D296, §10.109)* A USER report's `targetId` may be the user's id or the username (and `dmConversationId` when made from a conversation); the staff open a report's content from the app and act on it, which resolves that report only.
- **Privacy settings**: `whoCanMention` (`EVERYONE` default; `FOLLOWING` = accounts the user
  follows; `NOBODY`) and `defaultWhoCanComment` (`EVERYONE` default) for new posts;
  *(v1.25-live, CP-022)* `showActivityStatus` (default true): whether family members may see when
  the user was last active (§10.25).
  *(v1.40-social, D155)* `whoCanMessage` (`EVERYONE` default; `FOLLOWING` = accounts the user
  follows; `NOBODY`): who may send the user direct messages (§11.13).
  *(v1.47-social, D175)* `isPrivate` (default false): a private account (§10.47).

### 11.8 Rate limits (all per user; replace the per-user default)

| Endpoint | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /media/uploads` | 60 / hour; counted **before** the `MEDIA_UPLOADS_ENABLED` check |
| `POST /posts` | 20 / hour, 100 / day |
| `POST /posts/{id}/comments` | 60 / hour |
| `PUT`/`DELETE` like (posts and comments) | one bucket: 600 / hour |
| `PUT`/`DELETE` repost | 60 / hour |
| `POST /posts/{id}/shares` | 120 / hour |
| `POST /views` | 120 / hour |
| `GET /feed/posts`, `GET /search`, *(v1.41-social)* `GET /feed/reels` | 300 / 15 min (`GET /feed/reels` shares the `social:feed` bucket) |
| `PUT /users/{username}/block` | 60 / hour |
| `POST /reports` | 30 / hour |
| `POST /stories` *(CP-008)* | 30 / hour |
| `PUT /stories/{id}/seen` *(CP-008)* | 600 / hour |
| `GET /feed/stories` *(CP-008)* | 300 / 15 min |
| `GET /notifications`, `GET /notifications/unread-count` *(CP-009)* | one bucket: 300 / 15 min |
| `POST /notifications/read` *(CP-009)* | 120 / hour |

### 11.9 Stories *(CP-008, D91 — CP-006 M3, photos only)*

- A story is one `STORY_IMAGE` photo and an optional `text` (NFC, trimmed, ≤ 200 code points,
  §6 hygiene, ≤ 3 line breaks; mentions as §11.6, at most 10; hashtags stay plain text).
  `createStory` takes an `Idempotency-Key` with the rules of `createPost`.
- **Active** = not deleted and `expiresAt` (`createdAt` + 24 h) in the future. Expired stories
  leave every list except the author's archive (`GET /me/stories/archive`, newest first), which
  keeps them until the author deletes them. Deleting is soft and removes the story everywhere.
- **No moderation hold (owner, D91):** story photos are visible at once; safety relies on
  reports (`targetType: STORY`, admin `REMOVE_TARGET` removes the story) and the 24-hour expiry.
- **Visibility** as posts (§11.2): author ACTIVE, no block either way, author public or followed
  by the caller (the author always sees their own). Anything else → 404.
- **Tray** (`GET /feed/stories`): the caller's own entry first when they have an active story;
  then followed accounts with active stories, those with unseen stories first, each group by the
  newest story; muted accounts left out (§11.7). Keyset cursor (§5).
- **Seen**: one row per viewer and story, idempotent, never for the author; `viewCount` (author
  only) counts distinct viewers. `GET /stories/{id}/viewers` is for the author only and only
  until 48 h after posting; otherwise 404.
- Replies, video stories, highlights and stickers are not part of M3 (M7, M2, later).

### 11.10 Notifications *(CP-009, D92 — CP-006 M4, in-app only)*

- Types and targets: `LIKE_POST` (post), `LIKE_COMMENT` (comment), `COMMENT` on your post and
  `REPLY` to your comment (the comment), `MENTION` in a post, comment or story (that item, only
  when `whoCanMention` allowed it), `FOLLOW` (the follower), `REPOST` (post), and the system types
  `POST_PUBLISHED` (your scheduled post went live) and `CONTENT_REMOVED` (moderation removed your
  post, comment or story). Notifications are written in the same transaction as their action.
  *(v1.14-live, CP-016 C)* `LIVE_SCHEDULED_SOON`: a host you follow goes live in about 15
  minutes (target the host as `USER` with the title and `startsAt`, §10.16; setting `lives`).
  *(v1.21-live, CP-018, §10.21)* `CP_REQUEST` (someone sent you a CP request) and `CP_ACCEPTED`
  (your CP request was accepted): target the other person as `USER`; `FAMILY_JOIN_ACCEPTED` and
  `FAMILY_JOIN_DECLINED`: target `FAMILY` (the family id, its name as `text`), actor the leader or
  deputy who answered; `MEDAL_AWARDED` (system, no actor, always on): target `MEDAL` (the medal
  code as `id`, `text` null; the app reads name and icon from `GET /medals`). No setting switches
  these off. *(v1.48-social, D171, §10.45)* `BAG_ITEM_RECEIVED`: someone sent you a bag item (actor
  the sender; target `BAG_ITEM`: the item code as `id`, `text` null, `bagCategory` its category;
  the app opens the bag). Always on.
  *(v1.47-social, D175, §10.47)* `FOLLOW_REQUEST` (someone asked to follow your private account; target
  the requester as `USER`; withdrawn when the request is cancelled, accepted or declined) and
  `FOLLOW_REQUEST_ACCEPTED` (your request was accepted; target the account as `USER`), both under the
  `follows` setting; `AVATAR_REMOVED` (system, no actor, no target, always on: a moderator removed your
  profile photo).
- **Never yourself**; never between two users with a block in either direction (existing ones
  are hidden while it lasts); never from an account the recipient muted (owner, D92); actors no
  longer ACTIVE are left out of `actors` and `actorCount`, and a group left with no visible actor
  is hidden.
- **Grouping (owner, D92):** `LIKE_POST`, `LIKE_COMMENT` and `REPOST` on the same target join one
  **unread** notification (up to 3 recent `actors`, `actorCount` all); each new actor moves it to
  the top. A read group is closed: the next one starts a new group. Other types never group.
- **Undo:** unlike, un-repost, unfollow, deleting the comment and deleting or removing the target
  take that contribution away; a notification left with no actor is deleted.
- **Settings** (`/me/notification-settings`, all `true` by default): a switched-off type creates
  nothing new (`likes` covers both likes, `comments` covers `COMMENT` and `REPLY`). System types
  are always on.
- **Unread count** is capped at 99. `POST /notifications/read` takes `ids` (1–100, the caller's
  own; others are ignored) or `all: true`; idempotent.
- **Retention (owner, D92):** notifications whose latest activity is older than **30 days** are
  deleted by a sweeper.
- Delivery is in-app (the app polls the unread count) and, since v1.30-live (D152), a push on Android
  (§11.12).

### 11.11 Search trends *(v1.29-live, DRAFT — D147)*

Owner request (2026-10-28): the search page laid out like an authorized third-party reference
(layout only — no logo, art or photos copied): hot searches, hot hashtags and lives under an empty
field. Every list is real data; a section with too little data is hidden by the app (honest).

- **Counting a search** (`recordSearchQuery`, `POST /search/queries` `{q}` → 204): the app sends it
  when the person **submits** a search or **opens a result** of one — never per keystroke. `q`
  follows `search`'s rules (1–64 after NFC and trim; 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` otherwise). The server
  counts the **normalized term**: NFC, trimmed, one leading `@`/`#` dropped, inner whitespace
  collapsed, lower case; 2–64 code points with at least one letter. Never counted (accepted and
  dropped, 204, so the answer does not reveal it): control or format characters, `@` (emails), a
  link (`://`, `www.`), or **5+ digits in a row** (phone, room or account numbers).
- **Privacy**: no user id, IP or device is stored with a term. Each person counts **once per term
  per 7 days**: an HMAC (HKDF `search-searcher/v1` of `RATE_LIMIT_KEY_SECRET`) of user and term is
  kept in Redis with a 7-day expiry, then forgotten. Stored are only `search_terms` (term, first
  seen, hidden) and `search_term_counts` (term, UTC hour, number of searchers). A sweeper
  (`SEARCH_TRENDS_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, default 3600, 0 disables) deletes counts older than
  **14 days** and unhidden terms left without counts, in bounded batches.
- **Hot searches** (`listTrendingSearches`, `GET /search/trending`): at most **6** terms, the same
  for everyone (cached 60 s), ranked by searchers in the last 7 days, then the last 24 h, then the
  term. A term is listed only with at least **`SEARCH_TRENDING_MIN_SEARCHERS` (default 5)
  different searchers in 7 days** (nothing rare or personal surfaces), never when hidden by an
  admin or containing a **blocked word**. `tag`: `NEW` when first searched in the last 24 h; else
  `TRENDING` when at least 3 searchers in the last 24 h and at least twice the 24 h before; else
  null. Counts are hourly buckets: "24 h" and "7 days" are accurate to the hour.
- **Hashtags of the week** (`listTrendingHashtags`, `GET /search/trending-hashtags?limit`, 1–20,
  default 20): hashtags of posts **published in the last 7 days that the caller can see** (the
  visibility of hashtag pages, §11.6–§11.7: blocks, private accounts, hidden posts), with at least
  **3 such posts by at least 2 authors**; most posts first, then the newest post, then the tag;
  `postCount` counts those 7 days. Never a tag containing a blocked word. Not cached (per viewer).
- **Blocked words** (`search_blocked_words`): matched like a host's live blocked words (§10.14:
  case and Arabic spelling folded; Arabic words match inside words, others as whole words). Managed
  on the server only (this repository is public), like the reserved premium names.
- **Admin** (no API; `search-admin` CLI, migration role): `top` (the 50 most searched terms with
  their 7-day and 24 h numbers, hidden ones marked), `hide <term>` / `unhide <term>` (a hidden term
  is still counted but never listed; audited `search.term.hide`), `block-word add|remove|list`
  (audited `search.blocked_word`, without the word). The public list follows within 60 s.
- **The app** (D147): under an empty field — **Hot Searches** (ranks 1–3 coloured on a fading
  tint, tags Trending / New; shown only with **≥ 3** terms; a tap searches the term), **Hot Take**
  (four hashtags of the week in two columns; **More** opens the week's list only when there are
  more), **You may like** (the first 6 lives of `GET /live/rooms?tab=popular`, the live hub's
  cards; a tap opens the room). The hint rotates "Try searching: <term>" through the trending terms
  (the static hint without them). **Cancel** closes the search. With nothing to show the prompt
  shows. Typing shows the Accounts / Hashtags / Posts results as before.
- **Not in v1.29-live**: personal search history, suggestions while typing, QR scan (the
  reference's scan button has no Kabso feature; its slot is left empty), editorial topics.

### 11.12 Push notifications *(v1.30-live, DRAFT — D152)*

Owner request (2026-10-28): notification sounds — the owner's two Kabso sounds, a general one and
a message one. Phase 1 plays them in the app; phase 2 (this section) sends pushes.

- **Transport:** Firebase Cloud Messaging (project `kabso-27b19`), **Android only** for now. iOS
  needs an Apple Developer account and an APNs key (deferred): iOS tokens are accepted and kept,
  nothing is sent to them, and the iOS app does not start Firebase.
- **Tokens** (`registerPushToken`, `PUT /me/push-token` `{token, platform, appVersion}` → 204;
  `unregisterPushToken`, `DELETE /me/push-token` → 204; both idempotent, the per-user default rate
  limit of §7): a token belongs to the **calling session**, one per session. A new token replaces
  the session's old one; a token registered by another session (same phone, another account)
  moves to this one. The app registers after sign-in, at launch and on every token refresh
  (`lastSeenAt`). Removed: by `DELETE`, with the session (logout, revocation, refresh-token reuse,
  password reset), when Firebase answers that the token is not registered or invalid, and by the
  notifications sweeper when the session has ended or the token was not seen for 60 days. A token
  is never logged or returned.
- **Who gets a push:** only an ACTIVE account with a live session (not revoked, not expired)
  whose token is ANDROID. **Never the actor or sender.**
- **General** (Android channel `kabso_general`, the owner's general sound): every §11.10
  notification that is **created, or gains an actor while unread** (a like group), is pushed once,
  within `PUSH_DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS` (default 2 s; an outbox: `notifications.pushed_at`), only if
  it is still unread and visible under §11.10 at that moment (blocks either way, mutes, inactive
  actors, removed targets, the type's switch) and its latest activity is at most **10 minutes**
  old (a backlog after downtime is not pushed). **Bursts collapse:** at most one general push per
  recipient per `PUSH_GENERAL_GAP_SECONDS` (default 5) and one per notification per 60 s; what is
  skipped stays in the in-app inbox. Text in the recipient's account language (`users.locale`,
  Arabic by default): title «Kabso Live», body the inbox sentence («أعجب سارة و2 آخرون بمنشورك»).
  Android `tag` = the notification id (a group's newer push replaces the older one).
  Data: `kind: notification`, `channel: general`, `notificationId`, `type`, `targetType`,
  `targetId`, `targetPostId`, `actorUsername` (strings; absent when null).
- **Messages** (Android channel `kabso_messages`, the owner's message sound): a new **family chat**
  message (§10.25; private conversations do not exist yet, D86) is pushed to the family's other
  members who are ACTIVE, have `messages` on (`/me/notification-settings`, default on), have no
  block either way with the author and have not muted the author. **Bursts collapse:** one push
  per member per family per `PUSH_MESSAGES_GAP_SECONDS` (default 10); Android `tag`
  `family:<familyId>` (one notification per chat, replaced). Title: the family's name; body
  «<author>: <text>» with the leader's blocked words masked, at most 100 code points. Data:
  `kind: family_chat`, `channel: messages`, `familyId`, `messageId`.
- **Privacy:** pushes carry the text above; logs carry counts and Firebase error codes only —
  never a token, title, body or message text. The Firebase service-account key is a server file
  (`FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_FILE`, read-only mount), never in git or in the environment; unset,
  missing or invalid → push is **off** with one log line and everything else works.
- **The app** (D152): two Android notification channels with the owner's sounds from `res/raw`
  (`kabso_general` ← `kabi_voice_a`, `kabso_messages` ← `kabso_message`). Android 13+ asks for
  POST_NOTIFICATIONS **once**, after a sign-in or on first opening the notifications or a family
  chat (never at a cold start), with a rationale sheet first (D144a); refused for good → the
  notification settings offer «فتح الإعدادات». A tap opens the target (the inbox's own routing) or
  the family chat. In the foreground nothing is shown by the system: a message in another chat
  plays the message sound, a notification the general sound (also when the polled unread count
  grows), never for the chat on screen, never two at once, only while Settings → **Sound effects**
  is on and, on Android, not in silent or vibrate mode.
- *(v1.40-social, D155)* **Direct messages** are pushed on the same `messages` channel with
  `kind: dm` (§11.13); the `messages` switch covers family chat and direct messages.
- **Not in v1.30-live:** iOS pushes, pushes of live-room chat, per-chat mute, quiet hours,
  notification grouping on the device (summary notifications).

### 11.13 Direct messages *(v1.40-social, DRAFT — D155)*

Owner request (2026-10-28): real 1:1 private messages behind the Messages tab (D86 had none), with
gifts inside a conversation and a **24-hour life for every message** (owner: «الرسائل بين الأشخاص
تحذف بعد ٢٤ ساعة»). Every route needs a token (tag `messages`, `/dm/…`). Named numbers are server
configuration (`DM_*`).

- **Conversations:** one per pair of accounts, created by the **first message** (there is no
  "create" call). Each side has its own state: `status` (`ACCEPTED`; `REQUEST_RECEIVED` — a message
  request waiting for the caller; `REQUEST_SENT` — the caller wrote and the other side has not
  accepted yet), `muted`, the read pointer and a "deleted for me" time. The list
  (`listDmConversations`, `box=INBOX` — accepted and sent requests — or `box=REQUESTS`) is ordered
  by the last message (newest first, signed keyset cursor), each with the peer, the newest message
  still visible to the caller (`lastMessage`, null when none is left), `lastActivityAt`, the unread
  count (≤ 99) and `canSend`. A conversation never shows people with a block either way, nor
  accounts that are not ACTIVE.
- **Messages** (`sendDmMessage`, `POST /dm/messages` `{to, kind, text|mediaId|token, clientId}`;
  201, a retry with the same `clientId` → 200 with the first message): `TEXT` — NFC, trimmed,
  1–1 000 code points, ≤ 20 line breaks, the §6 hygiene (control, bidi-override, zero-width and
  confusable-format characters refused — `invalid_format`); **blocked words** are masked before it
  is stored (§10.14 matching: the server's list `search_blocked_words`, §11.11, and the recipient's
  own live blocked words); `IMAGE` — a `DM_IMAGE` upload (§11.1, processed like `POST_IMAGE`:
  re-encoded, metadata stripped); `VOICE` — a `DM_VOICE` clip (the CP-017 voice pipeline: `audio/mp4`,
  ≤ 1 MiB, ≤ 30 s); `EMOJI` — one of the owner's pack emojis as its token `:<pack>_<id>:` (§10.30
  list). An asset that is not the caller's unattached asset of that kind → 400 `mediaId` /
  `invalid_value`. **No moderation hold:** no moderation provider exists (and, v1.42-social, posts are
  visible at once too, §11.2), so — like stories (D91) — DM pictures are delivered at once and safety relies on
  requests (strangers cannot send pictures or voice), block, report and the 24-hour life.
  Order of checks: 400 body → the `clientId` retry → 400 `to` (`invalid_value`: oneself) → 404
  (`to` is not an ACTIVE account, or a block either way: **blocked people cannot message or see
  you**) → 403 `DM_NOT_ALLOWED` (privacy) → message-request rules (403 `DM_REQUEST_TEXT_ONLY`,
  403 `DM_REQUEST_LIMIT`, 429 `dm:request`) → 400 `mediaId` → stored.
- **Who may message you** (`PrivacySettings.whoCanMessage`, «من يستطيع مراسلتك»): `EVERYONE`
  (default), `FOLLOWING` (accounts you follow) or `NOBODY`. It is checked on **every** message,
  except in a conversation where you yourself have written (you started it or replied): then the
  other side may answer whatever the setting.
- **Message requests** («طلبات المراسلة»): a message to someone who does **not follow** the sender,
  in a conversation the recipient has neither accepted nor written in, is a request: it goes to the
  recipient's `REQUESTS` box (not counted in the Messages badge, `DmUnread.requests` instead). Until
  the recipient accepts (`acceptDmRequest`), replies, or follows the sender, the sender may send at
  most **`DM_REQUEST_MAX_MESSAGES` (3)** messages in it (the 4th → 403 `DM_REQUEST_LIMIT`; the
  count does not reset when messages expire or the request is deleted) and only `TEXT`, `EMOJI` or
  a gift (`IMAGE`/`VOICE` → 403 `DM_REQUEST_TEXT_ONLY`). The recipient accepts, deletes
  (`deleteDmConversation`, the sender is not told) or blocks (`PUT /users/{username}/block`).
- **Gifts in a conversation** (`sendDmGift`, `POST /dm/gifts` `{to, giftCode, quantity, source,
  clientId}` → 201 `DmGiftResult`, a retry → 200): the whole gift box of `getGiftCatalogue` — every
  category the catalogue lists, normal and `LUCKY` (MAX X) — through the **live gift pipeline**
  (§10.23, §10.27) with a conversation instead of a room: one recipient (the peer), the catalogue
  quantities, `COINS` or `BAG` (lucky: `COINS` only, its switch, region and 18+ gates), the same
  wallet charge and ledger (`DM_GIFT`; lucky `LUCKY_GIFT` and `LUCKY_GIFT_WIN`), the sender's family
  points, the lucky draw with the guarantee and the daily protection, the same idempotency
  (`clientId` is the send's id in `live_gifts`, whose `dm_conversation_id` is set and `room_id` is
  null), the same rate limits (`live:gift`, `live:gift:lucky`). Nothing room-only happens (no score,
  Contribution, popularity, wish list, data message or «لحظة الحظ» ticker). **The recipient's
  share** (what is counted for the recipient's charm, `ATTRACTIVENESS`, as the live host's share is):
  `GIFT_DM_RECIPIENT_SHARE_PERCENT` (owner: **50 %**) of the gift's coin value; the sender's
  support (and Wizard for lucky) count as in a live. **Exception — lucky gifts keep the lucky host
  share (`LUCKY_GIFT_HOST_SHARE_PERCENT`, 10 %)**: the lucky return is 85 % and 85 % + 50 % would
  give back more than was spent. In a conversation this share **replaces** the category's live
  share of §10.33 (`GIFT_HOST_SHARE_PERCENTS`): a paid quip, like any non-lucky gift, counts
  `GIFT_DM_RECIPIENT_SHARE_PERCENT`, and the send stores it as `live_gifts.host_share_bps` (lucky:
  the lucky share). **Quips** *(merge with v1.32-live, D154)*: a paid quip is sent as in a live
  (`COINS`, quantity 1, else 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`) without a room's queue (nothing plays for a
  room; the message shows it); a **free quip** (price 0) is the one free quip of a live and cannot
  be sent in a conversation — 409 `GIFT_UNAVAILABLE`, nothing charged or stored (the app does not
  offer it there). No coins are credited to the recipient (as in a live: a share is
  counted points, not coins). The gift shows as a `GIFT` message (icon, name from the catalogue,
  ×quantity, the lucky win). It follows every message rule above: the privacy setting, blocks, and
  a stranger's gift is a **request message** (it counts towards the 3, and the coins are spent even
  if the recipient never accepts — the app says so before sending, from `DmPeer.asRequest` or the
  conversation's `REQUEST_SENT`). Order: 400 body → retry → the
  checks of `sendDmMessage` (to, block, privacy, request limit) → the gift checks and charge of
  §10.23 (409 `GIFT_UNAVAILABLE`, 403 lucky gates, 409 `INSUFFICIENT_COINS` /
  `GIFT_BAG_INSUFFICIENT`). The gift message expires after 24 h like any message; the send, its
  ledger rows, draws and level credits are **permanent**.
- **24-hour life** *(owner)*: every message (any kind, read or unread) has `expiresAt` = sent +
  **`DM_RETENTION_HOURS` (24)**. From then on no read returns it and no count includes it; a sweeper
  (`DM_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, default 60; cannot be disabled in production) **hard-deletes** it
  with its picture or voice objects in bounded batches. The conversation stays (with
  `lastActivityAt`); with nothing left `lastMessage` is null. Deleting a message for everyone or a
  moderation removal sets `expiresAt` to now (the same path).
- **Delivery and read:** a message is *sent* (✓) once stored; `read` (✓✓) is true on the caller's
  own messages that the peer has read (`markDmRead {lastMessageId}`: everything received up to that
  message is read; `DmConversation.peerReadAt`). Unread counts: per conversation, and `getDmUnread`
  `{messages, conversations, requests}` — `messages` sums unread messages of accepted, **not
  muted** conversations (≤ 99; the tab badge), `requests` counts request conversations with unread
  messages. Expired, deleted and hidden messages are never counted.
- **Real time:** there is no socket for signed-in users; the app reads the open conversation's
  newest page while it is on screen (every 3 s, slowing to 15 s while nothing changes, paused in the
  background), the list and the badge every 30 s and on resume, and at once when a `dm` push arrives.
- **Delete:** a conversation **for me** (`deleteDmConversation`): everything up to now disappears for
  the caller (also a declined request); a new message brings it back with only the new messages. A
  message (`deleteDmMessage?scope=`): `me` — any message in the caller's conversation, for the caller
  only; `everyone` — the caller's own message within **`DM_DELETE_FOR_EVERYONE_SECONDS` (3 600)** of
  sending (later → 409 `DM_DELETE_WINDOW_PASSED`; someone else's → 403 `AUTH_FORBIDDEN`). Mute
  (`PUT` / `DELETE …/mute`): no push and not in the badge.
- **Search and unread mark** *(v1.43.1-social, D165)*: `listDmConversations?q=` keeps the box's order
  and returns only conversations whose peer's username or display name starts with `q`
  (case-insensitive, like §10.6 follow lists, D125). `markDmUnread` (`PUT …/unread`) marks a
  conversation unread for the caller only (the read pointer and the peer's ✓✓ do not move): it shows
  `markedUnread: true` and, while it has no unread message, counts as one unread message in
  `getDmUnread` (`messages` and `conversations` when accepted and not muted; `requests` for a
  request). `markDmRead` and `clearDmUnread` (`DELETE …/unread`) clear it; the app clears it when the
  conversation is opened.
- **Report** (`POST /reports {targetType: DM_MESSAGE}`): a message the reporter **received** and can
  still read. Because the message will be deleted, the report keeps a **snapshot** (kind, text,
  emoji token, gift, sender, time and a copy of the picture or voice file under
  `reports/dm/<messageId>.*`) for moderators (`Report.dmSnapshot`, admin views only). Retention: the
  snapshot lives while the report is open and **30 days after it is resolved**, then the sweeper
  clears it (text and file). `REMOVE_TARGET` removes the message (if it still exists). Reporting a
  whole conversation is a report of the person (`USER`). *(v1.93-social, D296, §10.109.5 — the owner's
  decision)* The snapshot also keeps **the whole conversation** as it was when reported (every message
  still there, at most 300, files for the newest 20), for a DM report and for a person reported from the
  conversation (`dmConversationId`); staff view only, every read audited; cleared with the snapshot.
- **Push** (§11.12, channel `kabso_messages`): a new message or gift is pushed to the recipient when
  they are ACTIVE, keep `messages` on, have not muted the conversation or the sender (§11.7) and
  there is no block either way; at most one per recipient per conversation per
  `PUSH_MESSAGES_GAP_SECONDS`; Android `tag` `dm:<conversationId>`. Title: the sender's display
  name; body: the text (masked, ≤ 100 code points), «📷 صورة» / "📷 Photo", «🎤 رسالة صوتية» /
  "🎤 Voice message", «ملصق» / "Sticker", «🎁 أرسل لك هدية ×N» / "🎁 Sent you a gift ×N"; a request
  says «طلب مراسلة: …» / "Message request: …". Data: `kind: dm`, `channel: messages`,
  `conversationId`, `messageId`, `senderUsername`. The open conversation plays and shows nothing
  (the app, §11.12).
- **Rate limits** (§7): `POST /dm/messages` 30 / min per user (`dm:send`,
  `RATE_LIMIT_DM_SEND_USER`); request messages additionally 20 / hour per user (`dm:request`,
  `RATE_LIMIT_DM_REQUEST_USER`, counted in the send after the request rules); `POST /dm/gifts` the
  live gift buckets; the other writes (`read`, `accept`, delete, mute) 300 / hour per user
  (`dm:write`, `RATE_LIMIT_DM_WRITE_USER`); reads the per-user default.
- *(v1.104-social, D339)* **Archived chats** «المؤرشفة» — §10.132; **group messages** «رسائل جماعية» — §10.133.
- **Not in v1.40-social:** group conversations (since v1.104-social, §10.133), typing and online indicators, message reactions,
  replies/quotes, forwarding and share-to-DM, video messages, captions on pictures, read-receipt
  opt-out, keeping a message beyond 24 h, end-to-end encryption, iOS pushes.

#### 11.13.1 The Messages tab's layout *(D336, app only — no wire change)*

Owner (2026-11-09), from a third-party reference (a Dribbble composite; the middle phone only — its layout, never
its photos, names, logo or texts; the image stays out of git, D40): «اجعلها مثل هذا التصميم مطابق 100٪». Sizes
were measured on the reference (533 px phone = 393 dp, 1.356 px/dp); colours are Kabso's tokens (red, not the
reference's blue / pink), light and dark; Arabic RTL mirrors English LTR. One scrolling page, top to bottom:

- **«القصص» / "Stories"** — the page title (30 sp bold, at 23 dp from the reading start) with a dark «+» disc
  (D336: a new story; **since D339 it makes a group** — «مجموعة جديدة», `/message-groups/new`, see below; a story
  is added from the caller's story card) and the paper plane (`AppIcons.send`, mirrored in Arabic; «رسالة جديدة», the D165
  sheet) at the reading end, on a 48 dp row under the status bar gap (D142).
- **Story cards** from `GET /feed/stories` (CP-008, the same tray as the posts page): the caller's card first —
  «أضف قصة» / "Add story" (89 × 152 dp, a faint red tint, their picture with a red «+»; a tap adds a story), or
  «قصتك» / "Your story" while they have one (a tap opens it; the «+» still adds) — then the followed accounts with
  active stories in the tray's order (97 × 152 dp, radius 12, 7 dp apart): their picture blurred behind, the
  ringed picture (red-to-gold while unseen, faint once seen), the name and the compact time of the newest story; a
  tap opens their stories. The tray carries no story media, so a card shows the account's own picture (red
  gradient without one). Loading, an empty tray or a failed tray show the caller's card alone — nothing is
  guessed. Followed accounts that are only live are not cards here (the posts page keeps D218's live ring).
  The stories step aside while the conversation search is open.
- **«الرسائل» / "Messages"** (23 sp bold) with, at the reading end, the **boxes button**, «من يستطيع مراسلتك»
  (D155) and search (D165, the field takes the title's place). *Owner follow-up (2026-11-09): «الدردشات، طلبات
  المراسلة، المؤرشفة، رسائل جماعية — يمكن وضع بجانب الفلتر خانة تفتحها، وأزلها كأيقونات».* No row of boxes in the
  page: the boxes button (a chevron that turns; «صناديق الرسائل» / "Message boxes"; also shown while searching —
  each box is searched on its own) carries the pending requests as a red count and opens a panel under the header
  (animated; instant with reduced motion) listing the boxes as rows — «الدردشات» and «طلبات المراسلة» with its
  count (D155). A row opens its box and closes the panel; tapping the button again closes it; the title names the
  requests box while it is open. *(D339, §10.132–§10.133)* The panel lists «الدردشات» (conversations **and groups**
  mixed by recency, `listDmChats`), «طلبات المراسلة» and «المؤرشفة» (`listDmChats?box=ARCHIVED`); groups have no box
  of their own. *Owner (2026-11-09): «ال+ في الاعلى … يجب ان يكون هذا الزر + زر عمل مجموعة».* The
  dark «+» disc of the «القصص» row opens «مجموعة جديدة» / "New group" (tooltip and label «مجموعة جديدة»); it is the
  only entry — there is no separate group button in the «الرسائل» header. Stories are added from «أضف قصة» /
  «قصتك»'s «+» on the caller's card.
- **Rows** (80.5 dp pitch): a 64 dp round picture at 23 dp, 20 dp to the text; the name (16 sp, medium; semibold
  while unread) with the verification seal (D293) and the muted icon; the preview (14.5 sp, tertiary grey, one
  line — pictures, voice, stickers and gifts as before); at the reading end the **compact time** («5د» / "5m",
  «3س» / "3h", «2ي» / "2d", a short date beyond 7 days; in words for screen readers) and under it the **red
  unread count** (24 dp, «99+» from 99; grey when muted; a dot when only marked unread). Long press keeps the
  D165 menu.

### 10.132 Archived chats «المؤرشفة» *(v1.104-social, DRAFT — D339)*

Owner (2026-11-09), on the D336 Messages tab: «الدردشات، طلبات المراسلة، المؤرشفة، رسائل جماعية — يمكن وضع بجانب الفلتر
خانة تفتحها»; then, for this work: «a user can archive/unarchive a conversation (per user, not for the other side) … a new
message from the other side unarchives it (Instagram/WhatsApp behaviour — pick one, document it)».

- **Per user.** `archiveDmConversation` / `unarchiveDmConversation` (`PUT` / `DELETE /dm/conversations/{id}/archive`;
  idempotent; `dm:write`) and `archiveDmGroup` / `unarchiveDmGroup` (`PUT` / `DELETE /dm/groups/{id}/archive`) set the
  caller's own archive time (`dm_participants.archived_at`, `dm_group_members.archived_at`). The other side is never
  told and sees nothing change. `DmConversation.archived` / `DmGroup.archived` carry it.
- **Where it shows.** An archived chat leaves «الدردشات» (`listDmChats?box=CHATS` and `listDmConversations?box=INBOX`)
  and is listed in «المؤرشفة» (`listDmChats?box=ARCHIVED`, the same order, search and cursor rules). It is not counted
  in the badge (`getDmUnread.messages` / `.conversations` / `.groups`). Muting is separate: an archived chat may be
  muted or not.
- **What brings it back — the decision (D339): classic WhatsApp.** A new message **from someone else** (the peer of a
  conversation; any other member of a group) clears the archive at once, in the send's transaction; the caller's
  **own** messages leave it archived (they are writing from «المؤرشفة» on purpose). Instagram's rule (a chat stays in
  its folder) and WhatsApp's newer «keep chats archived» setting were not chosen: with 24-hour messages (§11.13) a
  reply hidden in the archive would often expire unseen.
- **Requests.** A message request waiting for the caller cannot be archived (409 `DM_NOT_ARCHIVABLE`: accept or
  delete it, §11.13); a request the caller **sent** is in their chats and may be archived.
- **Delete for me** (§11.13) and archive are independent: a deleted conversation that comes back with a new message
  from the peer is also no longer archived.
- **App** (§11.13.1): «أرشفة» / "Archive" and «إلغاء الأرشفة» / "Unarchive" in the long-press menu of a row and in the
  conversation's ⋮ menu (a group's too); a swipe of a row towards the reading start archives it (towards the reading end
  in Arabic, mirrored); «المؤرشفة» is the third row of the boxes panel. Snack «تمت الأرشفة» / "Archived".

### 10.133 Group messages «رسائل جماعية» *(v1.104-social, DRAFT — D339)*

Owner (2026-11-09): «رسائل جماعية» in the Messages tab — create a group (a name, an optional photo, the members from
people you follow), the message types of a conversation, the members, admins, leave, rename, read state, a member cap,
report, mute and pushes. Every route needs a token (tag `messages`, `/dm/groups/…`).

- **A group** (`dm_groups`): a name (1–50 code points, one line, §6 hygiene), an optional photo (`DM_GROUP_PHOTO`: a
  centre-cropped square like `FAMILY_EMBLEM`, §11.1; a replaced or removed photo's files are deleted), its creator, and
  its members (`dm_group_members`, each with a role, mute, archive, a read pointer and the time they joined). Status
  `ACTIVE`, or `REMOVED` by moderation (gone for everyone: every read → 404).
- **Who may be added** — by the creator at creation, later by any ADMIN (`listDmGroupCandidates` lists exactly them):
  an ACTIVE account that is a **mutual follow** of the adder (the adder follows them and they follow the adder), with
  **no block either way** with the adder, whose «من يستطيع مراسلتك» (`whoCanMessage`, §11.13) is not `NOBODY`. Mutual
  follows because a group has no message-request step: nobody lands in a group of strangers. Checked under each pair's
  lock (the one follow and block use). Any other entry → 403 `DM_GROUP_MEMBER_NOT_ALLOWED` naming each refused entry
  with the same issue (a block is never told); oneself → 400 `members.<i>`; nothing changes.
- **The cap**: `DM_GROUP_MAX_MEMBERS` (server configuration like every `DM_*` number; default **100**, 3–256), the creator
  included; more → 409 `DM_GROUP_FULL`. Groups created: **2 a day** per user (owner; `dm:group`, §7 — the 3rd → 429 `RATE_LIMITED`; refused attempts count).
- **Roles.** The creator is an ADMIN who cannot be removed or demoted (they may leave). An ADMIN adds and removes
  members, renames the group, changes or removes its photo, makes members admins or admins members (not oneself: 400),
  and may delete any message. Any member leaves (`leaveDmGroup`). When no admin is left, the member who joined first
  becomes one; when the last member leaves, the group ends (its messages expire at once, its photo is deleted, it
  cannot be opened again).
- **Messages** (`sendDmGroupMessage`, `{kind, text|mediaId|token, clientId}`; 201, a retry → 200): `TEXT`, `IMAGE`
  (`DM_IMAGE`), `VOICE` (`DM_VOICE`) and `EMOJI` exactly as in a conversation (§11.13) — **no gifts in a group** (the gift
  pipeline has one recipient; D339 decision). The server's blocked words are masked (a group has no single recipient
  whose own live words would apply). The `CHAT_MUTE` restriction (§10.67) refuses it (403 `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED`). Each
  message lives **`DM_RETENTION_HOURS` (24 h)** and is hard-deleted by the DM sweeper with its file, like a direct
  message. A member reads the messages sent **since they joined**; messages between two people with a block either way
  are hidden from each other (the others still see both), and such a person is not listed in the other's members.
- **Read state**: one read pointer per member (`markDmGroupRead {lastMessageId}`, never back; sending moves one's own).
  `DmGroup.unreadCount` (≤ 99) per member; on one's own messages `DmGroupMessage.readCount` = how many other members'
  pointers reached it (no per-person list). `getDmUnread.groups` sums unread group messages that are neither muted nor
  archived (≤ 99); the app adds it to the tab badge.
- **Delete** (`deleteDmGroupMessage?scope=everyone`): one's own within `DM_DELETE_FOR_EVERYONE_SECONDS` (1 h; later →
  409 `DM_DELETE_WINDOW_PASSED`), or any message by an ADMIN; someone else's by a member → 403 `AUTH_FORBIDDEN`. There
  is no "delete for me" in a group (400 `scope`).
- **Mute** (`PUT` / `DELETE /dm/groups/{id}/mute`, the D155 pattern): no push, not in the badge. **Archive**: §10.132.
- **The list.** Groups are **mixed into «الدردشات»** by recency with the conversations (`listDmChats`, `DmChat {type:
  DIRECT|GROUP}`), one cursor; a group's `lastActivityAt` is its newest message or when the caller joined, whichever is
  later. `q` matches a group's name prefix. There is no separate groups box.
- **Push** (§11.12, channel `kabso_messages`): a new group message to every other member who is ACTIVE, keeps `messages`
  on, has not muted the group or the sender (§11.7) and has no block either way with the sender — one per member per
  group per `PUSH_MESSAGES_GAP_SECONDS`; Android `tag` `dmg:<groupId>`; title the group's name, body «<sender>: <the
  message>» (the §11.13 kinds' words). Being added: «<adder> أضافك إلى المجموعة» / "<adder> added you to the group".
  Data: `kind: dm_group`, `channel: messages`, `groupId`, `messageId` (messages only), `senderUsername`.
- **Report** (`POST /reports {targetType: DM_GROUP, targetId: <groupId>}`; a member only, else 404; once per open
  report): the report keeps a **snapshot** (`reports.dm_snapshot`): the name, the members (usernames as they were) and
  the newest 300 messages the reporter could read (text and emoji; pictures and voice are noted, their files are not
  copied — a minimal mirror of §10.109.5). Admin views: `Report.dmGroupSnapshot`; the staff app's report and its
  conversation view (`getStaffReportDmThread`, audited). `REMOVE_TARGET` removes the group for everyone (status
  `REMOVED`, its messages expire now, its photo is deleted). The snapshot is cleared 30 days after resolution (the
  members' names too). A group report is never put under an account's legal hold (D193): it is not one person's content.
- **Real time**: as §11.13 — the open group reads its newest page every 3 s (to 15 s while quiet), the list and the
  badge every 30 s and on a `dm_group` push.
- **Not in v1.104-social:** gifts, replies, reactions, mentions, system lines («فلان أضاف فلان»), invite links, a
  per-person read list, "delete for me", join requests, groups over 256.
- **App** (§11.13.1): the dark «+» at the top of the tab (the «القصص» row; owner: «ال+ في الاعلى … يجب ان يكون
  هذا الزر + زر عمل مجموعة»; the only entry) → «مجموعة جديدة» (the photo, the name, then the people from
  `listDmGroupCandidates` with search; «إنشاء»); a group row shows the group's photo (or a people disc) and «<sender>:
  <message>»; the group screen is the conversation screen with the sender's name over others' bubbles; its ⋮ menu has
  «معلومات المجموعة» (members, roles, add, remove, rename, photo), mute, archive, report and «مغادرة المجموعة».

### 11.14 Video posts and reels *(v1.41-social, DRAFT — D162, CP-023; CP-006 M2 without transcoding)*

- **Kinds and limits** (server-enforced): `POST_VIDEO` — `video/mp4` or `video/quicktime`, at most
  **209 715 200 bytes (200 MiB)** and **1–90 s** *(v1.45-social, D168, owner: «مدة الفيديو لا تتجاوز ٩٠
  ثانية»; 1–180 s before)*; `REEL_VIDEO` — the same types, at most
  **104 857 600 bytes (100 MiB)** and **1–60 s**; `VIDEO_POSTER` — an image (JPEG, PNG, WebP,
  ≤ 15 MiB), the video's first frame made on the phone, processed like `POST_IMAGE` (1 080 and
  320 px WebP and a blurhash). A video type for another kind, or another type for a video kind →
  400 `contentType` / `invalid_value`; a larger `byteSize` → 400 `byteSize` / `too_big`. The
  presigned PUT signs `Content-Type` and `Content-Length`, so storage refuses any other bytes.
  *(v1.45-social, D168)* Post videos stored before the 90 s limit keep their length and stay
  playable (`durationMs` up to 180 000); a `POST_VIDEO` asset longer than 90 s that is not attached
  yet can no longer be attached (`createPost` → 400 `mediaIds` / `invalid_value`, as for any asset
  that is not attachable). The database keeps the old 1–180 000 ms shape check for every row and a
  second check, created `NOT VALID`, that holds new and updated `POST_VIDEO` rows to 90 000 ms.
- **Completing a video** (`completeMediaUpload` with `{posterId}`). Check order: auth →
  `MEDIA_UPLOADS_ENABLED` → the slot (404) → body (`posterId` required for a video kind, refused for
  every other kind with `unknown_field`, and it must be a READY, unattached `VIDEO_POSTER` of the
  caller younger than 24 h, else `invalid_value` — the slot stays open) → the bytes. The server
  does not decode or re-encode the video. It checks: HEAD size = `byteSize`; the top-level boxes,
  read with ranged GETs — `ftyp` first, every box inside the file, exactly one `moov` of at most
  16 MiB and an `mdat`; `video/quicktime` ⇔ major brand `qt  ` (the bytes and the declared type
  agree); the length from `moov/mvhd` (at least 1 s, at most the kind's maximum; up to 500 ms of
  encoder padding is accepted and reported clipped to the maximum); at least one video track
  (`hdlr` `vide`) whose first sample entry is H.264 (`avc1`, `avc3`) or HEVC (`hvc1`, `hev1`); and
  the display size from that track's `tkhd` (a 90° / 270° matrix swaps width and height), 16–4 096 px
  per side. Anything else → 422 `MEDIA_INVALID`, the slot is closed and the object deleted.
- **Storage:** the bytes are copied unchanged by the storage service to
  `media/{mediaId}/video.mp4` (or `.mov`) with the declared type and an immutable cache header,
  then the upload object is deleted. The poster's two WebP objects become the video's poster and
  thumbnail and the poster asset no longer exists on its own. The asset is `type: VIDEO`: `url` the
  file, `thumbUrl` the poster at 320 px, `posterUrl` the poster at 1 080 px, `blurhash` the
  poster's, `width` / `height` the display size, `durationMs` the length. Like every asset it is
  attachable once, by its owner, within 24 h; never-attached videos and posters are swept with
  their objects.
- **Posts:** a `POST` holds text and/or either 1–10 `POST_IMAGE` assets **or exactly one**
  `POST_VIDEO` (a mix, two videos or another kind → 400 `mediaIds` / `invalid_value`). A **reel**
  (`CreatePostRequest.format: REEL`) holds exactly one `REEL_VIDEO` (none → 400 `mediaIds` /
  `required`, anything else → `invalid_value`) and an optional caption under the §11.2 text rules.
  Every other post rule applies to reels unchanged: drafts, scheduling, edits, pins, likes,
  comments, saves, reposts, views (§11.4), reports, hashtags, mentions, search, privacy and blocks.
  **Moderation:** *(v1.42-social, D162a)* a post or reel with a video is `VISIBLE` at once, like
  every post (§11.2); reports and `REMOVE_TARGET` are the safety net.
- **Lists:** `GET /feed/posts` lists `format: POST` only. `GET /feed/reels?tab=` lists reels only:
  `following` — reels of followed accounts and the caller's own, and reels reposted by followed
  accounts, newest first (a post appears once; muted and hidden left out); `trending` — the §11.3
  score over visible public reels published in the last 7 days, not the caller's own, at most 2
  per author in any 10, frozen for 10 minutes. *(v1.92-social, D294)* `mixed` — 1 `following` : 2
  `trending` as one frozen list, the posts home feed's rule; the app's reels page lists it alone (§10.107).
  Not personalised (M5). Profile grids, saved,
  reposts, search and hashtag pages list both formats; every item carries `format`.
- **Playback** (the app): the phone streams `url` (progressive download; storage serves byte
  ranges), shows `posterUrl` / `thumbUrl` until the first frame, and starts muted.
- **Not in v1.41-social:** server-side transcoding, HLS / adaptive bitrate and server-made
  thumbnails (CP-006 Q1, later — `url` stays a playable file, so clients need no change), video
  stories, video in direct messages and the live chat, trim / filters / music / editing (M6),
  mixing photos and a video in one post, personalised ranking (M5).

### 11.15 The reels page and reels nearby *(v1.68-social, DRAFT — D202)*

The Moments reels page (the owner's reference: a third-party composite, kept out of git; only its layout and type scale
are matched, with Kabso's colours, icons and data).

*(v1.92-social, D294)* The app no longer has Nearby: the reels page lists `tab=mixed` only, under the posts page's
header (§10.107); its tabs «متابَعون / لك / القريبة», the «المنشورات» chip and the «اختر بلدك» prompt are gone. The
API keeps `tab=nearby` exactly as below (additive contract; older apps).

- **Nearby:** `GET /feed/reels?tab=nearby` — visible public reels (`moderation: VISIBLE`, not a private account) whose
  author's country (`user_profiles.country_code`) is the caller's own `Me.country` (D133; chosen by the person, never
  inferred), newest first by `publishedAt` then id; never the caller's own, muted or hidden (§11.7); blocks both ways
  left out. A caller with no country → 200 with an empty page (the app shows «اختر بلدك» with the country picker). The
  keyset cursor is bound to the caller **and** the country: after a country change the old cursor → 400 `cursor` /
  `invalid_value`. Same `social:feed` bucket. `GET /feed/posts` has no `nearby` (400 `tab` / `invalid_value`).
- **Interactions** reuse §11.2–§11.5 unchanged: like / unlike (`PUT`/`DELETE /posts/{id}/like`), comments (§11.5),
  save (`PUT`/`DELETE /posts/{id}/save`), and an outside share counted once per user, post and UTC day
  (`POST /posts/{id}/shares` → `ShareState`). Counts shown are the API's (`likeCount`, `commentCount`, `shareCount`).
- **Share text** (the app): the system share sheet carries the author's handle and the caption's first line. There is
  **no public post link yet** — kabsolive.com never shows user content (§10.55) and the app has no app-link /
  universal-link setup — so no URL is invented; a reel link needs an owner decision (a public reel page or app links).
- **Not in v1.68-social:** a verified badge (no verified flag exists), sounds / music pages (the disc and «صوت أصلي ·
  {author}» are display only), translation of captions, personalised or distance-based nearby ranking.

### 10.66 Gift categories and the gift's files in the admin panel *(v1.46-live / v1.71-social, DRAFT — D207)*

Owner (2026-10-31): «يجب ان يكون صلاحية لاضافة او حذف او تعديل تصنيف. وعند اضافة هدية … الملف الاساسي الذي سيعرض بصيغة
mp4/mp3/svga وصورة لها». Owner answer: MP4 gift effects are of **both** kinds — a plain video (with its background,
played full screen as is) and side-by-side alpha — chosen per gift. Replaces the fixed tab list of §10.23 / §10.27 /
§10.33; nothing else of those sections changes.

- **Categories are rows** of `gift_categories`: `code` (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,39}$`, never changes), `kind` (`NORMAL` |
  `LUCKY` | `QUIPS`), `nameAr` / `nameEn` (1–30), `sortOrder` (0 … 10^6), `enabled`, an optional icon (PNG/WebP,
  square, 32–512 px, ≤ 256 KB). The migration seeds the five former values with the app's names in the former order.
  `gifts.category` is a foreign key to it. *(v1.100-social, D312: a third special kind, `CUSTOM` «مُخصَّص», seeded with the
  code `CUSTOM`; its gifts name an owner — §10.118.)* **Special kinds:** at most one LUCKY and one QUIPS category, each with the
  code equal to its kind — so every rule written as `category = 'LUCKY' | 'QUIPS'` (lucky draws §10.27, quips §10.33,
  boosters §10.58, the bag) keeps its meaning. A special category may be renamed, reordered and given an icon; it is
  never turned off or deleted, and no gift is moved into it by a delete.
- **Delete:** refused (409 `ADMIN_ACTION_REFUSED`, «… has N gift(s)») while gifts are in the category, unless the
  request names `moveTo`, another NORMAL category: the gifts move there and the category is deleted in one transaction
  (the category row is locked first); the audit row lists the moved gifts. An empty category is deleted at once.
- **Off:** a disabled category is not a tab; its gifts are neither listed (`getGiftCatalogue`, `getMyGiftBag`, wishes)
  nor sendable (409 `GIFT_UNAVAILABLE`), like a disabled gift.
- **The app's tabs** are `GiftCatalogue.tabs` (code, kind, name in the reader's language, icon URL) in the categories'
  sort order, enabled only (LUCKY only while `LUCKY_GIFTS_ENABLED`); `categories` stays as the codes for older apps.
  The panel keeps its look: Recent after Popular (after the first tab when there is no Popular), Lucky / Quips only
  when they have gifts, the bag last; the sub-category chips (§10.23) are unchanged. A category added in the panel
  takes the POPULAR host share.
- **Audit and permission:** every change needs a reason and writes `gift.category.add | update | enable | disable |
  delete` with `via` (`panel` / `cli`), the actor and the reason. Capability `gifts.categories` (OWNER); reading is
  `catalog.view`. `gift-admin category-*` runs the same rules.
- **The gift's files** are uploaded from the add / edit form (`uploadAdminGiftFile`, the raw bytes, `catalog.manage`)
  to content-addressed immutable keys under `media/gifts/<code>/`; the form then sends the keys and the gift change is
  the audited step (the server checks each key belongs to that gift and is in storage, and reads the effect's size and
  the sound's length itself):
  - «صورة الهدية» — **required** to create a gift in the panel: PNG/WebP, square (sides within 2 %), ≥ 128 px,
    ≤ 512 KB. It can be replaced, not removed. (`gift-admin --image` keeps D126's 1 MB / 64 px / 5:4 rule.)
  - «ملف العرض» — optional: an **SVGA 2.x** (≤ 25 MB, the CLI's checks) or an **MP4**: an MPEG-4 file with an H.264
    (`avc1` / `avc3`) video track, 1 … 15 s (+0.5 s encoder padding), ≤ 8 MB, 16–4096 px, read from its boxes (no
    decode; no ffprobe in the API image). «الشفافية» `NONE` (a plain video) or `SIDE_BY_SIDE` (left half colour,
    right half the alpha mask): the upload answers `detectedAlpha` (SIDE_BY_SIDE when width ≥ 1.8 × height), the
    admin may change it, and it is stored per gift (`Gift.animationAlpha`; required with an MP4, refused with an SVGA).
  - A sound — optional, alone or with either effect: an **MP3** (MPEG audio Layer III frames, ID3 allowed), 0.1 … 15 s,
    ≤ 1 MB; never on a QUIPS gift (it has its bundled sound).
  - «إزالة» clears the effect or the sound (`null`). The panel previews from `getAdminGiftFile` (same origin: the
    image, the MP4 — side-by-side composited on a canvas —, the SVGA's bitmaps, the MP3).
- **The app** downloads `animationUrl` / `audioUrl` on demand into the gift-art cache (D126; small ones prefetched when
  the panel opens) and plays: an SVGA as before; an MP4 with `video_player` (already a dependency) from the cached
  file — *(D309, owner from a device: «أليس من المفترض ظهورها بشكل كامل»)* a **plain** one (`NONE`, its own
  background) fills the **whole live screen** as decided above («played full screen as is»): scaled to cover it,
  centred, over the header and the chat (a video of another shape loses an equal strip at two opposite edges, never
  a band of the room; upload it at the phone's shape, e.g. 1080 × 2340, to lose nothing) —, a side-by-side one
  (transparent) fitted like an SVGA (full width, on the bottom edge) through the fragment shader
  `shaders/gift_alpha_sbs.frag` (`ImageFilter.shader`, Impeller); the MP3 with the effect (or alone, for its length).
  Sound — the SVGA's, the MP4's own (only when there is no MP3), the MP3 — plays only while «المؤثرات الصوتية» is on,
  the live's local sound switch is not muted and the app is in the foreground. What the device cannot play (an
  unknown format, side-by-side without shader support, a file that fails) is skipped: the strip's picture is all that
  shows, never an error.
- D272b (owner: «حاول اصلاح المشكلة بالكامل», after D272's entry car): the gift's SVGA goes through the app's **one
  SVGA engine** (`lib/core/svga/svga_engine.dart`, shared with the VIP perks, the PK battle emoji and the profile
  headers). As a gift with an animation **arrives** (it plays now or waits in the queue) its art is read ahead: an
  SVGA downloaded and read on **another isolate** (`SvgaDocs.warm`, the 4 latest files kept), an MP4 and an MP3
  downloaded to the device. The effect then decodes the pictures at the size they are drawn (the drawn area across the
  screen's width, never bigger than the picture), keeps them for a small clip (≤ 12 M pixels, all clips ≤ 24 M: a
  combo replays at once) or reads a big one through a window of about a second (released behind), and **starts only
  when its first second is ready** — within `animationWait` (8 s) from the effect's start, else skipped (the strip
  has shown the gift; the file goes on being read for the next send). The clock picks the frame and the sound
  (`GiftEffectSound`: from its `startFrame`, `startTime` ms in); a late picture keeps the last frame a moment.
  Drawing past the canvas still shows in the drawn area (D145c). A file with **vector shapes or clip paths** plays on
  the package's player as before, but read and decoded by the engine (`SvgaDoc.toMovie`). The MP4 path was already off
  the UI thread (the platform's decoder); it gains the download ahead. Queue, combo and hold timing are unchanged.

### 10.116 Rooms rank by their cherries «ترتيب الغرف بالكرز» *(v1.86-live, DRAFT — D310)*

Owner (2026-11-08): «ترتيب الغرف اجعله بالكرز … كل 1 مليون كوينز يرسل يصل 6.5 مليون كرزة ولصانع المحتوى 7 مليون». Approved
points: the ranking value is the real cherries the cherry ledger credited in this live to the host AND the guests on seats
together (each send's stored share, never recomputed); heart taps no longer count (they stay for the charm level, §10.18);
lucky gifts count their real cherries (10 % → 1 a coin), quips and the rest their stored share; the hub chip, the room card
and the host pill show cherries; the popularity boards (§10.15) and PK points stay on points.

- **`live_rooms.cherries`** (`LiveRoomSummary.cherries`, `LiveScore.roomCherries`): per live send, the sum of every
  recipient's `GIFT_RECEIVED` credit of that send (floor(coins × the send's stored `host_share_bps` × CHERRIES_PER_COIN),
  §10.46: a normal gift 65 % → 6.5 a coin, a content creator's live 70 % → 7, a custom gift 60 % → 6 (§10.118), a lucky
  gift its stored share — 10 % → 1, a quip its share; a free quip nothing). Added in the send's own transaction right after
  the ledger credit (the room row is already locked by the send). Every recipient of a live send is the host or seated, so
  the host and the seated guests count; a recipient gifting themself counts as credited. **A reversal**
  (`reverseGiftCherriesIn`) takes the reversed `GIFT_RECEIVED` credits back out (never below 0), in its own transaction.
  Taps, PK boosters' points, the score and viewers never change it. A new live starts at 0 (D129: the ranking belongs to
  one live).
- **Order:** `popular` = `cherries` desc, `startedAt` desc, `id` desc (§10.4); `featured=true` after the feature rank; the
  D295 host / creator interleave uses the same key; «رائج» (`LiveRoomSummary.popular`, §10.89) is the top
  `LIVE_POPULAR_TOP_N` of each kind in this order. Indexes `live_rooms_live_popular_cherries_idx` and
  `live_rooms_live_cat_popular_cherries_idx` replace the score ones.
- **Cursor:** format v3 — `n` is the room's cherries. A v2 cursor (the score) → 400 `cursor` / `invalid_value`, like any
  unknown version; an app paging across the deploy reloads the list once.
- **Live updates:** the media room metadata carries `roomCherries` next to `score` and `hostCherries` (the same 2-second
  throttle, left out at 0). Apps read a missing key as "unknown" and fall back to `hostCherries` (older servers).
- **The apps:** the host pill (video, multi, audio, podcast; host and viewer) shows `roomCherries`; the host's own seat
  tile and the data pages keep `hostCherries` (§10.95, the host's own share). *Owner follow-up (2026-11-08, «أرى أن
  المعلومات على بطاقة البث كثيرة»):* the hub card draws no number but the viewers — one type badge (Live / PK / multi /
  the voice kinds' label) and the viewer count (0 included; no «جديد»), a small creator mark on a creator's live, and the
  title alone (the host's name when empty, 2 lines). `cherries` still orders the list and stays in the response.
- **Unchanged:** `LiveRoomSummary.score` / `LiveScore.total` (points), the popularity boards (§10.15, points), PK points
  (§10.58), the charm level from taps (§10.18), the Contribution list (§10.12).
- **Backfill:** the migration fills the rooms LIVE at deploy from the ledger itself (`GIFT_RECEIVED` + `GIFT_REVERSAL` of
  each send's recipients), so any CHERRIES_PER_COIN is exact; an ENDED room keeps 0 (it is never listed).

### 10.117 «إجراءات المؤسس» — the founder's moderation actions in the app *(v1.99-social, DRAFT — D311)*

Owner (2026-11-08): «يمكنه حذف او حظر او تحذير اي شخص», and he chose **no code (no authenticator, no password)** for these —
a confirmation dialog only. **Owner decision recorded:** D286 / D288 kept the permanent ban and the account deletion behind
the panel's step-up for the staff; the OWNER waives that for himself, in the app only. Every other role is unchanged (the
panel and the staff tools keep their rules).

- **`createOwnerModerationAction`** — `POST /owner/users/{userId}/actions` `{action, reason (1–500, trimmed), days?,
  clientId}`; 201 `OwnerModerationResult`, or 200 with the first result for a retry with the same `clientId` (nothing
  done again; unique `(actor, clientId)`, a concurrent retry answered the same way).
