### 10.142 «رمز الدعوة أو رمز المشرف»: one sign-up code, the personal link, credit only for a new person *(v1.108-social, DRAFT — D343)*

Owner (2026-11-09): «في انشاء الحساب هناك صندوق يدخل شخص اما رمز الدعوة او رمز المشرف الذي استقطبه. يمكن للمشرف ايضاً
ارسال رابطه للشخص ليقوم بتحميل التطبيق والنظام يأخذ المستخدم الجديد وحده بحيث يدخل رمز الدعوة تلقائي عند انشاء حساب،
النظام يعرف ان كان الشخص قام بتحميل التطبيق قبل المرة يلا يعتبره مستخدم جديد ولا حالة استقطاب. واريد تصميم صفحة انشاء
الحساب بشكل ابسط وازالة كابي من الصفحة هذه». Builds on D217 (§10.71, invite codes), D223 (§10.75, the stable device id),
D250 (sessions keep the device HMAC) and D285 (§10.96.13, recruitment by staff). §10.132–§10.141 are left for the work
in flight.

- **The codes accepted** (one optional field, `RegisterRequest.referralCode`, ≤ 200 characters, spaces / dashes ignored,
  any case, an invite link `…/i/<code>` read): **INVITE** — a D217 invite code of an ACTIVE account (8 characters, no
  `O`); **SUPERVISOR** — a staff ID «Kabso07» (`@` optional, leading zeros optional) of an ACTIVE staff member holding
  MODERATION or BD now (D285's recruiters). They never collide (every staff ID contains `O`). Not accepted: staff
  usernames (the field names a code, and a staff ID is public), SUPPORT / FINANCE / OWNER staff IDs (they do not
  recruit), agency invite codes (D179: they attach an existing host to an agency, with the agency's approval — not a
  sign-up attribution; owner decision if wanted).
- **Validation, server side.** `checkSignupCode` (`POST /api/v1/auth/signup-code/check`, public, `signup_code:ip`
  RATE_LIMIT_SIGNUP_CODE_IP 30 / 10 min): 200 `{kind, code}` (the stored form), or 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` `code`
  `invalid_format` / `not_found`. `register` answers the same 400 on `referralCode` before the username, the password
  hash and the email are looked at (the answer depends on the code only — no address is revealed). `not_found` covers
  unknown, a closed or suspended account, a staff ID of someone who left the team or does not recruit — never told
  apart; nothing about the owner of a code is returned (no name, no username). The programme switched off (D217
  `enabled` false) does not make an invite code unknown: the account is created without a referral, as before.
- **Attribution** (once the account exists, in a transaction of its own after the account's — no attribution problem
  ever fails a sign-up): an INVITE code makes the D217 referral (`attachReferralIn`, source SIGNUP); a SUPERVISOR code
  makes one `staff_signup_recruits` row `{user, recruiter, code, status GRANTED | WITHHELD, withholdReason, createdAt}`
  (audited `staff.recruit.signup` `{code, recruiter, status, reason}`). A GRANTED row makes that supervisor the
  recruiter of the person's later host / creator / agency / recharge-agent application (`recruiterOfForm`; the form's
  own field is then not read) while the supervisor can still recruit; the D285 attribution then happens at the
  activation as before, with its commission. The supervisor's sign-ups are counted in `getMyStaffRecruits`
  (`signups.granted` / `withheld`); the OWNER sees them in `listAdminSignupRecruits` (`recruits.view`).
- **Cannot be changed after sign-up.** An account with a supervisor row cannot enter an invite code later
  (`applyReferralCode` 409 `REFERRAL_NOT_ALLOWED` `ALREADY_REFERRED`); a referral stays one per account (D217); a
  supervisor row is never edited (D285's OWNER reassignment applies to recruitments, not to this row).
- **Credit only for a new person** (both kinds). The account is always created; only the credit is withheld, with the
  reason, in order:
  - `SELF_DEVICE` (INVITE): the device's other accounts include the inviter (also D217's install-id rule);
  - D217's `SELF_EMAIL`, `SELF_IP`, `DUPLICATE_DEVICE`, `DUPLICATE_EMAIL` (INVITE) unchanged;
  - `RECRUITER_INACTIVE` (SUPERVISOR): the supervisor could not recruit any more at the account's creation;
  - **`DEVICE_HAD_ACCOUNT`**: the new account's device (its `device_signups` HMAC, D223) knew another account — one
    created on it (any status: a purged account's tombstone row too) or one signed in on it (any `sessions` row with the
    same `device_hash`, signed-out ones too, D250). Without a device key (the website, an app older than D223) this half
    cannot run (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS);
  - **`EMAIL_HAD_ACCOUNT`**: another account was created with the same mailbox (alias-folded like D217:
    `canonicalEmail`) — live, or purged less than SIGNUP_IDENTITY_RETENTION_DAYS ago.
  A withheld INVITE is a REJECTED referral (no reward, D217's panel shows the reason); a withheld SUPERVISOR is a
  WITHHELD row (never the recruiter of a later application). **No fingerprinting:** no IP or user-agent matching is
  used for this rule (D217's existing SELF_IP inviter check is unchanged).
- **What is kept (data minimisation).** The device: nothing new — the D223 HMAC already kept per account
  (`device_signups`) and per session. The mailbox: `signup_email_marks` `{user_id, email_hash, created_at, purged_at}` —
  HMAC-SHA-256 of the canonical mailbox under a key from HKDF(SIGNUP_DEVICE_KEY when set, else RATE_LIMIT_KEY_SECRET;
  info `signup-email/v1`), never the address; written at the account's creation, and by the referral sweeper (500 per
  run) for accounts that existed before the migration (the key is not in the database). Read only by this rule; never
  shown (not in the panel, not in the data export — an internal anti-abuse signal like D223's).
- **Deletion and retention.** At the purge (D193) the mark gets `purged_at`; SIGNUP_IDENTITY_RETENTION_DAYS (default
  **365**, 30–2557) later the referral sweeper deletes it — after that the mailbox counts as new again. The device HMAC
  follows D223 (kept with the tombstone). A `staff_signup_recruits` row stays with the tombstone like D285's
  recruitments (ids, the staff ID typed, the status; no personal data). Changing the key source makes every mailbox new.
- **The personal link.** A supervisor's is `<APP_PUBLIC_URL>/i/<staffId>` (`StaffRecruitList.signupLink`,
  `signupCode`; app: «رابطك الشخصي» on «استقطاباتي» with «نسخ الرابط» / «مشاركة»); an inviter's stays
  `MyReferral.link` (D217). The website's `/i/<code>` (Caddy → `invite.html`): Kabso branding, the code with «نسخ
  الرمز», «مشرف من كابسو لايف يدعوك» for a staff ID, and the download buttons of `config.json` `apps`:
  - **Google Play** (shown when `apps.playListed` is true): `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=<androidPackage>
    &referrer=kabso_code%3D<code>`; the app reads the Play Install Referrer once per install (Google's
    `com.android.installreferrer:installreferrer:2.2` over the `com.kabso/install_referrer` channel — no pub package)
    and pre-fills the field with «أُضيف تلقائياً من رابط الدعوة. يمكنك إزالته.»; the code is kept in the app's
    preferences until a sign-up is sent with it or the person removes it;
  - **the direct APK** (`apps.apkUrl`, the staging mirror `https://live.<domain>/app/`) and **the App Store**
    (`apps.appStoreUrl`): no referrer exists, so the page explains «لديك رمز دعوة؟» → «لصق الرمز», and the app reads
    the clipboard **only when «لصق الرمز» is tapped** (never on open, never silently).
  The text follows the buttons shown (owner, int21): Google Play is named only while its button is shown — with
  `apps.playListed` false the page reads «حمّل التطبيق وأنشئ حسابك، ثم انسخ الرمز والصقه في «لديك رمز دعوة؟» عند إنشاء
  الحساب.» and never mentions Google Play; the note under the buttons says «بعد تثبيت التطبيق» (the APK or the App Store).
  The page stays tracker-free (`scripts/check-site-no-tracking.sh`): plain links, no cookie, no third-party script; the
  code leaves the page only inside the Play link the visitor taps.
- **The app's sign-up page** (owner: «ابسط وازالة كابي»): no Kabi stage (AuthScaffold without `hero`: the wordmark, the
  back button and the language switch in the bar, the title), the fields as before, the code field collapsed under
  «لديك رمز دعوة؟» unless pre-filled, a live check under the field after a 500 ms pause («رمز دعوة من صديق» / «رمز
  المشرف Kabso07» / «الرمز غير صحيح. تأكد منه أو اتركه فارغاً.»; offline: nothing), the 400 shown on the field, one
  primary button. Login keeps its own design (it never used this layout).

### 10.143 «الشحن من الموقع» inside the app, signed in; Stripe's fee in the website price *(v1.109-social, DRAFT — D344)*

Owner 2026-11-09: «زر الشحن من الموقع يدخلك متصفح خارج التطبيق ويطلب اليوزر والباسورد. اريد جعل الشحن من الموقع يفتح من
نفس التطبيق ويدخل اليوزر والباسورد تلقائي دون ملاحظة الشخص». The person never types anything — but **no password is ever
passed, stored or filled in**: the app's own session vouches for the website once. §10.53 is unchanged otherwise.

#### 10.143.1 The one-time website sign-in

- **Mint** (`POST /wallet/topup-session`, the app's access token): 32 random bytes (base64url, 43 characters); the server
  stores only their **SHA-256** (`topup_handoffs.code_hash`, unique) with the user, the **minting session**, `expires_at`
  = now + **60 s** (a CHECK bounds it to 60 s) and `consumed_at`. A new code deletes the session's unused one and the
  caller's expired ones (the table stays small). The answer is `websiteUrl` =
  `<TOPUP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/topup?lang=ar|en#h=<code>` (`lang` from `Accept-Language`) and `expiresAt`. The code rides in
  the **fragment**: browsers never send a fragment to a server or in a `Referer`, so it is in no Caddy or API access log
  (the API logs paths without the query anyway). Audited `topup.handoff.mint` (the handoff id, the platform — never the
  code). 503 `TOPUP_UNAVAILABLE` when top-ups are off or the link is off for the session's platform (below); 429 after
  `RATE_LIMIT_TOPUP_HANDOFF_USER` (10 / 10 min per user).
- **The page** (`/topup`, D190's): its script first takes `#h=` out of the address (`history.replaceState`, before any
  request), then sends the code once to `POST /topup/handoff` without an `Authorization` header. 200 → it keeps the
  access token in the tab's `sessionStorage`, exactly as after its own sign-in (D190: **no cookie**; the website top-up
  page lives on the API's host, not on kabsolive.com, and sets no cookie at all — the kabsolive.com no-tracker / no-cookie
  rule of D198 is untouched). Anything else → the normal sign-in form, no error message and no retry loop; a 503 shows
  «الشحن بالبطاقة غير مفعّل». Direct visitors sign in as before.
- **Exchange** (`POST /topup/handoff`, public; body `{handoff}` only, 400 otherwise): one SQL `UPDATE … SET consumed_at
  WHERE code_hash = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now() RETURNING …` — of concurrent requests exactly one
  wins. Then the code counts only while the **minting session** is not revoked or expired, the account is `ACTIVE`, not
  locked (D208), and the session's device not banned (D250). So signing out, «تسجيل الخروج من الأجهزة الأخرى», a team
  revocation, a password reset, a suspension, a deletion request or a device ban void every pending code (deleting the
  session or the account deletes them: CASCADE). Success creates a **new session** (platform `web`, «Kabso website
  (app)», the app session's device hash and install id, the request's IP / user agent) and answers `{accessToken,
  accessTokenExpiresAt, username}` — **no refresh token** (the page never refreshes; after 15 minutes it asks to sign in).
  Every refusal (unknown, used, expired, voided) is the same **410 `TOKEN_EXPIRED`**; audited `topup.handoff.exchange` or
  `topup.handoff.refused` (`used`, `expired`, `session_revoked`, `account_not_active`, `account_locked`, `device_banned`;
  never the code; an unknown code has no account and is not audited). 429 after `RATE_LIMIT_TOPUP_HANDOFF_IP` (30 /
  10 min per IP). An `Authorization` header sent along is ignored: the code alone names the account.
- **Logs:** `handoff` and `websiteUrl` are redacted keys (`REDACT_PATHS`); a bare 43-character base64url value is masked
  in free text (SEC-017's pattern).
- **The app** opens `websiteUrl` in an **in-app browser tab** — url_launcher's `LaunchMode.inAppBrowserView` (Android
  Custom Tabs, iOS `SFSafariViewController`; the plugin already pinned, 6.3.2, no lockfile change). Not a WebView: Stripe's
  3-D Secure, Google Pay and Apple Pay are not reliably supported in one, and the website keeps its own origin, cookie
  jar and address bar. The tab has its own close button back to the wallet; when the app is in front again the balance is
  read again (`AppLifecycleListener.onResume`). Android needs the `CustomTabsService` `<queries>` entry; without a Custom
  Tabs browser the system browser opens. If the code cannot be had (offline, an older server) the plain
  `websiteTopupUrl` opens and the website asks to sign in.
- **Per store** (`TOPUP_APP_LINK_PLATFORMS`, default `android,ios` = D190's behaviour): `websiteTopupUrl` (and the mint)
  only for a session whose sign-in platform is listed; a session of another or no platform only when both are. The
  panel / `TOPUP_APP_LINK_ENABLED` switch still turns it off everywhere. Whether a store allows the link is the owner's
  decision (PP-79).
- Migration `20270416090000_topup_handoffs`.

#### 10.143.2 Stripe's fee in the website price

Owner 2026-11-09: «اسعار الشحن من الموقع يجب اضافة عليها عمولة stripe». The website price is grossed up so that, after
Stripe takes `percent × charged + fixed`, Kabso keeps at least the package's base price (`TOPUP_PACKAGES` ×
`COIN_RETAIL_USD_PER_MILLION`):

`charged = ceil((base + fixed) / (1 − percent))` — integer arithmetic in the currency's minor unit (USD cents today; the
formula is the same for a zero-decimal or a three-decimal currency), rounded up once.

- **One all-inclusive price** per package (`TopupPackages.priceMinor`, the one Checkout line's `unit_amount`) — never a
  separate «fee» line or field: surcharging consumer cards is forbidden in the EU / UK (legal review, PP-79). The coins
  of a package do not change; in-app recharge agents and store purchases are unaffected.
- **Rates:** env `TOPUP_STRIPE_FEE_GROSS_UP` (default `true`), `TOPUP_STRIPE_FEE_PERCENT` (0–20, two decimals; default
  **2.9**), `TOPUP_STRIPE_FEE_FIXED_MINOR` (0–10000 cents; default **30**). The defaults are **placeholders** (Stripe's US
  list price for domestic cards); the OWNER sets the account's real rates in «الدفع (Stripe)» («اضبطها حسب نسبة حسابك في
  Stripe»: `stripeFeeGrossUp`, `stripeFeePercentBps`, `stripeFeeFixedMinor`, null = the server's; OWNER only, code +
  reason, audited `payment.settings.update`), shown with `feeCurrency` and an example price.
- **Each order** keeps `base_price_minor`, `fee_percent_bps`, `fee_fixed_minor` (0 when the gross-up is off) next to
  `amount_minor`, and the checkout's audit row repeats them. After the webhook credits an order the API reads the fee
  Stripe really took (the charge's balance transaction) into `stripe_fee_minor`; when it is more than `amount − base` the
  server logs a warning and audits `topup.fee.exceeded` (the rates are too low, e.g. international cards or currency
  conversion). Best effort: a failure is logged, never fails the webhook, and **never changes the coins**. A bank
  transfer's fee is lower than a card's; the same price applies.
- Migration `20270416090100_topup_stripe_fee` (the three settings with CHECKs; the four order columns with a CHECK).

#### 10.143.3 «الشحن من الموقع» only in the direct APK: the install source *(v1.112-social, DRAFT — int21)*

Owner (2026-11-09, «موافق على الاقتراحات» on D345 #7 + D344): a build installed from a store never shows the website
link; the direct APK keeps it.

- **The app reports where it was installed from** (`InstallSource`): Android asks the system for the installer package
  (`PackageManager.getInstallSourceInfo(…).installingPackageName`, API 30+, else `getInstallerPackageName`) over the
  `com.kabso/device_id` channel (`installerPackage`) — `com.android.vending` (Google Play) ⇒ **PLAY**, anything else or
  none (the browser / a file manager / adb: the direct APK) ⇒ **SIDELOAD**; iOS is always **APP_STORE** (TestFlight
  counts as the App Store: it is reviewed by Apple). The web and other platforms report nothing. Asked once per run;
  if the platform call fails, nothing is reported (never a guess).
- **Sent** in `DeviceInfo.installSource` with every sign-in (`login`, `registerVerify`, and the other paths that create
  a session) and in the `refresh` body (`installSource`, optional) on each token refresh, so a session signed in before
  the app was updated — or a phone that moved from the APK to the Play build with the same sign-in kept — gets the
  current source within one access-token lifetime. The server keeps the latest on the session (`sessions.install_source`,
  CHECK PLAY | APP_STORE | SIDELOAD; omitted on a refresh: kept). An unknown value is a 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`.
- **The rule** (`appLinkShownFor`): the master switch (`TOPUP_APP_LINK_ENABLED` / the panel), then
  `TOPUP_APP_LINK_PLATFORMS` (§10.143.1, unchanged), then **`TOPUP_APP_LINK_SOURCES`** — comma-separated PLAY, APP_STORE,
  SIDELOAD; empty = none; **default SIDELOAD**. A session that reported no source (an app older than this, the website)
  is **not** offered the link. Both `RechargePackages.websiteTopupUrl` and the mint (`createTopupWebsiteSession` → 503
  `TOPUP_UNAVAILABLE`) follow it. The app needs no other change: it shows the link only when `websiteTopupUrl` is set.
- **Honest limits.** The source is what the app says (a modified APK could claim anything): this is a store-policy
  display rule — a store build simply never shows the link — not a security boundary; the website top-up itself stays
  open to anyone signed in there. An app older than this build shows no link until it is updated (it never reports).
- Migration `20270418090100_session_install_source` (nullable column + CHECK; no backfill, no table rewrite).

### 10.144 Coins from the stores «الشراء من المتجر» — Google Play Billing and App Store In-App Purchase *(v1.110-social, DRAFT — D345)*

Owner (2026-11-09): sell coins through the stores (consumable packages); store purchases are **open** (no cap), with a
server switch «شراء واحد لكل حساب وجهاز» (default **off**). **A refund is fraud:** any store refund, void or chargeback
takes the coins back (the balance may go below 0), **bans the account and the device** automatically with the reason
shown in the panel, and only the OWNER lifts it («فك الحظر», audited, with a reason). A **no-refund policy** is shown
before every purchase with explicit consent and in the terms; the server **answers the store** — Apple's
`CONSUMPTION_REQUEST` with the consumption information (only with the buyer's consent), Google's voided purchases polled
daily and on demand (Google has no consumption API and decides refunds itself). §10.141–§10.143 are left for D342–D344.

This replaces §10.53's «never inside the app» for the **stores' own billing only**: the website's card top-up (§10.53)
and the recharge agents are unchanged.

#### 10.144.1 Off unless configured

- **Per store.** Google Play is on when `STORE_IAP_GOOGLE_PACKAGE_NAME` and `STORE_IAP_GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE` (the
  service-account JSON's **path**, read at boot) are set; the App Store when `STORE_IAP_APPLE_BUNDLE_ID`,
  `STORE_IAP_APPLE_ISSUER_ID`, `STORE_IAP_APPLE_KEY_ID`, `STORE_IAP_APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` (the `.p8` path) and
  `STORE_IAP_APPLE_ROOT_CERT_FILES` (Apple's root certificate(s), DER or PEM, comma-separated paths) are set. A partial
  set, an unreadable file or a key of the wrong kind **refuses to boot**. No secret is ever in git, chat, a response, a
  log or an audit row. Optional: `STORE_IAP_APPLE_APP_ID` (the numeric Apple ID; checked on notifications when set),
  `STORE_IAP_GOOGLE_RTDN_TOKEN` (≥ 32 characters; switches the RTDN endpoint on).
- A store that is off: `getStoreIapCatalog` says `available: false, unavailableReason: OFF` (the app hides «الشراء من
  المتجر»), `verifyStorePurchase` and that store's notification endpoint answer 503 **`STORE_IAP_UNAVAILABLE`** (no
  `Retry-After`).
- **Sandbox.** Apple's `Sandbox` / Xcode environments and Google test purchases (`purchaseType` 0, licence testers) are
  **accepted while `STORE_IAP_ACCEPT_SANDBOX=true`** (default true: App Review and Play pre-launch testing buy in the
  sandbox against the production server) and recorded `environment: SANDBOX` (shown in the panel); false refuses them
  with 400 `STORE_IAP_VERIFICATION_FAILED` `{field: environment, issue: sandbox}`. Production purchases are always
  `PRODUCTION`. Owner (int21): keep it on until the App Store approves the app, then turn it off in production (PP-80).

#### 10.144.2 The catalogue «باقات المتجر»

`iap_products` (panel, `store_iap.manage` = OWNER; audited `store_iap.product.create|update` with a reason): one row per
**store and product id** (the id created in Play Console / App Store Connect, `[A-Za-z0-9._]{1,150}`) → **coins**
(1 … 10^12), an optional **reference price in US cents** (shown in the panel; used only for the lifetime amounts below),
a sort order and **enabled**. Never deleted (switched off), so purchases keep their product. The price the buyer pays is
the store's (localized by the store); the app shows the store's price string. A product id the server does not know, or
a disabled one, is never credited at verification (400 `STORE_IAP_VERIFICATION_FAILED` `{field: productId}`) — a product
switched off after the purchase started is still credited (the buyer paid; `enabled` only hides it).

#### 10.144.3 The app's flow

1. `GET /store/iap/catalog?platform=ANDROID|IOS` (`getStoreIapCatalog`) → `{available, unavailableReason, platform,
   products: [{productId, coins}], consentVersion, oncePerAccountDevice, accountToken}`. `unavailableReason`: `OFF`,
   `DEVICE_BANNED` (the session's device has an active ban, §10.91.6), `LIMIT_REACHED` (the switch is on and this account
   or this device already bought), else null. `accountToken` binds a purchase to the account: iOS sends it as StoreKit 2's
   `appAccountToken` (the account id, a UUID); Android as `obfuscatedAccountId` (SHA-256 hex of
   `kabso-live/store-account/v1|<account id>`).
2. The **consent sheet** (every purchase, before the store sheet): the package, «تُسلَّم العملات فوراً وتُستهلك عند
   استخدامها، ولا تُسترد بعد الشراء.», «طلب استرداد عبر المتجر يعدّ احتيالاً: تُسحب العملات ويُحظر الحساب والجهاز.», and
   «أوافق على مشاركة بيانات استخدام هذه العملات مع Apple/Google عند طلب استرداد.» — the purchase button stays disabled until
   the box «أوافق على سياسة عدم الاسترداد» is ticked (English mirrors it). Both statements are one consent (the owner's
   «الموافقة تشمل ذلك»): `consent: {accepted: true, version, shareConsumptionData: true}` (a different version: 400
   `{field: consent.version, issue: stale}`; `accepted` not true: 400 `{field: consent.accepted}`).
3. The store sheet (`in_app_purchase`); then `POST /store/iap/purchases` (`verifyStorePurchase`) `{platform, productId,
   purchaseToken (ANDROID) | signedTransaction (IOS, StoreKit 2's JWS), consent, device?}`. A **pending** purchase
   (Google `purchaseState` 2, a slow card / cash) answers 409 `STORE_IAP_PENDING` and nothing is stored; the app shows
   «قيد المعالجة» and retries when the store says it is purchased. On success the app finishes the transaction
   (`completePurchase`); an unfinished one is delivered again by the store and verified the next time the wallet is
   open («استعادة»). Android finishes only what the server credited (an unacknowledged Google purchase is refunded by
   Google after 3 days); iOS also finishes a definitive refusal (else it would come back forever).

**Server verification** (never the client's word):
- **Google:** `purchases.products.get` (Android Publisher v3, the service account's OAuth token, scope
  `androidpublisher`) for `packageName / productId / token`: `purchaseState` 0, the `obfuscatedExternalAccountId` equal to
  the caller's token when present (else 409 `STORE_IAP_PURCHASE_CONFLICT`), `orderId` (test purchases may have none: the
  token's SHA-256 is used). After the credit's commit: `consume` (a consumable: consuming also acknowledges); a failed
  consume is retried by the sweeper (`consumed_at` null) — an unacknowledged purchase is refunded by Google after 3 days.
- **Apple:** the JWS is verified locally — header `alg` ES256, `x5c` leaf → intermediate → a configured root (each
  issued and signed by the next, valid at the transaction's `signedDate`, the leaf carrying OID 1.2.840.113635.100.6.11.1
  and the intermediate 1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.1, the root byte-equal to a configured root), then the signature with the
  leaf key. Then `bundleId`, `type: Consumable`, `productId` equal to the request's, no `revocationDate`, the
  `appAccountToken` equal to the caller's when present, the environment allowed. The transaction id is the key.
- **Idempotency:** one row per `(store, transaction)` — Google `orderId` (or the token hash), Apple `transactionId`;
  the token hash is unique too. A second verification of the same purchase by the **same** account returns the stored
  result (`alreadyProcessed: true`, 200, nothing credited again); by **another** account 409
  `STORE_IAP_PURCHASE_CONFLICT`. The ledger's `(STORE_IAP, purchase id)` key backs it.
- **The credit:** `STORE_IAP` (reference: the purchase), the D187 recharge-badge hook (source `STORE_IAP`) and the D217
  first-recharge hook, in the purchase row's transaction; audited `store_iap.credit` (no token). The purchase keeps the
  device (the session's `device_hash`, else the request's `device.deviceKey` HMAC, D223's key), the consent (version,
  time, locale, `shareConsumptionData`), the environment, Apple's `price` / `currency` when given.
- **Device ban:** a banned device (the session's or the request's) gets 403 `DEVICE_BANNED` before the store is called
  (§10.91.6). A suspended account has no session (401).
- **«شراء واحد لكل حساب وجهاز»** (`iap_settings.once_per_account_device`, default **false**, OWNER, audited
  `store_iap.settings.update` with a reason): while on, an account that already has a credited store purchase, or a
  device that has one (any account), gets `LIMIT_REACHED` in the catalogue; a purchase that still reaches verification
  (a race, an old app) is **not credited on Google** (`REJECTED`, reason `ONCE_LIMIT`; not consumed, so Google refunds
  it within 3 days — such a refund never bans) and **credited on Apple** with `limitExceeded` in the audit (Apple cannot
  refund automatically; the buyer paid). Off: no limit.

#### 10.144.4 A refund «استرداد» — claw-back and ban

Detected by (a) Google's **Voided Purchases API** (`voidedpurchases.list`, `type=0`, a window ≤ 30 days: from the last
poll's end minus 1 hour, first run 30 days, paged; every `STORE_IAP_VOIDED_POLL_HOURS` (24, 0 = off) by the sweeper and
on demand from the panel), (b) **RTDN** (`POST /payments/google/rtdn?token=…`, Pub/Sub push; a `voidedPurchaseNotification`
only *triggers* a poll of the last 3 days — the notification itself is never trusted), (c) Apple's **App Store Server
Notifications v2** `REFUND` (`POST /payments/apple/notifications`, `{signedPayload}`, verified as above; the
notification's and the transaction's bundle id, app id and environment checked). Each notification is applied once
(`iap_notifications`, Apple `notificationUUID` / Pub/Sub `messageId`).

For a **credited** purchase, once (`refunded_at`), in one transaction:
- **claw-back:** the purchase's coins taken back (`STORE_IAP_REVERSAL`, reference: the purchase), **the balance may go
  below 0** (spent coins stay a debt, §10.53's rule: no gift while below 0); host cherries are not taken back
  automatically (the FIFO attribution is kept in `refund_detail` for the team, §10.53);
- **account ban:** an ACTIVE account becomes SUSPENDED (the panel's «حظر», D191: the live ends, seats are freed, every
  session ends; sign-in answers 403 `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`);
- **device ban:** the purchase's device **and every device seen for the account** — its sign-ups (`device_signups`)
  and its sessions' history (`sessions.device_hash`, ended sessions included), newest first, ≤ 100
  (`STORE_REFUND_MAX_DEVICES`), §10.91.6 — are banned **permanently** (`device_bans.iap_purchase_id`), ending every
  session on them (owner, int21: «موافق على الاقتراحات», D345 #5; was the purchase's device only);
- **the reason** (≤ 500, shown in the panel and, on the device, as `DEVICE_BANNED`'s reason): «استرداد عبر Google Play
  بتاريخ YYYY-MM-DD — طلب GPA.…» / «استرداد عبر App Store بتاريخ YYYY-MM-DD — معاملة …» (+ Google's `voidedReason`
  name when given: `remorse`, `chargeback`, `fraud` …);
- `iap_refund_bans` (one per purchase) and audit `store_iap.refund` {purchase, coins, balance, source,
  accountBanned, devicesBanned}.

Not a ban: a Google void whose `voidedSource` is **developer** (the team refunded in Play Console: the coins are taken
back, no ban — as §10.53's team refund), a purchase that was never credited (`REJECTED`), Apple `REFUND_DECLINED`
(recorded) and `REFUND_REVERSED` (recorded; nothing changes automatically — the owner decides, see D345). A refund of a
purchase the server never saw is recorded and ignored.

**«فك الحظر»** (`store_iap.unban` = **OWNER only**; `POST /admin/store-iap/refund-bans/{banId}/unban` `{account,
device, reason, totpCode}` — the authenticator code again): lifts the account (SUSPENDED → ACTIVE) and/or the device
ban; the coins already taken stay taken; audited `store_iap.unban` {account, device, reason, before, after}. The general
«فك الحظر» of a user (`users.ban`) and the device-ban list's «رفع» refuse a store-refund ban (409 `ADMIN_ACTION_REFUSED`,
«حظر استرداد — يُفك من «مشتريات المتجر» بواسطة المالك»), so a MODERATION role cannot lift it.

#### 10.144.5 Answering the store

- **Apple `CONSUMPTION_REQUEST`** → `iap_consumption_requests` (once per notification; deadline = received + 12 h).
  Only when the purchase's consent has `shareConsumptionData: true` (Apple requires `customerConsented: true`; without it
  nothing is sent, `SKIPPED_NO_CONSENT`). The body is Apple's current **`ConsumptionRequest`** for
  `PUT /inApps/v2/transactions/consumption/{transactionId}` (App Store Server API ≥ 1.19; production or sandbox host by
  the transaction's environment, ES256 JWT `iss` issuer, `kid`, `aud: appstoreconnect-v1`, `bid`, ≤ 20 min):
  `{customerConsented: true, consumptionPercentage, deliveryStatus: "DELIVERED", refundPreference: "DECLINE",
  sampleContentProvided: false}` — `consumptionPercentage` in milliunits (0 … 100 000) is the purchase's coins already
  spent, FIFO (§10.53's attribution: the older coins go first); a purchase not credited is `UNDELIVERED_OTHER` with 0 and
  no preference. **Note:** the fields the owner listed (account tenure, play time, lifetime dollars purchased / refunded,
  user status, platform) belong to Apple's older `ConsumptionRequestV1`, which Apple now documents for the Advanced
  Commerce API only; they are computed and stored in the row's `context` (tenure bucket, lifetime purchased / refunded
  buckets from the reference prices, user status) for the team and for a switch back if Apple asks, but not sent.
  A failure is retried by the sweeper until the deadline (`FAILED` after it).
- **Google:** no consumption API. Refunds are decided by Google (and the card networks); the server consumes every
  credited purchase (the coins were delivered), polls voided purchases and claws back. Documented for the owner.

#### 10.144.6 The panel «مشتريات المتجر»

Capabilities: `store_iap.view` (OWNER, MODERATION, SUPPORT, FINANCE) — the overview, the purchases and the refund bans;
`store_iap.manage` (OWNER) — products, the switch, «مزامنة الاستردادات الآن»; `store_iap.unban` (OWNER). Routes under
`/admin/store-iap`: `GET overview` (each store: configured, sandbox accepted, RTDN on, the Apple notification and RTDN
paths; the switch; the last voided poll), `PATCH settings`, `GET|POST products`, `PATCH products/{id}`, `GET purchases`
(table: `q` user / order, `platform`, `status`, `environment`), `GET refund-bans` (table: `status` ACTIVE / LIFTED; the
reason, the user, the order, coins, whether the account and the device are still banned), `POST
refund-bans/{id}/unban`, `POST google/voided-sync`. The device is never shown (only that one was banned).

#### 10.144.7 Data and privacy

`iap_purchases` keeps the store token (needed to consume and to match voids) and its SHA-256, the order /
transaction ids, the device HMAC, the consent and the price; it is financial and anti-fraud data kept with the ledger
(7 years, §10.56); the account's purge keeps the rows (the user id stays a tombstone). The data export gains the section `store_purchases`
(store, product, coins, the store's transaction id, environment, status, dates, the consent; no token, no device). The privacy policy names the
store-purchase data and the sharing of consumption data with Apple on a refund request (with consent).

#### 10.144.8 Migrations

`20270417090000_store_iap_enums` (`wallet_ledger_reason` `STORE_IAP`, `STORE_IAP_REVERSAL`) and
`20270417090100_store_iap` (the enums `iap_platform`, `iap_environment`, `iap_purchase_status`,
`iap_consumption_status`; `iap_products`, `iap_purchases`, `iap_notifications`, `iap_consumption_requests`,
`iap_refund_bans`, `iap_settings` (one row); `device_bans.iap_purchase_id`; the ledger's sign rule).

### 10.145 The streamer's screen capture: the service, the order, the failures and the problem report *(app + `kabso_streamer`, D346)*

Owner (2026-11-09, device test of the staging APK `809063b`): «في بث ستريمر لا يمكن مشاركة الشاشة». No API change.
§10.145 follows the numbers reserved by in-flight work (§10.132–§10.144). Extends §10.86 (D213) and D262 / D262b.

- **The live's foreground service survives leaving Kabso.** flutter_foreground_task 11.0.3's `stopWithTask: true` installs
  `TrackVisibilityUtils`, which stops the service on the first `onActivityPaused` with no resumed Activity — as soon as
  the host goes to the game. Android 10+ (targetSdk ≥ 29) ends a MediaProjection whose app has no running service of
  type `mediaProjection`, so the screen stopped the moment it was meant to be seen (and Android 14 cut the background
  microphone of every live, D123). The app passes `stopWithTask: false`; the manifest's `android:stopWithTask="true"`
  still stops the service when the task is swiped away. Never turn the option back on.
- **Order (Android 10–15), one consent per capture session, one projection:** consent (`kabso_streamer`
  `requestCapture`, handed to this engine's flutter_webrtc) → the service started again with
  `microphone|mediaPlayback|mediaProjection|camera` — its failure stops the start (`LiveBackgroundKeeper.lastStartFailure`;
  `LiveBackgroundStartException`) → room, token, camera / microphone → **`captureCheck`** → `getDisplayMedia` (the one
  `getMediaProjection`) → publish → `attach` (the game sound's `AudioPlaybackCapture` on that same projection — never a
  second one). «شارك الشاشة من جديد» asks a new consent and passes the same check.
- **`captureCheck`** (native, right before the capture): `unsupported_os` (< Android 5), `no_consent` (our consent never
  reached flutter_webrtc — it would ask with its own dialog), `consent_used` (that consent already started a capture —
  Android 14 throws on reuse), `no_service` (Android 10+: the live's service is not in the foreground). A capture that
  would fail is never started; when it may, the consent is marked used.
- **Each failure its own message** (`StreamerProblem` → `streamerFailureMessage`, ar + en): `refused`, `consentFailed`
  (D262's code), `serviceDenied`, `security` (a SecurityException), `stoppedBySystem` (the projection ended while the
  service was not in the foreground — `projectionStopped {serviceForeground: false}`; a stop with the service still
  in front is the host's own, from the status-bar chip, and only offers «شارك الشاشة من جديد»), `unsupportedOs`,
  `captureFailed` / `publishFailed` (with the exception's short code). A failure of the usual go-live steps (`other`)
  keeps the usual message. Never a generic «try again».
- **«نسخ تقرير المشكلة»** (`StreamerProblemCard`, in the setup panel and on the host's stage under «شارك الشاشة من
  جديد»): copies a short English report — app version, Android release / SDK, maker and model, the step, the problem,
  the exception class and a scrubbed message (no URLs, e-mails, paths, tokens or long numbers; one line ≤ 160), the
  service's state and types, the consent's state, the steps so far, a UTC time. No account, no user, no room, no title.
  `kabso_streamer` `diagnostics` gives the device facts; the steps are logged (`AppLogger`, debug builds) and natively
  in logcat (`KabsoStreamer`: `consent: …`, `capture check: …`, `projection stopped (service …)`).
- **R8:** the plugin reads flutter_webrtc members by name; its own `consumer-rules.pro` keeps exactly those (flutter_webrtc's
  rules keep its whole package today). The staging APK is a `--profile` build (Flutter: `initWith(debug)`, no R8).
- **PK is a SOLO live's only** (owner: «بث الستريمر لا يحتاج زر pk»): `KHostBar.showPk` is false on a streamer live (no
  button, not even «قريباً»); an incoming invitation is shown over a SOLO room only; viewers of a streamer have no PK
  entry. The server's SOLO-only rule stands.

### 10.146 The global lucky banner «شريط المردود في كل اللايفات» *(v1.111-live, DRAFT — D347)*

Owner (2026-11-09, approved design): «شريط المردود يظهر في كل لايفات للشريط x250 / x500 / x1000». §10.146 follows the
numbers reserved by in-flight work (§10.132–§10.145).

- **Which wins** *(owner)*: a lucky send (§10.27) whose best paid multiplier (`luckyResult.topMultiplier`, after the daily
  protection) is **one of** `LUCKY_GLOBAL_BANNER_MULTIPLIERS` (API env, default `250,500,1000`; each must be one of
  `LUCKY_GIFT_MULTIPLIERS`, distinct, else the server refuses to start). It is a set, not a threshold: a new ×2000 tier
  is global only when listed. Smaller wins keep today's behaviour — the `lucky-win` banner in their own room only.
  `LUCKY_GIFT_BIG_WIN_MULTIPLIER` no longer decides it (it stays the odds' `bigWinMultiplier`).
- **Where:** every **other** room whose status is `LIVE` — every mode: SOLO / PK (video), MULTI, AUDIO, PODCAST,
  STREAMER — newest first, at most 5 000 rooms. The room the win happened in is excluded by the server and, again, by
  the app (it shows its own `lucky-win` banner; never the global copy twice).
- **Delivery** *(CTO, D347)*: server-side fan-out, the existing pattern of every global strip (D148, D178, D254, D305):
  one reliable LiveKit data message per room through the server SDK (`SendData`, the media provider's
  `broadcastData`, with §10.123's retry of a briefly missing room), 8 rooms at a time. At ~500 live rooms that is
  ~500 small calls per banner and, with the gap, at most ~50 calls a second for the whole service — no client
  polling, no new connection, no database write. LiveKit has no multi-room send; a poll by every viewer would cost
  far more at the same latency.
- **Rate limit and queue** *(owner: at most one per room every 10 s)*: at most **one global banner per
  `LUCKY_GLOBAL_BANNER_GAP_SECONDS`** (API env, default 10, 1–600) for the whole service (Redis gate
  `lucky:ticker:gate`, shared by all API instances) — every live room gets each banner, so this is also one per room.
  A win offered inside the gap waits in **one** slot (`lucky:ticker:pending`, at most 30 s): a bigger win (multiplier,
  then coins) replaces the waiting one, a smaller or equal one is dropped; when the gap ends the waiting win goes out.
  A waiting win whose live is **no longer LIVE** when its turn comes is dropped (its tap would lead nowhere). The app
  keeps its own small line too: one banner at a time (the room banner's 3.5 s and a breath), at most 3 waiting, the
  biggest first (the smallest dropped when full), none older than 30 s, a send seen before never again.
- **The message** (`lucky-ticker`, topic `lucky`; additive fields):
  `{"type":"lucky-ticker","win":{giftId, roomId, giftCode, sender: UserSummary, multiplier, coinsWon, createdAt},
  "gift":{"code","assetKey","imageUrl"},"room":{"id","title","mode","host":UserSummary}}` — `gift` is the gift's art
  as the send's `LiveGift` carries it (the app names it from its catalogue, else «هدية»; the art lets a viewer whose
  catalogue has no lucky gifts still see it), `room.mode` the live's `LiveRoomMode`. An older app ignores both.
- **The app** *(owner: reuse «شريط المردود»)*: the banner is the room's own win banner (D159's tier frames, timeline,
  ×N, «فلان أرسل …» / «ربح ×N وحصل على …») with a tag under it: the winner's avatar, «في {room title}» (ellipsis), the
  gift's picture and, when it opens the live, a chevron toward the reading end. It sits under the header with the
  global strips (it steps aside while this live's own win banner shows). Reduced motion: still.
- **Tap** *(owner)*: a viewer's tap opens that live — the app first reads it (`getLiveRoom`): ended or gone → the
  toast «انتهى هذا البث.» and nothing moves; a **seated guest** (on a mic) is asked first («ستترك مقعدك وتنتقل إلى
  …»); then the live opens through the normal join (its own rules: guests, bans, kicks). The same check now applies to
  the other global strips' taps. A **host on air** (the go-live screen) sees the banner but it is **not a button**
  (never pulled out of their own live).
- **Privacy:** Kabso has no «mystery» / invisible / hidden-identity mode today (checked: no such setting in the schema
  or the contract), so the winner's public `UserSummary` (as in the room's own banner) is shown. Blocks apply as for
  every strip (a viewer never sees a banner about someone they blocked, or in a live of someone they blocked). When a
  hidden-identity mode is added, the server must mask `win.sender` here (and in `lucky-win`).
- **Best effort:** Redis or the media server down → no banner, never a failed send.

#### 10.146.1 Follow-up: the panel setting and «إخفاء أشرطة الفوز» *(v1.111-live, DRAFT — D347; owner «نعم موافق», 2026-11-09)*

The owner approved the five D347 decisions (×100 stays in its room; the defaults ×250 / ×500 / ×1000 and 10 s; the
placement) and asked for the two follow-ups below.

- **Panel setting** (the D305 / D318 pattern): the set and the gap are part of the `site_settings` row `globalStrips`
  (`luckyGlobalMultipliers`, `luckyGlobalGapSeconds`), edited in «إعدادات الموقع» → «شريطا الهدايا والألعاب»
  (`GET|PUT /admin/global-strips`, capability `site.settings` — the OWNER, as for D305 / D318; CSRF; audited
  `site.settings.update` with before / after and the optional reason in the same transaction). Both fields are
  optional in the PUT (absent: unchanged — an older panel keeps them) and validated like the env: the set is 1–32
  distinct whole numbers, each one of `LUCKY_GIFT_MULTIPLIERS` (else 400 `luckyGlobalMultipliers` / `invalid_value`;
  stored ascending), the gap a whole number 1–600 s (else 400). A stored value that is no longer valid reads as the
  configuration's. `LUCKY_GLOBAL_BANNER_MULTIPLIERS` / `LUCKY_GLOBAL_BANNER_GAP_SECONDS` stay the defaults. The ticker
  service reads the values per win through a 30 s cache (also the flush of a waiting win), so a change applies within
  30 s on every instance, no restart. Every lucky win is now offered to the ticker service, which decides.
- **«إخفاء أشرطة الفوز» / "Hide win banners"**: a per-account switch `NotificationSettings.luckyStrip` (default true =
  shown; `PATCH /me/notification-settings` `{luckyStrip: false}` hides), stored with D305's `giftStrip` / `gameStrip`
  so it follows the account to every phone (migration `20270418090000_lucky_strip_setting`, `notification_settings.
  lucky_strip`). It is in every live's settings sheet — the viewer's «إعدادات المشاهدة» and the host's — under the
  strip switches, worded as the owner said (on = hidden). Off for a guest (no account) and with an older server. When
  hidden, the app drops the global lucky banner (the one on screen goes, new ones are not queued); the server still
  sends it (one message per room, not per person). **Included:** only the global lucky banner (`lucky-ticker`). **Not
  included, on purpose:** the gifts and games strips (`gift-ticker`, `game-win-ticker`) — they already have their own
  switches «إظهار شريط الهدايا» / «إظهار شريط الألعاب» on the same path, and folding them in would make one switch
  silently override two others; the level banner (`level-ticker`, D254) is not a win; the live's own win banner
  (`lucky-win`) always shows. D151's hide flag (`luckyTickerHiddenProvider`) is now this switch.


### 10.151 «واتساب» — the official Kabso WhatsApp number answered by the staff *(v1.116-social, DRAFT — D355)*

Owner (2026-11-10): «ربط رقم واتساب رسمي واحد لكابسو، يفتح كل مشرف وموظف دعم زر «واتساب» في التطبيق وفي لوحة الإدارة،
مع عداد غير مقروء وإشعار عند وصول رسالة، ويرد على العميل». The owner has no Meta Business account yet: everything is
behind configuration and **off** until the credentials are on the server (§10.151.1). Module `whatsapp` (owns `wa_*`).

**Assumptions (D355).** developers.facebook.com was not reachable from the build machine; the design follows the
documented WhatsApp Business Platform **Cloud API** (Graph API v2x) shapes, cross-checked with Meta's own sample
repository (`fbsamples/whatsapp-api-examples`) and a typed schema of the webhook. Marked conservative: the webhook
parser ignores what it does not know (an unknown message type is stored as UNSUPPORTED, unknown fields are dropped),
`WHATSAPP_GRAPH_API_VERSION` (default `v23.0`) is a setting the owner keeps current (Meta retires versions about two
years after release), and the read-receipt / media / template calls are the documented ones listed in
`graph-client.ts`. Nothing was tested against Meta; PP-87 is the first real run.

#### 10.151.1 Configuration (off until set)

Five settings, **all or none** (a partial set refuses to boot): `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`,
`WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID` (numeric ids, not secrets) and three **file paths** read once at boot —
`WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE` (the System User's permanent token with `whatsapp_business_messaging` and
`whatsapp_business_management`), `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET_FILE` (the Meta app secret: the webhook signature) and
`WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN_FILE` (a random string the owner also types in Meta). A missing, unreadable or empty file (< 8
characters, or with spaces) refuses to boot. No secret is ever in the environment, git, a log, an API answer or the
panel. Optional: `WHATSAPP_GRAPH_API_VERSION` (`v23.0`), `WHATSAPP_GRAPH_BASE_URL` (tests only), `WHATSAPP_DISPLAY_NAME`,
`WHATSAPP_RETENTION_DAYS` (180, 7–3650), `WHATSAPP_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES` (16 MiB), `WHATSAPP_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (3600),
`WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_CACHE_SECONDS` (600), `WHATSAPP_PUSH_GAP_SECONDS` (30). Off: every inbox route and the webhook answer
503 `WHATSAPP_UNAVAILABLE`; `GET …/summary` answers `{enabled: false}` (the app and the panel hide «واتساب»).

#### 10.151.2 Permissions

Two panel capabilities (§10.54.1), checked on **every request** against the roles held now, from the panel (cookie,
`/api/v1/admin/whatsapp/*`) and from the staff's app account (bearer + StaffAppGuard, `/api/v1/staff/whatsapp/*`;
staff work switches the shift on, §10.96.14, except the summary and «me/settings»):

| Capability | OWNER | MODERATION «مشرف» | SUPPORT «دعم» | FINANCE | BD |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| `support.whatsapp` — the inbox, replies, claim / release / transfer / close / reopen, notes, the account link, templates, the agents, my push mute, reading the quick replies | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | |
| `support.whatsapp.manage` — quick replies (create / edit / delete), the settings page and «اختبار الاتصال», and acting on a conversation assigned to someone else (transfer, release, close) | ✓ | ✓ | | | |

The OWNER grants them by granting the role («الموظفون والصلاحيات», §10.96.5) — no new role. Both are in
`StaffStatus.capabilities` (the app shows «واتساب» only with `support.whatsapp`).

#### 10.151.3 The webhook (public)

`GET /api/v1/webhooks/whatsapp?hub.mode=subscribe&hub.verify_token=…&hub.challenge=…` → 200 the challenge as
`text/plain` when the mode is `subscribe` and the token equals the file's (constant-time); else 403 `AUTH_FORBIDDEN`.
`POST /api/v1/webhooks/whatsapp` — no session, no rate limit, the body kept raw (≤ 3 MB): `X-Hub-Signature-256:
sha256=<hex>` must be the HMAC-SHA256 of the exact bytes with the app secret (constant-time), else 403 (audited
`whatsapp.webhook.refused`, nothing stored). Then each `entry[].changes[]` with `field: messages`:
- **messages** (`text`, `image`, `audio` incl. `voice`, `video`, `document`, `sticker`, `location`, `reaction`,
  `contacts`, `interactive` / `button` replies; anything else UNSUPPORTED) from a valid `wa_id` (E.164) — one
  conversation per phone (created on the first message, the profile name kept fresh); the message is stored **once**
  (`wa_messages.wa_message_id` unique and a per-phone advisory lock: Meta's retries and duplicates change nothing); the
  conversation's unread count +1, `last_inbound_at` (the window) and the preview move, a CLOSED conversation reopens
  (assignee kept, history REOPEN with no actor); a **reaction** sets the emoji on the message it reacts to and is not an
  unread message;
- **statuses** (`sent`, `delivered`, `read`, `failed` with Meta's first error code and title) of our outbound messages,
  forward only (a late `delivered` never replaces `read`; `failed` is final);
- events for another `phone_number_id` are ignored. The answer is 200 `{received: true, events}` even when one event
  failed to store (logged): Meta would otherwise retry the whole batch.

**Media in:** after the answer, `GET /{media-id}` then the URL with the same bearer token (only Meta's hosts —
`*.fbsbx.com`, `*.facebook.com`, `*.whatsapp.net`, `*.fbcdn.net` — are fetched; no redirects), the type checked
against the allowlist (JPEG, PNG, WebP stickers, AAC / MP4 / MPEG / AMR / OGG audio, MP4 / 3GPP video, PDF, plain text,
Word / Excel / PowerPoint) and the size against `WHATSAPP_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES` while streaming; stored in the **private**
bucket at `private/whatsapp/<conversation>/<message>.<ext>` (`private, no-store`). `media.state`: STORED, TOO_LARGE,
TYPE_REFUSED or FAILED (the message text says so; nothing else is kept). Read with `GET …/messages/{id}/media`
(always `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `nosniff`).

#### 10.151.4 Replies and the 24-hour window

`POST …/conversations/{id}/messages` `{type: TEXT, text}` or `{type: TEMPLATE, template: {name, language,
parameters[]}}`; `POST …/conversations/{id}/media?mime=&filename=&caption=` with the raw bytes
(`application/octet-stream`; outbound images JPEG / PNG only). Rules, in order: the conversation is OPEN (else 409
`WHATSAPP_CONVERSATION_CLOSED`); it is the caller's or unassigned — an unassigned one becomes the caller's (CLAIM in
the history) — else 409 `WHATSAPP_CONVERSATION_ASSIGNED`; **text and media only within 24 hours of the customer's last
message** (Meta's customer-service window; else 409 `WHATSAPP_WINDOW_CLOSED` — the app switches the composer to
«إرسال قالب»); a **template** any time, only an **APPROVED** one from Meta's list (`GET …/templates`, cached
`WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_CACHE_SECONDS`; `?refresh=true` reads now) with exactly its number of `{{n}}` body parameters (400
`template` `not_approved` / `parameters` `count_mismatch`); the stored text is the template's body filled in. Meta's
answer: accepted → stored SENT (then the statuses move it); refused → **nothing stored**, 502 `WHATSAPP_SEND_FAILED`
with `meta_<code>`; Meta's 131047 (re-engagement) → 409 `WHATSAPP_WINDOW_CLOSED`; Meta's throughput limits (130429,
131056 pair rate limit, 80007, 4) → 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After: 60`. Every send is audited
`whatsapp.message.send` {messageId, type, claimed, via}. **Not idempotent towards Meta:** a send cannot be undone, so
the clients disable «إرسال» while a send is in flight; a client retry after a timeout may send twice (documented, as
Meta's API has no idempotency key).

`POST …/read` sets the unread count to 0 and sends Meta the read receipt of the last inbound message (best effort).

#### 10.151.5 Assignment, notes, account link, pushes

- `claim` (unassigned only), `release` (the assignee or `manage`), `transfer {toUserId}` (to an agent holding
  `support.whatsapp` now; by the assignee, on an unassigned one, or `manage`), `close` (the assignee, an unassigned one
  or `manage`; unread → 0), `reopen`. Each under a row lock, in `wa_assignments` {action, from, to, actor} and audited
  `whatsapp.conversation.assign`. `GET …/assignments` (newest first, ≤ 100), `GET …/agents` (with their shift).
- **Notes** `wa_notes` — internal, never sent to the customer, never in the data export; audited
  `whatsapp.note.create`.
- **Account link** (§10.151.7): `POST …/link {username}` / `DELETE …/link`, audited; the card (`WaAccountCard`)
  shows only what `users.view` shows: username, display name, avatar, status, country, joined — never an email, a
  balance or a phone.
- **Pushes** (staff channel `kabso_staff`, data `{kind: whatsapp, conversationId}`, tag `wa:<conversation>`): a new
  customer message → the **assigned agent** (if still an agent); unassigned → the agents **on shift**; nobody on shift
  → every agent. A muted agent («كتم إشعارات واتساب», `PUT …/me/settings {pushMuted}`) never; at most one push per
  agent and conversation every `WHATSAPP_PUSH_GAP_SECONDS`. The text never has the message: «رسالة واتساب جديدة من
  {name}» / the masked number (`+9665••••5678`). The badge is `GET …/summary` — `mine` + `unassigned` open
  conversations with unread messages; the clients poll it (60 s, and on a `whatsapp` push), like «بلاغات» (§10.101).

#### 10.151.6 Quick replies

`wa_quick_replies` {title (unique, ≤ 60), body (≤ 1024)} — every agent reads them (`GET …/quick-replies`), OWNER and
MODERATION create / edit / delete (audited `whatsapp.quick_reply.change`). Inserting one fills the composer; it is sent
like any text (window rules apply).

#### 10.151.7 Matching a phone to a Kabso account

Kabso keeps **no verified phone number** on accounts (sign-up is by e-mail, §6; the recharge-agent application's phone is
private KYC, not verified, and never used here). A phone match would therefore prove nothing and could show a stranger's
account to the staff, so **there is no automatic match**: the staff member asks the customer for their username (or the
customer writes it) and links it; the link is audited and can be removed. If the owner later adds verified phones
(e.g. an SMS check), the match can be offered as a suggestion behind the same card (a contract change).

#### 10.151.8 Privacy and retention

The customer's phone (E.164), profile name, messages and media are personal data. **Retention:** a conversation with
no message for `WHATSAPP_RETENTION_DAYS` (180) is deleted with its messages, notes, history and media files by the
WhatsApp sweeper (audited `whatsapp.retention.purge` with counts only). **Account deletion:** the purge (§10.56) marks
every conversation linked to the account (`purge_after`); it disappears from the inbox at once and the sweeper deletes it
and its files; a later message from that phone starts a new conversation. **Data export:** section `whatsapp` — the
linked conversations' messages (who wrote, type, text, file name, status, time), never the notes or which staff member
answered. Meta keeps its own copy under Meta's terms (the privacy policy must say so — PP-87).

#### 10.151.9 Data model (migration `20270421090000_whatsapp_inbox`)

`wa_conversations` (phone unique, wa_id, profile_name, status OPEN / CLOSED, assigned_to_id / assigned_at, unread_count,
last_inbound_at, last_message_at, last_preview, last_direction, linked_user_id / linked_by_id / linked_at, closed_*,
purge_after), `wa_messages` (direction, type, body ≤ 4096, media key / state / mime / size / filename / voice,
location, reaction, template name / language, status, error code / title, sent_by_id, wa_timestamp, status_at;
`wa_message_id` unique), `wa_notes`, `wa_assignments`, `wa_quick_replies`, `wa_agent_settings` (push mute). Staff ids
carry no foreign key (accounts are tombstoned, never deleted).

#### 10.151.10 Costs

Meta charges per message / conversation category and changes its pricing (the move to per-message pricing in 2025 is
one example); service replies inside the 24-hour window and templates are priced differently by country. No number is
written here on purpose — the owner reads the current prices at
https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing before sending templates at scale.
